Kinetic isotope experiments (H2O vs. D2O) show that deuteration suppresses the 2CPET channel, shifting the population toward the two‑electron transfer pathway, further confirming the competitive branching between the two channels. pH-dependent measurements show that the 2CPET channel is progressively suppressed as the intermolecular hydrogen bonds are disrupted. DFT calculations provide a molecular-level explanation for this observation, revealing pre‑organized intermolecular hydrogen bonds in ground state with a short donor-acceptor distance (~2.0 Å) that serve as the structural basis for the ultrafast 2CPET. Our findings establish a direct spectroscopic view of 2CPET and identify hydrogen-bond preorganization as a key molecular prerequisite for efficient multi-equivalent proton-electron transfer, with H2O2 as the oxidation product, offering potential implications for photoelectrochemical energy storage.
papers.title: Intermolecular Hydrogen-Bond Preorganization Enables Concerted 2e−/2H+ Transfer in the Franck–Condon Region

papers.abstract: Cryptic pockets, drug-binding sites absent from a protein’s static structure but exposed through conformational change, expand the scope of druggable targets, yet remain difficult to identify computationally. PocketMiner, a structure-based graph neural network trained on molecular dynamics simulation data, predicts cryptic pocket formation from a single static structure (ROC-AUC 0.87). Recent protein language model (PLM)-based approaches report further improvements over this structure-only baseline (up to 0.93), but do so by simultaneously replacing the structural architecture with a sequence-only model and switching to substantially larger, differently-sourced training data–leaving it unclear whether these gains stem from the languagemodel signal itself or from increased training data scale. We isolate this variable directly: holding architecture family and PocketMiner’s original, small molecular-dynamics-derived training set fixed, we compare three matched variants–geometry-only (baseline), ESM2 embeddings only, and both combined (fused)–under identical training conditions. The geometry-only baseline achieves chance-level test performance (ROC-AUC 0.498), while both the ESM2-only (0.817) and fused (0.835) variants perform far above it, with statistically indistinguishable confidence intervals between the two, indicating that language-model signal alone accounts for nearly all of the achievable performance, and that structural information contributes marginally under these conditions. This result is confirmed on CryptoBench, an independent, larger benchmark (baseline 0.494 vs. fused 0.716, non-overlapping confidence intervals), and holds consistently across every pocket-formation mechanism examined in a stratified analysis. These findings suggest that a substantial share of the improvement reported by prior sequence-based methods is attributable to language-model signal itself rather than training data scale, with implications for data-efficient strategies in structure-based pocket prediction more broadly.
papers.title: The Limited Contribution of Structural Information Relative to Language-Model Signal in Data-Limited Cryptic Pocket Prediction

papers.abstract: Machine-learning models that estimate the state of health (SOH) of lithium-ion cells from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) are rarely compared with models using only data a battery management system (BMS) records. Of 30 audited studies using three public datasets, one reported such a baseline. With whole cells held out, impedance brought no detectable gain over the strongest baseline on two exploratory datasets. A test on 88 independent coin cells, registered before the data were downloaded, was inconclusive (19 cells; +0.79 SOH points with impedance, 95% CI −0.07 to +1.66; smallest effect of interest 1.32). The capacity label varied strongly with cycling currents. Post hoc, with the label corrected for these currents without the test cell, impedance changed the full-life error of all 88 cells by −1.95 points (−2.86 to −1.03). With features of the previous discharge curve in the baseline, the change was −0.39 (−1.10 to +0.33). The comparison of impedance with these features, repeated as originally published, lost most of its gain within sets once the baseline received the previous discharge current, but not when models trained at 23 °C were tested at 35 °C. Impedance-based SOH studies should compare impedance with the strongest baseline a BMS can build.
papers.title: Critical Evaluation of Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy for State-of-Health Estimation of Lithium-Ion Cells Against Battery Management System Baselines

papers.abstract: One-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (1D COFs) featuring double-chain architectures offer abundant exposed active sites for photocatalysis. However, topological constraints and entropy-driven stacking disorder severely impede their controllable synthesis, obscuring definitive structure–activity relationships. Herein, we report a series of sp2-carbon-bridged 1D COFs with atomically tailored chain-edge microenvironments (C=R-COFs, R = C, O, S) for efficient photocatalytic H2O2 production. In a water/benzyl alcohol (9:1, v/v) system under an O2 atmosphere, C=S-COF exhibited the highest H2O2 production rate of 3750.7 μmol g-1 h-1, corresponding to 1.8- and 20.0-fold enhancements over C=O-COF and C=C-COF, respectively, ranking among the best reported 1D COFs. Combined experimental and theoretical calculations reveal that the superior activity of C=S-COF stems not only from its red-shifted light harvesting (up to 810 nm), prolonged exciton lifetime, and supplementary 1O2-mediated pathway, but more critically, from an interfacial "moderate balance" effect. Specifically, endowing the chain-edge active sites with intermediate local charge density and moderate hydrophilicity reconciles competing elementary steps—simultaneously optimizing interfacial wetting, reactant (O2/H2O) activation, and H2O2 desorption, rather than maximizing a single descriptor. The “moderate balance” effect offers a new design paradigm for the development of advanced COF photocatalysts.
papers.title: Tailoring Chain-Edge C=R (R = C, O, S) Microenvironments in sp2-Carbon-Bridged 1D COFs Unlocks a ‘Moderate Balance’ Effect for Photocatalytic H2O2 Production

papers.abstract: In this work, we identify and characterize a cooperative interaction between adsorbates in which hydrogen bonding and surface-mediated bond redistribution reinforce one another across a solid interface. We show that this phenomenon, which we term adsorbate resonance-assisted hydrogen bonding (ARAHB), arises from the transfer of covalent bond character along a hydrogen-bond coordinate, coupled to bond redistribution throughout the adsorbate-surface complex. We develop a computational workflow to test and identify ARAHB among coadsorbates. Although first identified computationally, we connect ARAHB to previous experimental observations of symmetric hydrogen-bonded water/hydroxyl surface structures. Through computational screening of homo-and heteronuclear adsorbate dimers, we identify ARAHB across a range of X − H · · · Y motifs (X, Y = N, O, F). These interactions are characterized by strong adsorbate-adsorbate stabilization, substantial redistribution of surface bonding, and pronounced X − H bond elongation, demonstrating the generality of the phenomenon. We find a strong correlation between interaction energetics and geometry, culminating in nearly equalized X − H · · · Y configurations that exhibit the strongest stabilization. We find that the donor species principally determines the interaction geometry, whereas the acceptor largely governs the extent of bond redistribution. The overall stabilization reflects contributions from both species as well as the local adsorption environment. These findings establish ARAHB as a general interaction mechanism at solid interfaces and provide a framework for understanding cooperative adsorbate interactions that cannot be inferred by isolated adsorbate behavior.
papers.title: Adsorbate Resonance-Assisted Hydrogen Bonding across Solid Interfaces

papers.abstract: Support architectures critically govern the molecular organization and excited-state pathways of organic chromophores. Chitosan, one of the most widely studied sustainable, biomass-derived polysaccharides, has typically served as a low-loading, aggregation-suppressing host for photofunctional chromophores such as porphyrins. By contrast, high chromophore loading remains largely unexplored because it is generally assumed to cause detrimental aggregation-induced quenching. Here, this sustainable biopolymer is redefined as an active, high-density scaffold for controlling the excited-state branching of covalently attached platinum(II) meso-tetrakis(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin (PtTCPP). PtTCPP was grafted onto partially acetylated chitosan over a broad loading range of 0.050–1.00 equivalents per glucosamine unit. At low loading (<0.25 eq), the chitosan scaffold preserved predominantly monomer-like PtTCPP photophysics and promoted Type II energy transfer to oxygen. Increasing the loading (≥0.25 eq) promoted J-type PtTCPP assembly, suppressed singlet-oxygen generation, and stabilized a long-lived, oxygen-sensitive triplet component associated with electron-transfer-dominant photochemistry. Cocatalyst-free photocatalytic hydrogen evolution served as a functional readout of this loading-induced pathway switching, reaching 74.1 mmol g -1 h -1 at 0.50 eq, with an apparent quantum yield of 0.4% at 405 nm. These findings establish chromophore loading density on chitosan as a practical design lever for directing excited-state branching between energy-transfer and electron-transfer pathways, repositioning a widely used sustainable biopolymer from a passive dispersion matrix to an active scaffold for aggregation-enabled photochemistry and solar-driven hydrogen production.
papers.title: Chitosan as a Sustainable Loading-Density-Tunable Scaffold for Switching Energy- and Electron-Transfer Pathways in Porphyrin Photocatalysis

papers.abstract: Automated reaction exploration can generate more candidate elementary steps than can be practically characterized with transition-state searches. Thermodynamic screening provides an inexpensive first filter, but endpoint energies contain no information about the path connecting reactants and products. Here, we introduce SPARTA (Steric Path Alignment for Reactive Transformation Assessment), a geometric kinetic proxy that generates reaction-biased endpoint conformers, refines them through iterative image-dependent pair potential path optimization, and evaluates electronic single-point energies along the resulting path. Across two large reaction-barrier datasets, the SPARTA barrier discriminates highand low-barrier reactions better than reaction energy. Across curated reaction classes, SPARTA reproduces experimentally established steric trends when kinetic differences are governed by accessibility to the reactive configuration, while identifying clear limitations for stereoelectronically or orbital-symmetrycontrolled transformations. Applied to glucose pyrolysis and formose reaction networks, a single SPARTA threshold retains more than 98% of reactions with reference barriers below 50 kcal mol−1. In the glucose network, adding SPARTA after thermodynamic screening reduces the number of candidate transitionstate searches from 13,436 to 4,760 while retaining all 241 reactions below 20 kcal mol−1. These results establish the geometric accessibility of the reaction path as a useful complement to thermodynamic screening for reducing the cost of automated reaction-network exploration.
papers.title: Geometric Reaction Path Alignment for Kinetic Feasibility Assessment

papers.abstract: Macrocyclic peptides represent a promising modality for modulating intracellular protein–protein interactions; however, macrocyclic peptide datasets with reliable experimental activity measurements that can inform rational design remain limited. Here, we developed DEL-Flow, a pocket-conditioned generative framework for the design of MDM2-p53 inhibitors. Using an iterative DEL-selection strategy, a first-generation symmetric dimeric macrocyclic peptide DEL identified a half-scaffold associated with highly enriched library members, which was retained to construct a second-generation asymmetric focused DEL. Experimentally derived selection signals from this focused DEL were combined with computationally generated conformations and macrocyclic topologies for model training. DEL-Flow integrates these priors with MDM2 pocket and PackDock-derived pose information to generate side-chain variants while retaining the macrocyclic core. An SE(3)-equivariant flow-matching model generates all-atom coordinates, and a MASK denoising module predicts editable-region atom types, chirality, and bond connectivity. Starting from templates 126 and 319, DEL-Flow generated 20 candidates from each template, yielding 40 candidates in total. Following prioritization, 126-18 and 319-18 were synthesized off DNA and inhibited the MDM2-p53 interaction in fluorescence-polarization assays, with IC50 values of 1.95 and 6.50 μM and Ki values of 163 and 548 nM, respectively. These results support the use of DEL selection signals and pocket geometry to guide the generation of macrocyclic peptides absent from the original library that inhibit the MDM2–p53 interaction.
papers.title: DEL-Flow: AI-Driven Structural Generation and Activity Validation of MDM2-Targeting Macrocyclic Peptides

papers.abstract: Graphene oxide (GO) is an emerging product experiencing exponential growth in popularity and demand. This comprehensive research evaluates the technical and economic feasibility of implementing a large-scale GO production plant in Malaysia, based on existing pilot-scale data from the industry. The major aspect of the GO production process is the GO synthesis reaction, carried out in a jacketed, stirred tank batch reactor of approximately 500 L capacity. Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) software COMSOL Multiphysics is used to simulate the dynamic behaviour of reactants within the reactor to obtain the best possible configurations and dimensions of the reactor. The results indicated that the reactor should have a height-to-diameter (H/D) ratio of 1.75, with an inner diameter of 0.71 m and a total height of 1.63 m. The entire proposed production process is simulated using SuperPro Designer software, and the results obtained are used to aid in the plant's equipment sizing calculations and economic analysis. A comprehensive economic analysis has assessed its profitability and economic viability. All calculations indicate that the plant would be a potentially profitable venture with a high return on investment (ROI) of 126.9% and a short payback period of 0.83 years.
authors: Abu Danish Aiman Bin Abu Sofian
papers.title: Scaled-Up Production of Graphene Oxide: Design, Simulation, and Analysis of a Stirred Tank Batch Reactor

papers.abstract: Propellanes are molecules with unique three-dimensional (3D) structures and chemical properties. Owing to their strained and rigid molecular frameworks, propellanes have attracted considerable attention in various fields. Heteroacenes, such as benzothieno[3,2-b]benzothiophene (BTBT), are widely used in materials science. However, there are few reports on the synthesis of heteroacene-derived propellanes. Therefore, the development of general synthetic strategies for constructing heteroacene-derived propellanes and the elucidation of the physical properties of these derivatives are of significant interest. Meanwhile, photocycloaddition via triplet energy transfer (EnT) process with photosensitizers has received considerable attention for the synthesis of 3D molecules from planar substrates. Herein, we report the photochemical synthesis of BTBT propellanes via triplet-sensitized [2 + 2] photocycloadditions. Photochemical reactions of benzothieno[3,2-b]benzothiophene S,S-dioxide (BTBT-DO) with alkenes were performed in the presence of 4-CzIPN under visible light irradiation conditions, affording a variety of BTBT-DO propellanes. Several spectroscopic studies and control experiments support that this reaction proceeds via the EnT process. The BTBT-DO propellanes enable further derivatization, including Pd-catalyzed transformations. This strategy provides an opportunity to access heteroacene-derived propellanes in materials science.
papers.title: Synthesis of Benzothieno[3,2-b]benzothiophene Propellanes via [2 + 2] Photocycloadditions through Energy Transfer Process

papers.abstract: Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) are widely used to tune the properties of metal electrode surfaces, with applications ranging from sensing to electrocatalysis. However, the structure, coverage, and stability of SAMs often evolve under applied potential, and no single experimental technique provides a complete description of these changes. This work demonstrates the application of several surface characterization techniques, including voltammetric, spectroscopic, and gravimetric methods, on a model SAM system comprised of 4-mercaptobenzonitrile (4-MBN) on a gold electrode. We evaluate and cross-validate these complementary techniques, discussing their ability to support inferences about dynamic surface behavior. These analyses provide information regarding molecular identity, relative orientation, surface accessibility, and adsorbate coverage; specific to the 4-MBN SAM we report for the first time the adsorption isotherm and kinetic parameters for adsorption. This study demonstrates a characterization framework to investigate SAM dynamics and aims to support contemporary in situ SAM studies within the electrochemistry and surface science communities.
papers.title: Cross-Validation of Electrochemical, Spectroscopic, and Gravimetric Methods for Characterizing Self-Assembled Monolayers

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT: Mixtures of water and NaCl, the archetypal salt, play important roles in industrial processes and natural environments on Earth and throughout the Solar System, yet their structural diversity at low temperatures remains poorly understood. Here, we determine the crystal structure of the metastable sodium chloride hydrate formed upon flash freezing using three-dimensional electron diffraction. Our analysis reveals a sodium chloride pentahydrate (NaCl∙5H2O), which consists of one-dimensional chains of hydrated sodium octahedra, with Cl− ions and water molecules located between the chains and linked by hydrogen-bonding interactions. NaCl∙5H2O introduces a new structural motif in the NaCl hydrate family and differs considerably from the thermodynamically stable and denser sodium chloride dihydrate that forms upon slow cooling. Fully dissociated ions in this metastable phase suggest that rapid freezing of saline solutions may provide a synthesis route to hydrates that retain local coordination environments resembling those of the parent solution.
papers.title: Metastable hydrate of sodium chloride is a pentahydrate as revealed by 3D electron diffraction

papers.abstract: The enantioselective synthesis of bicyclic dihydrouracil and sulfamide derivatives through an intramolecular 1,3-diamination of acrylates is described. The method relies on the cyclization of urea and bis-sulfamide substrates, bearing a remote conjugated p-nitrophenyl ester, in the presence of a chiral isothiourea catalyst and diphenyl phosphate as an acid additive, affording the corresponding bicyclic products in good yields (up to 97%) and with excellent enantioselectivities (typically 94:6-97:3, up to 99.5:0.5 er). The transformation proceeds through a tandem intramolecular aza-Michael addition/ lactamisation sequence, with the latter releasing the catalyst and closing the catalytic cycle. Covalent activation of the acrylate through the formation of an acyl ammonium intermediate, combined with non-covalent interactions that facilitate nucleophilic attack and organize the reactive species, provides a plausible basis for the high levels of stereocontrol observed. This metal- and oxidant-free approach overcomes the low electrophilicity of acrylates and shows that nitrogen nucleophiles can participate in isothiourea catalysis.
papers.title: Enantioselective intramolecular 1,3-diamination of acrylates

papers.abstract: Accurately predicting the steep, S-shaped water adsorption isotherms of mildly hydrophobic MOFs and other hydrophobic porous materials remains challenging. This difficulty stems from the delicate balance between framework–water and water–water interactions that governs cooperative pore filling. Here, we develop a machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP), trained on reliable density functional theory reference data, for the prototypical mildly hydrophobic channel MOF MIP-211(Al). Combined with a Molecular Dynamics-based transition-matrix Monte Carlo (MD-TMMC) scheme, this accurate MLIP enables to predict the sorption isotherm in excellent agreement with the corresponding experimental data, capturing both the low-pressure gradual water uptake increase and the sharp adsorption step at P/P0 ≈ 0.3. This accuracy enables to elucidate the adsorption mechanism, from initial adsorption to complete pore filling: water first anchors through a characteristic OCOO···H2O···μ-OH dual hydrogenbond interaction motif; as these sites saturate, a secondary and competitive OCOO···H2O···H2O dual interaction motif emerges, driving cooperative self-assembly and triggering the adsorption step. At saturation, the confined water network approaches, but does not fully reach, bulk-water connectivity. This work demonstrates that combining a reliable MLIP-training level of theory with an appropriate MC strategy enables both quantitative prediction and mechanistic understanding of water adsorption, providing a foundation for the rational design of mildly hydrophobic MOFs of key interest for heat transformation technologies and water harvesting applications.
papers.title: Achieving Accurate Prediction of Water Adsorption in Mildly Hydrophobic MOFs

papers.abstract: Main-group compounds show drastic differences in properties and reactivity between their n and n+2 oxidation states. While this often precludes transition-metal mimetic redox catalysis, precise control over prevalent oxidation states in a switchable compound could offer promising avenues for main-group-mediated processes. We demonstrate that hypercoordination-induced valence tautomerism unlocks high effective Lewis acidity in a phosphorus cation. By employing a redox-non-innocent, pincer-coordinated phosphenium(+III) cation, we enable low-barrier inversion at phosphorus coupled with valence tautomerism. Counterintuitively, adding a neutral Lewis base does not quench the cation's electrophilicity; instead, it triggers valence tautomerism, generating a formal phosphorus(+V) cation. This hypercoordinated species exhibits enhanced reactivity and is capable of abstracting fluoride from stable inorganic anions like [SbF 6 ] -. Furthermore, in the presence of hydrosilanes, metal-free catalytic hydrodefluorination of fluoroalkanes is achieved.
papers.title: Lewis Base-Induced Valence Tautomerism in a Phosphorus Cation Enables the Activation of Strong Element-Fluorine Bonds

papers.abstract: Blood–brain barrier (BBB) permeability is a major challenge in the development of drugs targeting the central nervous system (CNS). Computational prediction methods can help prioritize candidate compounds and reduce the experimental workload during early drug discovery. In this study, machine learning models were developed to predict the blood-to-brain concentration ratio expressed as its decimal logarithm (logBB). The objective was to investigate whether molecular docking scores obtained with AutoDock Vina for P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP), together with quantum-chemical descriptors, could provide additional information for logBB prediction. The dataset comprised 685 compounds. A linear regression analysis identified eight factors associated with logBB: hydrogen bond donors, gas-phase electronic energy, electronic energy difference between water and hexane, number of heavy atoms, LogP, gas-phase geometry optimization time, number of aromatic rings, and fraction of sp3-hybridized carbon atoms. Notably, the electronic energy difference between water and hexane showed a stronger association with logBB than the corresponding Gibbs free energy difference, suggesting that electronic energy descriptors may provide complementary information. Higher-level quantum-chemical calculations will be required to investigate this finding further. Twenty-one machine learning models were evaluated. The selected support vector regression model using a radial basis function kernel (SVR-RBF; C = 0.869, ε = 0.135, γ = 0.165) was trained on 585 compounds and evaluated on a held-out validation set of 100 compounds, achieving an R2 of 0.605, an MAE of 0.368, and an RMSE of 0.459. Finally, the computational time analysis showed that descriptor generation was strongly dependent on molecular weight, with quantum-chemical calculations and molecular docking accounting for most of the computational cost. Overall, this work highlights the potential of combining physicochemical, molecular docking, and quantum-chemical descriptors for machine learning-based logBB prediction.
papers.title: A Machine Learning Approach to logBB Prediction Combining Molecular Docking and Quantum-Chemical Descriptors

papers.abstract: We report a boomerang-type iridium catalyst that combines the high activity of homogeneous catalysis with spontaneous and quantitative catalyst recovery without external operation. The catalyst consists of a Cp*Ir complex immobilized on a cross-linked poly(acrylic acid) gel (PAA). Upon addition of formic acid (FA), Ir species are released into solution, enabling the aqueous transfer hydrogenation of a broad range of ketones under air without additional additives. In situ analyses confirmed the presence of soluble Cp*Ir reaction intermediates during the reaction. Upon complete consumption of formic acid (FA), the dissolved Ir species were spontaneously and quantitatively recaptured by the support without requiring temperature modulation or solvent exchange. The catalyst retains over 90% of its initial activity over five consecutive runs, with no detectable Ir remaining in the reaction solution after recovery. This autonomous boomerang mechanism provides a promising strategy for combining the high activity of homogeneous catalysts with the reusability of heterogeneous catalysts.
papers.title: A Boomerang Catalyst Combining High Catalytic Activity and Reusability for Aqueous Transfer Hydrogenation of Ketones

papers.abstract: Heterogeneous olefin metathesis catalysts composed of highly dispersed Mo sites on support carriers are used to produce key olefin building blocks for higher value-added products, e.g. the Shell Higher Olefin Process (SHOP). However, understanding the nature of Mo sites in catalysts, i.e. molybdenum oxides supported on amorphous supports like silica, MoOx/SiO2, is hampered by a low fraction of surface metal sites (low loading), the possible distribution of surface species and the lack of very sensitive characterization methods to distinguish subtle changes in the coordination environment of Mo sites on amorphous supports. Here, we show how 95Mo NMR spectroscopy enables identifying various Mo sites in olefin metathesis catalysts, pointing out the presence of isolated tetrahedral Mo-dioxo sites along with MoOx clusters, whose quantities depend on the preparation methods and Mo-loadings. Most notable is the use of NMR signatures as a structural refinement tool. Following a validation with molecular mono- and di-oxo Mo(VI) complexes characterized by single-crystal XRD measurements, we are able to determine the exact coordination environment, geometry and structural parameters of the dominant Mo sites, a highly dispersed dioxo Mo bis-grafted species in a tetrahedral environment with d(Mo=O) = 1.71 ± 0.07 Å, d(Mo-OSi) = 1.91 ± 0.15 Å, ∠(O-Mo-O) = 107 ± 7° and ∠(Mo-O-Si) = 140 ± 40°. This structure closely resembles this of the [MoO2(OSi(OtBu)3)2] molecular analogue. Additionally, this signature indicates a narrow distribution of Mo sites, highlighting the well-defined nature of these sites. Noteworthily, while well-defined, the large promotional effect observed upon co-feeding 2,3-dimethyl-1-butene further supports the role of nearby protons to initiate metathesis, rather than the sole nature of the isolated Mo sites themselves, hence the importance of promoters and the small fraction of active sites in their absence.
papers.title: Structure Determination of Surface Sites in Heterogeneous Olefin Metathesis Catalysts from 95Mo NMR Signatures

papers.abstract: Fe incorporation strongly modifies the activity of Ni-based electrocatalysts, but how heterogeneous surface states contribute to this behavior remain unclear due to improper understanding about intermediate evolution. Here, we investigate whether correlations between spatially resolved spectroscopic features and electrochemical responses can reveal distinct energetic and kinetic characteristics of NiFe electrodes. We combine in-situ Raman mapping, electrochemistry and microkinetic modeling to study three NiFe electrodes prepared under different Fe-deposition conditions. Potential-dependent spectra reveal site-to-site variations in NiOOH related vibrational features and higher-wavenumber oxygen-associated spectral signatures across individual surface sites. Correlation and regression analyses identify a compact set of Raman descriptors associated with the electrochemical response, while sitespecific predicted scores reveal distinct potential-dependent trajectory patterns. Raman-guided projection into a model-derived intermediate-energy space further enables comparison of these trajectory phenotypes within a common thermodynamic framework. Although the projected energetic distributions exhibit substantial overlap, their arrangement and model-estimated kinetic characteristics vary across different trajectory phenotypes and kinetic regimes. These findings suggest that spatially heterogeneous NiFe surface states may exhibit different kinetic responses under applied potential, instead of following a uniform catalytic evolution. More broadly, this study demonstrates the potential of integrating independent spectroscopic and electrochemical observations with microkinetic modelling to uncover energetic and kinetic heterogeneity in OER electrocatalysis.
papers.title: Uncovering Heterogeneous Energetic Trajectories in NiFe Oxygen Evolution Electrocatalysis through Integrated Raman, Electrochemical and Microkinetic Analysis

papers.abstract: Organic molecular crystals with piezoelectric and pyroelectric responses are emerging as soft, biocompatible materials for next-generation energy harvesting. However, quantifying crystal polarity in such materials—and its variations under mechanical or thermal stimuli—on a structural basis remains challenging. Here, we estimate pyroelectric coefficients directly from high-resolution X-ray quantum crystallography (QCr) via accurate modelling of hydrogen positions and electron densities. QCr modelling of a series of piezoelectric crystals reveals in-crystal molecular dipole moments (μ) and spontaneous polarization (P S ) at variable temperatures (~100 and ~298 K) with pronounced crystal-field effects, including enhanced μ relative to isolated molecules and elevated P S . Temperature-dependent variations in P S (∆P S /∆T) predict pyroelectric behaviour, corroborated by variable-temperature voltage-output measurements in γ-glycine. The pyroelectric coefficients (p) and P S values thus estimated agree well with experimental measurements. The results demonstrate QCr as a powerful route to elucidating the molecular and electronic level origins of pyroelectric phenomena in crystalline materials, with potential extension to piezoelectric and ferroelectric properties.
papers.title: Direct Determination of Pyroelectric Coefficients in Molecular Crystals by X-ray Quantum Crystallography

papers.abstract: Mapping a protein’s local environment is essential for understanding its cellular roles. Proximity labeling (PL) identifies nearby proteins, while photoproximity labeling (PPL) adds temporal control through light activation. However, intracellular applications of these methods commonly rely on genetically encoded fusions that could alter protein localization or function and offer limited control over defined, site-specific post-translational modifications (PTMs). Here, we combine chemical protein synthesis with bead loading (BL) to enable live-cell PPL using fully chemically synthesized photocatalyst–protein of interest (PC–POI) conjugates. Synthesis enables site-specific PC attachment, while BL delivers conjugates directly into cells, bypassing endocytosis and preventing endosomal trapping. As a proof of concept, we demonstrate the strategy using chemically synthesized small ubiquitin-like modifier (SUMO) proteins. Notably, PC selection was critical: conjugation to Eosin Y altered SUMO2 nuclear localization, whereas 5-deazaflavin (DF) preserved both nuclear localization and the ability to conjugate to cellular proteins. Using TAMRA–DF–SUMO conjugates, blue-light-triggered deazaflavin–diazirine energy-transfer (DarT) labeling captured nearby proteins for enrichment and quantitative proteomics. Comparing SUMO2 with its non-conjugatable variant SUMO2ΔG93 and its paralog SUMO1 showed that the approach resolves proximity profiles associated with conjugation competence and paralog identity. The biological relevance of the SUMO interactome was supported by established associations of selected proteins and by the finding that approximately 70% of proteins preferentially captured by SUMO2 over SUMO2ΔG93 were reported as SUMO2 substrates. This work establishes live-cell PPL without genetically encoded labeling fusions or target-protein overexpression, opening opportunities to investigate how defined, site-specific PTMs shape local protein environments.
papers.title: Combining Chemical Protein Synthesis and Cell Delivery for Photoproximity Labeling in Living Cells

papers.abstract: Electrolyte additives, present at a few weight percent or less, decide whether a lithium battery forms a stable solidelectrolyte interphase, survives high-voltage operation, tolerates trace water and HF, or resists fire. For three decades most additives were found by trial and error, and the few design rules that emerged, most famously “a lower LUMO than the solvent”, were known to fail almost as soon as they were formulated. Here we organize the computational literature on additive discovery, from the first quantum-chemical studies of vinylene carbonate (2002) to self-driving laboratories, chemical foundation models and LLM agents (2026), into a step-by-step roadmap: define the function the additive must perform; choose a descriptor that is actually predictive for that function; define and enumerate the chemical space; screen it with tiered quantum-chemical funnels; establish the decomposition mechanism; accelerate with machine learning; generate candidates beyond existing libraries; simulate the interphase the additive builds; and close the loop with automated experiments. For each step we summarize what has been established, what has only been correlated, and what has failed. We show that the hierarchy of redox descriptors (frontier orbitals → vertical and adiabatic electron affinities and ionization potentials → thermodynamic cycles → Li+-and anion-containing clusters → explicit-interface dynamics) is now quantitatively documented, that solvation-and product-level descriptors are emerging as the missing axes, and that the decisive bottleneck has shifted from candidate generation to reliable, fast, function-specific experimental labels. We close with a table of what each class of method can and cannot predict and with a realistic outline of a closed-loop additive-discovery framework.
papers.title: How to Discover New Electrolyte Additives for Lithium Batteries: A Computational Roadmap

papers.abstract: Extending density-based bootstrap embedding (BE) with perturbative triples to large molecules requires control of both fragment solver cost and tensor storage. We present a restricted and unrestricted BE-CCSD(T) implementation combining density-fitted embedding transformations, fragment parallelism, and streamed contractions of triples density contributions. Explicit one-and two-particle terms and the correction to the coupled-cluster multipliers are retained without assembling a molecular two-particle density matrix or storing a complete triples tensor. Fixed-order fragmentation bounds the local correlated problem under stated locality assumptions, while blockwise evaluation controls temporary storage. Timings for
papers.title: Scalable Density-Based Bootstrap Embedding with Perturbative Triples for Large Molecular Systems

papers.abstract: Computational electrocatalysis has contributed significantly to the design of electrocatalysts for energy conversion and storage. Yet three avoidable shortcomings constrain the reliability and reusability of computational results: incomplete reporting, oversimplification of reaction pathways and/or active sites considered, and inconsistent protocols for constructing free-energy changes (ΔG). Researchers may therefore be forced to repeat calculations simply to recover structures, verify reference conventions, or identify the source of conflicting results. This Perspective argues that reproducibility must encompass the full computational record: electronic-structure settings, surface models, atomic configurations, thermochemical and electrochemical corrections, and the explored reaction network. We examine the roles of surface structure, coverage, stability, mechanistic breadth, and descriptor choice under operating bias, and propose modular benchmarks spanning numerical verification, surface chemistry, electrified interfaces, and mechanistic validation. We also outline how journals and repositories can strengthen methodological transparency and Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable (FAIR) data deposition. Our aim is to stimulate discussion around a persistent reproducibility deficit that leads to inefficient use of computational resources, obstructs cumulative science, and leaves valuable data unavailable for benchmarking, data mining, and trustworthy artificial-intelligence-assisted discovery. More complete and standardized computational records would make results both more credible today and substantially more reusable tomorrow.
papers.title: Reproducibility, Benchmarks, and Mechanistic Diversity: Building Trust in Computational Electrocatalysis for the AI Era

papers.abstract: Rapid analogue generation is central to early-stage drug discovery, creating demand for synthetic methods that combine modularity, operational simplicity, and broad substrate compatibility. N-Heterocyclesubstituted α-amino carbonyls are poorly served in this respect, their synthesis largely depending on a narrow pool of commercially available α-halogenated carbonyls. Here we report a one-pot three-component platform that addresses this gap through a formal reductive 1,2-aminoalkylation of ynoates, combining phosphine-catalysed a-funαtionalisation with a photoredox-mediated decarboxylative Giese reaction. The method accommodates azoles, lactams and imides alongside diverse carboxylic acids and ynoates, enables late-stage diversification of pharmaceuticals, and is compatible with array-based library synthesis for rapid analogue generation.
papers.title: Modular Synthesis of N-Heterocycle-Substituted α-Amino Esters

papers.abstract: The growing number of chemical foundation models calls for a standardized benchmarking method both for practitioners choosing representations and researchers identifying gaps. Previous work that ranked latent abilities of various chemical embeddings to predict ADMET properties suffered from significant shortcomings, including the use of biased datasets incongruent with real world usage and overstating statistically significant differences in model performance. We derive from first principles a variance inflation factor of (M+1)/3 for the Bayesian Bradley-Terry model evaluating M models on E endpoints at the exchangeable null and use numerical simulation to show variance inflation is still present in the non-exchangeable case. We propose a new method to directly model the margin of error as a function of latent ability and use it to evaluate models retrospectively on the datasets from the OpenADMET Polaris, ExpansionRx, and PXR competitions. We compare 35 embeddings and 13 end-to-end fine-tuned models across 17 ADMET endpoints. Although endpoint-to-endpoint variability means that no neural representation is expected to outperform ECFP on a hypothetical new endpoint in more than 95% of cases, our model concludes that 29 of 47 representations outperform ECFP in terms of latent ability with posterior probability above 0.95.
papers.title: A Latent Ability Model for Benchmarking Molecular Representations

papers.abstract: This work presents a retrieval resource covering 72,199 protein–ligand complexes from the Protein Data Bank. Each complex carries a 1,280-dimensional pocket embedding, obtained by mean-pooling final-layer ESM-2 representations over binding-site residues within 8 Å of the ligand and computed per chain rather than over a concatenation of all polymer chains; a 2,048-bit RDKit Morgan fingerprint of the ligand, taken from the idealized Chemical Component Dictionary entry and therefore shared by complexes binding the same component (26,619 distinct fingerprints across the 72,199 rows); and HDF5 coordinates, per-residue heavy-atom centroids for the pocket and per-atom for the ligand, with residue and element identifiers. A residue-to-token mapping makes each pooled embedding reproducible from the released files. FAISS indices are provided over the two modalities separately, because they answer different questions: pocket-only retrieval recovers a same-UniProt complex at rank 1 for 81.2% of queries, whereas ligand-only retrieval is the stronger signal for chemotype search.
papers.title: Pocket and ligand embeddings for 72,199 protein–ligand complexes from the Protein Data Bank

papers.abstract: We show that power-law extrapolation of the correlation energy can be carried from a sequence of orbital bases into a shell hierarchy within one molecular virtual space. In shell-nested virtual spaces (SNVS), atomic natural orbitals guide the radial and angular content of successive layers, and the correlating-orbital count beyond the valence-virtual space replaces the cardinal number in a two-point formula. The construction uses one Hartree–Fock reference in one parent basis. We calibrate and cross-validate the formula for 200 small molecular states of H and B–F at the MP2, CCSD and CCSD(T) levels, then test MP2 and CCSD transfer without refitting on 40 larger systems. In the standard ANO family, the full quadruple-zeta layer pair gives an MP2 RMS error of 0.79 mEh for the larger set, compared with 2.16 mEh for conventional extrapolation. Diffuse augmentation reduces the anion bias, and placing the excess functions in the valence-virtual space preserves the counting variable. The CCSD and reaction-energy tests show how the benefits depend on correlation level and error cancellation. Measured CCSD(T) workflow costs are comparable to those of the conventional pair. These results demonstrate the usefulness of atomic shell information for molecular extrapolation and motivate basis sets designed for the successive SNVS layers.
papers.title: Correlation-Energy Extrapolation within Shell-Nested Virtual Spaces

papers.abstract: Pharmaceutical formulation development frequently encounters formulation–process conditions that fail before a viable product is produced, leaving downstream performance unobservable and experimental feasibility unknown a priori. Here, we demonstrate a closed-loop formulation-development workflow that jointly optimizes formulation and process variables while learning experimental feasibility from physical outcomes. Using caffeine-loaded extended-release pellets produced by wet granulation and extrusion-spheronization, ANDROMEDA 1 selected formulation compositions and processing conditions within a large mixed categorical and numerical design space. Across 51 experiments performed in 13 sequential batches, 29 conditions produced pellets suitable for downstream characterization and 22 (43%) were infeasible. Failed experiments were retained as feasibility observations without assigning artificial drug release scores. Among feasible formulations, the best observed deviation from a predefined four-hour zero-order release target decreased from 1.63 to 0.17 fraction-hours. Release performance, pellet morphology and drug loading followed distinct trajectories, with an empirical trade-off between release deviation and median pellet aspect ratio. Retrospective Gaussian-process modelling showed that replacing an excipient-slot encoding with slot-independent material mass fractions increased leave-one-out cross validated R2 for release prediction from 0.39 to 0.60. Adding four derived wet-mass descriptors reduced release prediction R2 to 0.38 but yielded the highest morphology prediction R2 (0.64). Neither alternative representation improved forward-in-time release prediction. Together, these results show that unknown feasibility, competing product attributes and formulation representation can be incorporated within a single adaptive formulation-process workflow. Analyses further identify design space coverage and representation choice as important considerations for machine learning-guided pharmaceutical development.
papers.title: Closed-loop formulation–process optimization under unknown feasibility for extended-release pellets

papers.abstract: Polymer composite linings are increasingly used in trenchless renewal technologies. These technologies are advantageous when material durability, structural requirements, application quality and service exposure are considered together, yet renewal decisions are still made largely case by case, often overlooking some of these aspects. This paper develops an evidence-based decision framework in which every decision rule is an explicit, traceable statement linked to measured or published evidence. The evidence base integrates long-term hygrothermal ageing of reinforced polyester and elastomer-modified epoxy linings, linings removed from service after up to ten years, measured application quality, cure kinetics, material identity verification and environmental assessment. Screening flowcharts decide whether to renew, repair or replace and which lining system or polymer composite is technically suitable; an evidence matrix then compares the remaining options with stated evidence levels; and a staged quality assurance and quality control protocol, linked to a defect–cause–control table, makes application quality verifiable. Three asset archetypes demonstrate how it routes decisions and what records each decision must leave.
papers.title: Decision Framework for Polymer Composite Linings in Trenchless Renewal: Integrating Materials Durability, Operational Performance, Application Quality, and Environmental Sustainability

papers.abstract: The free-energy surface (FES) of a mobile species in a crystalline host governs its behavior within the material, including properties such as adsorption and transport, but reducing it to quantitative descriptors remains challenging. We present the Energy–GeOmetry Analysis Toolkit (EnGOAT), an open-source framework for the energetic, geometric, and topological analysis of volumetric FES data. Building on the TuTraSt algorithm, EnGOAT partitions the FES into basins and transition states, quantifies their volumes, surface areas, and energy–volume histograms, represents their connectivity as periodic graphs from which minimum-energy pathways and merge trees are obtained, and computes directional self-diffusion coefficients by kinetic Monte Carlo. Because accessibility is defined from energy isosurfaces of the FES rather than from van der Waals radii, the extracted descriptors are probe-specific and reflect the energy landscape actually experienced by the mobile species. Results are stored in a JSON/NumPy data model suited for high-throughput screening and can be explored with a dedicated visualization tool. We demonstrate EnGOAT for CH 4 adsorption in a zeolite and for Li + ion transport in a ceramic electrolyte.
papers.title: EnGOAT: An Energy–Geometry Analysis Toolkit for Free-Energy Surfaces of Mobile Species in Crystalline Materials

papers.abstract: Replacement of C–C bonds with isoelectronic B–N units offers a compelling yet underdeveloped strategy for modulating molecular structure and electronic properties. Here we report that tacn-family ligands (1,4,7-triazacyclononane and its N-alkyl derivatives) enable the straightforward assembly of polycyclic boronium(+2) cations through a simple one-pot reaction with Me 2 SBHBr 2 under ambient conditions. These reactions produce rigid cage structures in which three fused five-membered rings are formed in a single step via tridentate coordination of the ligand to a [BH] 2+ core. The resulting boronium salts are readily isolated and exhibit remarkable thermal and aqueous stability, as demonstrated by multinuclear NMR spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, and differential scanning calorimetry. In the parent system, the N–H groups display Brønsted acidity (pKa1 ≈ 3.2) while maintaining structural integrity, with reversible protonation/deprotonation behavior observed. Electrostatic potential analyses reveal that substitution of B–N linkages for C–C bonds preserves overall molecular topology while substantially altering surface electron density, underscoring the utility of B–N/C–C isosterism for tuning intermolecular interactions. Limiting ligand donation to a bidentate mode affords a related bicyclic boronium(+1) framework containing a tertiary amine, whose geometry, reduced basicity (pKb1 ≈ 8.7), and reactivity of which are strongly influenced by the adjacent cationic boron center. Protonation yields a dication featuring a short N–H···H–B distance consistent with a dihydrogen bond, and thermal H 2 elimination cleanly generates the parent tridentate boronium cage. These findings demonstrate that tacn ligands provide a general and operationally simple route to robust boronium-based cage architectures. The resulting three-dimensional, electrostatically tunable frameworks expand the accessible structural space of organoboron chemistry and suggest potential utility as scaffolds in applications where shape and charge distribution are critical, including molecular recognition and pharmacophore design.
papers.title: From Boron Flatland to 3D Pharmacophore Space: Tacn-Supported Boronium Cage Cations

papers.abstract: The effect of TaC additions on the oxidation behaviour of ZrB 2 -SiC based ultra-high-temperature ceramics, with and without AlN, was evaluated at 1600 °C in stagnant air. Three spark-plasma-sintered compositions were studied: ZSA721 (70ZrB2-20SiC-10AlN), ZSAT72-5-5 (70ZrB 2 -20SiC-5AlN-5TaC), and ZST631 (60ZrB2-30SiC-10TaC). After 10 h, ZSA721 gained 58 mg cm -2 and formed a 1388 ± 100 μm oxide layer. Partial replacement of AlN by TaC lowered the mass gain to 45 mg cm -2 and produced a thicker SiO 2 -rich surface layer, but the total oxide thickness remained comparable at 1357 ± 100 μm, while the SiC-depleted zone increased from 156 ± 12 to 240 ± 15 μm. To promote SiO 2 formation further, we increased the SiC content (ZST631); however, oxidation of ZST631 resulted in the highest mass gain (69 mg cm -2 ), the thickest oxide layer (1477 ± 200 μm) and a discontinuous SiO 2 scale. Our results, when contextualized with the research literature, indicate that TaC promotes cooperative degradation, potentially through porosity created by gas-evolution and restricted lateral spreading and healing of the Ta-containing borosilicate glass, thereby hindering the oxidation resistance.
papers.title: Effect of TaC additions on the oxidation behaviour of ZrB2-SiC-AlN ultra-high temperature ceramics at 1600 °C

papers.abstract: Turning a scientific idea into an experiment often requires researchers to build, configure and repeatedly adapt the labo- ratory around it. This work demands resources and specialized expertise that can place ambitious experiments beyond reach. Here we introduce a framework for self-evolving laboratories (SEL), connecting computation, physical experiments and AI models through persistent cycles of observation and revision. GPT Astra uses camera observations and physical feedback to adapt robotic actions, digital twins and CAD designs. These changes are retained as reusable skills and infrastructure, allowing the laboratory to develop alongside its scientific tasks. In our fume-hood SEL prototype, GPT Astra identified the need for a beaker holder and storage stand and generated successive designs for on-demand 3D printing. Four holder generations and two stand generations culminated in parts integrated into the robotic workflow with operator assistance. A photoresist campaign proposed by Raven, an agentic AI platform for materials discovery, connects this platform to materials fabrication. Exposure to a 405 nm continuous-wave laser in the two-photon polymerization setup produced circular features that survived development; optical microscopy and reduced acrylate-band absorbance in ATR–FTIR support polymerization and qualitative double-bond conversion. The scientific workflow connects experimental outcomes and retained capabilities to the resources needed to establish and extend them. By making laboratory capabilities reusable and adaptable, SEL offer a path towards broader participation in experimental science, empowering researchers to build and extend the tools their ideas require. Project website: https://ai4ssi.github.io/self-evolving-superintelligence-lab/.
papers.title: Self-Evolving Laboratories Through Persistent Digital and Physical Adaptation

papers.abstract: Desalination brine, a byproduct of seawater desalination, contains valuable resources, including magnesium. Recovering magnesium requires selectively retaining Mg 2+ while allowing the dominant monovalent cation, Na + , to permeate. Nanofiltration (NF) membranes fabricated by interfacial polymerization are promising for this Mg 2+ /Na + separation, but their performance depends on coupled formulation and processing variables that are inefficient to optimize through trial and error. Here, we demonstrate a workflow integrating dataset curation, forward prediction, and inverse design of thin-film composite NF membranes. A dataset of 1,253 entries, comprising literature and in-house records, was cleaned, imputed, and augmented through chemically constrained permutation of interchangeable polymer, solvent, and salt variables in the training split only. Optimized extremely randomized tree regressors predicted pure water permeability, solute rejection, and intermediate membrane properties, achieving test-set coefficients of determination above 0.79. Shapley analysis indicated that permeability was governed primarily by formulation and processing variables, whereas rejection depended mainly on solute identity and charge, as well as membrane tightness. Using Bayesian optimization with a scalarized objective, two membrane recipes with favorable Mg 2+ /Na + selectivity were identified and experimentally validated. The inversely designed membranes exhibited the required Mg 2+ /Na + selectivity, demonstrating the capability of this workflow to design Mg 2+ -selective NF membranes for resource recovery from desalination brine.
papers.title: Machine learning–driven inverse design of nanofiltration membranes for selective Mg2+/Na+ separation

papers.abstract: Quantum simulation has been proposed as a route to treating strongly correlated electronic structure problems relevant to catalysis, but most existing studies focus on faulttolerant algorithms beyond current hardware capabilities. Here we assess the feasibility of near-term quantum simulation for catalytic materials through industrially relevant use cases. We consider zeolite clusters from classical QM/MM simulations relevant to NH3-SCR, and construct electronic active-space and embedding-based models of the catalytic active site. Using variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) ansätze, we estimate qubit requirements and circuit depths to produce the ground-state for both full and reduced Hamiltonians. Direct simulation of the full system is intractable on near-term devices, but fragmentation and active-space approaches, combined with low-rank Local Unitary Cluster Jastrow ansatz constructions, substantially reduce resource requirements. These results indicate that, while full catalytic models remain out of reach, reduced representations of chemically relevant fragments begin to approach the capacity of near-term quantum hardware. This highlights the role of physically informed model reduction in applying quantum simulation to applied materials problems.
papers.title: Perspective on the Feasibility of Near-Term Quantum Simulation for Industrially Relevant Catalyst Materials

papers.abstract: The use of alginate-only beads, alginate–Opuntia (AO) beads, and chitosan-treated AO beads for the removal of Cu(II) and a PET glitter (a microplastic surrogate) from water has been investigated. The beads were shaken for 6 h in jars of water that had glitter, Cu(II), or both in them, and AO beads soaked in dilute acetic acid with no chitosan were used to check the acid. The Cu(II) removal increased by 13.72 percentage points with the addition of Opuntia and by a further 24.75 points with the chitosan post-treatment, and both increases were found in each of the three bead batches (p ≤ 0.0015). In the presence of 2.00 g of glitter, the chitosan-treated beads removed about 84% of the Cu(II), about the same as without glitter. About 8% of the Cu was also lost in the jars without beads. Meanwhile, the glitter removal increased by about 7 points with Opuntia but changed by less than 0.25 points with chitosan (batch-level p = 0.635 and 0.389). No significant difference was found between the separately run acid control and untreated AO beads. According to these results, the glitter capture of the beads was improved by the addition of Opuntia, and most of the improvement in Cu(II) removal was obtained with the chitosan post-treatment.
papers.title: Removal of Cu(II) and a PET Glitter Microplastic Surrogate by Alginate, Alginate–Opuntia, and Chitosan-Treated Alginate–Opuntia Beads

papers.abstract: Renewable biopolymers are increasingly explored as alternatives to fossil-derived materials, yet bio-based origin alone does not determine performance or commercial relevance. This review compares alginate, lignin, cellulose, chitosan, and starch through an integrated structure–processing–architecture–property–scalability framework. Molecular functionality is linked to processing pathways and to the resulting coatings, fibers, crosslinked networks, porous structures, carbon materials, and composite architectures. A dedicated cross-cutting discussion then argues why three comparison axes common in the existing literature, chemistry, biodegradability, and application category, each fail, on their own, to predict which material and processing combination is actually useful for a given job, and what a comparison needs to include instead. The review closes with application-specific design rules to support material and processing selection for sustainable packaging, thermal management, water purification and separations, carbon capture, energy storage and electrocatalysis, biomedical scaffolds and controlled release, and construction materials.
papers.title: Structure–Processing–Architecture–Property Relationships and Scalability in Renewable Polymer Selection for Sustainable Biomaterials

papers.abstract: Generative models are increasingly proposed for choosing where adaptive molecular dynamics should restart, but whether their proposals are physically sound starting points and whether they outperform simple rules has rarely been tested together. Using adenylate kinase, we first audited a workflow that reconstructs restart structures from a diffusion model's latent space: judged by per-domain native contacts calibrated on unbiased MD, most reconstructed structures were damaged from their first frame, and the rare states identified from them were partially unfolded LID domains. We then compared restart selection by a denoising diffusion probabilistic model with a latent-space Gaussian ablation, least-counts and two unbiased baselines, starting only from intact MD frames, with targets fixed and timestamped before any production run, equal simulation time and three replicates of every strategy and baseline. No strategy reached the primary target within the pre-specified 0.84 µs per series, so the binary comparison cannot distinguish them; adaptive restarts covered the reference distribution slightly better than the baselines, and in an exploratory closest-approach analysis the diffusion model did not come closer to the target than the simple strategies. The target differed from the data shown to the strategies only in a combination of domain states, which the diffusion model did not propose. Selecting starts by novelty in the latent space, with or without a learned model, tended to choose frames farther from the target than random picks, and the diffusion model's samples stayed close to the data. The value of a generative model lies in proposing structures beyond the data, yet that is the capability that produced the damaged restarts; confined to intact frames, its role reduces to a novelty rule on existing frames. We recommend domain-resolved integrity gates, pre-specified targets, simple baselines at equal simulation time and replicated runs for evaluating generative adaptive sampling.
papers.title: Diffusion-Model-Based Restart Selection for Adaptive Sampling of Adenylate Kinase: Structural Integrity Assessment and Comparison with Simple Baselines

papers.abstract: Electrolyte-gated organic transistor (EGOT) biosensors enable label-free volumetric biosensing, yet their performance in physiological environments remains constrained by polymer microstructure and inefficient ion–channel coupling. Here, we demonstrate that substrate-induced nanocorrugation reconfigures mixed ionic–electronic transport in poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) channels. The corrugated SiO2/Si substrates alter the structural and electrochemical response of conformally deposited PEDOT:PSS channels. Structural and electrochemical measurements show changes in molecular ordering, crystalline orientation, local structural heterogeneity, and mixed ionic-electronic transport in the nanocorrugated films. Compared with flat counterparts, the nanocorrugated devices exhibit enhanced molecular ordering, improved ion accessibility, and stronger gate–channel coupling. The proposed platform enables ultrasensitive nucleic-acid detection and label-free sensing of stroke-related protein biomarkers in buffer, serum, and whole blood. For DNA sensing in buffer, the mean response exceeded the detection threshold at 20 aM, the regression-derived threshold concentration was ~15.4 aM, and statistically significant separation from the negative control began at 200 aM. IL-6 produces a concentration-dependent response down to the lowest tested concentration of 1 fM. Overall, nanoscale corrugation enables a route to tune ion transport, reconfigure the polymer network, and enhance volumetric transduction in conducting polymer EGOTs, thereby facilitating robust biosensing under physiologically relevant environments.
papers.title: Nanocorrugated Conducting Polymer–Based Electrochemical Transistors with Enhanced Ionic-Electronic Transduction for Ultrasensitive Biomolecular Detection

papers.abstract: Ferroelectric nematic (N F ) liquid crystals are fluids with macroscopic polar order, yet the molecular pathway by which an isotropic liquid spontaneously develops long-range polar order remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrated that microsecond-scale, unbiased all-atom molecular dynamics simulations can reproduce the spontaneous development of strong, system-wide polar order from an isotropic state. For DIO, highly polar local domains emerged upon cooling but remained nanoscopic because slow molecular diffusion might suppress their further growth. In contrast, UUZU-2-N, which exhibits an enantiotropic N F phase at relatively high temperatures, developed progressively stronger global polar order, ultimately reaching a nearly monodomain state with a polar order parameter of . The calculated spontaneous polarization reached 6.7 μC/cm 2 , in reasonable agreement with experiment. Nematic orientational order developed rapidly, whereas long-range polar order continued to develop over several microseconds. The spontaneous development of strong polar order was also reproduced for C2-BOE. Structural analyses revealed characteristic offset configurations and head-to-tail correlations between neighboring molecules. Comparison with molecular electrostatic distributions suggests that longitudinally asymmetric and modulated charge distributions contribute to stabilizing these polar arrangements. These results provide atomistic insights into the development of collective polar order and its associated local packing in the N F liquid crystals.
papers.title: Spontaneous Ferroelectric Nematic Ordering from an Isotropic Liquid in All-Atom Molecular Dynamics Simulations

papers.abstract: Promoting diversity and inclusion for students with diverse visual abilities is crucial for advancing equity in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) education. While existing research heavily focuses on macro-level laboratory modifications and instructional accommodations, the systemic and psychological barriers faced by chemistry researchers with mild color-vision deficiency (CVD) remain largely underexplored. Guided by the Social Model of Disability, this study critically distinguishes between biological "impairment" and sociostructurally "disability" to investigate how a century-old, rigid screening tool—Ishihara's pseudoisochromatic plates—forces functional individuals into a cycle of marginalization and academic anxiety. Using a constructivist qualitative approach, we conducted semi-structured interviews with 20 CVD undergraduate and graduate chemistry students, alongside two medical professionals and three university administrators across five institutions. The thematic analysis reveals that standardized "one-size-fits-all" screening practices inflict severe institutional trauma and erode students' academic self-efficacy, triggering persistent self-doubt despite their actual functional equivalence in modern laboratories. Facing anachronistic policy regulations and extensive workplace stigmatization, participants often resort to "compulsory masking" or concealment strategies to navigate graduate admissions and career entry, occasionally resorting to legal resistance such as labor arbitration. Furthermore, collaborative learning environments exhibit an aesthetic hegemony where peers' resistance to adaptive, high-contrast designs translates into verbal microaggressions.
papers.title: From Physiological Variations to Institutional Barriers: A Qualitative Inquiry into the Academic and Professional Life Cycles of Color-Vision Deficient Chemistry Students

papers.abstract: Reaction-condition optimization requires substantial experimental time and resources, making early candidate selection important when no target-specific yield data are available. Can pretrained chemical knowledge improve the use of the initial experimental budget? We evaluate RxnScout, a locally served vision-language model agent, in a wet-lab pilot to screen a previously unoptimized substrate pair in nickel-catalyzed C-glycosylation. RxnScout reads reaction-scheme images, selects candidates for testing from a chemist-curated set of commercially procurable reagents, and updates recommendations from measured yields. Sequential screening varies one condition dimension at a time, while a chemist reviews the accompanying rationales before execution. Wet-lab comparisons showed that RxnScout reached the best catalyst yield observed during the campaign (the campaign-best catalyst yield) in fewer trials than the baselines. We discuss deployment trade-offs, limitations, and errors in the generated rationales. A high-throughput experimentation (HTE) platform has been purchased, installed, and commissioned, providing the hardware foundation for the next deployment stage.
papers.title: RxnScout: Deploying a Vision-Language Agent for Nickel-Catalyzed C-Glycosylation Condition Optimization

papers.abstract: Learning aqueous solubility remains a fundamental challenge in drug discovery, as it directly influences oral bioavailability and the selection of viable drug candidates. While data-driven approaches have achieved considerable success, conventional supervised learning models often fail to fully exploit the complementary chemical and structural information encoded within molecular representations. Beyond accurate prediction, understanding the molecular features that drive solubility is essential for developing interpretable models and guiding molecular design. In this work, we propose an additive learning framework that jointly models chemical descriptors and graph-based molecular representations while providing quantitative insights into their individual contributions to solubility prediction. The framework is evaluated on a dataset comprising over 9,000 molecules with diverse structural, chemical, and electronic properties. Graph-theoretic descriptors derived from molecular connectivity are used to capture structural characteristics associated with aqueous solubility. Our analyses reveal that the relative importance of chemical and structural descriptors shows an interesting association with molecular weight: chemical descriptors dominate the structural ones below the median molecular weight, whereas graph-theoretic descriptors become increasingly influential for heavier molecules, reflecting the growing importance of atomic connectivity in determining solubility.
papers.title: How Molecular Weight Shapes the Relative Importance of Chemical and Structural Descriptors for Aqueous Solubility

papers.abstract: The transition to green energy is causing rising demand for critical minerals and expanded mining. While mines must obtain permits from local authorities, they must also achieve a social license to operate in their communities. With this relationship in place, project delays from community 2 opposition are less likely to delay mining projects and communities are likely to be more satisfied with mining projects. Herein, we use public comments about projects in the U.S. and Chile as a data source and propose a modelling framework that combines sentiment analysis to characterize overall public attitudes with topic modelling to identify and rank the mining impacts of greatest public concern. The proposed approach facilitates standardized assessment of public sentiment about mining across multiple cultural contexts and supports more rapid responses to public feedback.
papers.title: Public comment evaluation with large language models as a window into pathways towards social license to operate for mining companies

papers.abstract: Photoinduced ligand exchange in transition-metal carbonyl complexes couples bond dissociation, coordination rearrangement, and excited-state relaxation, yet the relationship among these processes and the resulting optical response remains incompletely understood. Here, tungsten carbonyl–bipyridine complexes are investigated using density functional theory, time-dependent excited-state molecular dynamics (TDESMD), and nonadiabatic density-matrix calculations. Laser-driven TDESMD trajectories show CO dissociation together with changes in W–N coordination, including sequential formation of two W–N bonds in the bpy-coordinated complex. Fragment analysis further identifies carbonyl-loss products consistent with the evolution from to . Across representative structures containing zero, one, and two W–N bonds, the calculated final transition energies decrease, indicating substantial reorganization of the low-energy electronic states as the coordination changes. The structure, which contains two W–N bonds, additionally exhibits a low-energy absorption feature at approximately 800–850 nm in the near-infrared region (NIR). Selected molecular-orbital isosurfaces reveal substantial metal–ligand mixing, with several occupied-to-unoccupied state pairs displaying spatial distributions consistent with metal-to-ligand charge-transfer (MLCT) character. Nonadiabatic density-matrix calculations show that electron and hole relaxation rates depend on the coordination environment and produce distinct population-weighted emission profiles for the three representative complexes. Despite access to lower-energy optical transitions, the calculated photoluminescence quantum yields of the bpy-coordinated complexes remain below that of the reference. These results connect photoinduced changes in carbonyl content and W–N coordination with electronic-state reorganization, nonadiabatic relaxation, and optical response, while showing that spectral shifts toward lower energies do not necessarily lead to enhanced photoluminescence efficiency.
papers.title: Photoinduced Ligand Exchange and Photoluminescence Dynamics in Tungsten Carbonyl Complexes

papers.abstract: Aluminium chlorofluoride (ACF) is a highly Lewis-acidic amorphous material used to catalyse various organic reactions. The local structure of its catalytically active sites is not fully known. In this work, we constructed different ACF models derived from the β-AlF3 structure, and investigated, by first-principles, how different types of chloride incorporation affect the structure and induce amorphicity. We considered two different ways of incorporating chloride; direct substitution of fluoride by chloride and substitution of an AlF4 –unit by chloride. In the first approach the crystalline framework was largely preserved and only limited local distortion was observed, whereas in the second approach we observed larger structural changes and undercoordinated aluminium centres. The analysis of pair correlation functions shows that these larger defects lead to a pronounced loss of medium and long range order, while preserving the local Al–F coordination environment. These results show that atomistic models describing the structural disorder characteristic of ACF might require larger defects.
papers.title: From β-AlF3 to Amorphous Aluminium Chlorofluoride (ACF) Models: A First-Principles Study

papers.abstract: The effect of TaC additions on the oxidation behaviour of ZrB2-SiC based ultra-high-temperature ceramics, with and without AlN, was evaluated at 1600 °C in stagnant air. Three spark-plasma-sintered compositions were studied: ZSA721 (70ZrB2-20SiC-10AlN), ZSAT72-5-5 (70ZrB2-20SiC-5AlN-5TaC), and ZST631 (60ZrB2-30SiC-10TaC). After 10 h, ZSA721 gained 58 mg cm-2 and formed a 1388 ± 100 μm oxide layer. Partial replacement of AlN by TaC lowered the mass gain to 45 mg cm-2 and produced a thicker SiO2-rich surface layer, but the total oxide thickness remained comparable at 1357 ± 100 μm, while the SiC-depleted zone increased from 156 ± 12 to 240 ± 15 μm. To promote SiO2 formation further, we increased the SiC content (ZST631); however, oxidation of ZST631 resulted in the highest mass gain (69 mg cm-2), the thickest oxide layer (1477 ± 200 μm) and a discontinuous SiO2 scale. Our results, when contextualized with the research literature, indicate that TaC promotes cooperative degradation, potentially through porosity created by gas-evolution and restricted lateral spreading and healing of the Ta-containing borosilicate glass, thereby hindering the oxidation resistance.
papers.title: Effect of TaC additions on the oxidation behaviour of ZrB2-SiC-AlN ultra-high temperature ceramics at 1600 °C

papers.abstract: We report CeO2 as an additive for tuning oxidation behaviour of ZrB2-SiC ultra-high temperature ceramics (UHTCs). Four compositions were compared: AlN-only, AlN-CeO2 co-doped, and two CeO2-only compositions with different SiC contents. Samples consolidated by spark plasma sintering (96-99% density) were oxidised in stagnant air at 1600 °C for up to 10 h. Ce-bearing compositions consistently outperformed the AlN-only reference. The co-doped sample showed the greatest improvement: mass gain reduced from 58 to 40 mg cm-2, oxide thickness from 1388 to 550 μm, and the SiO2-rich surface layer increased from ~5 to 82 μm. EDS-PhaSe analysis identified significant ZrSiO4 formation across Ce-containing samples. CeO2 appears to operate at two scales: enhancing borosilicate melt spreading to form a continuous surface barrier and promoting subsurface ZrSiO4 formation. CeO2, particularly combined with AlN, represents a promising strategy for improving oxidation resistance in ZrB2-SiC UHTCs.
papers.title: CeO2 as a novel additive for enhancing the oxidation resistance of ZrB2–SiC ultra-high temperature ceramics: role of Ce-mediated ZrSiO4 formation

papers.abstract: Ethyl acetate (EtOAc) is a staple solvent across the chemical industry, owing to its favourable combination of high volatility, moderate polarity, and low toxicity. These properties make it a versatile solvent capable of dissolving a broad range of organic compounds while also allowing for its rapid and efficient removal by evaporation. To obtain insights into the molecular arrangements behind EtOAc macroscopic properties, here we measure the structure of liquid EtOAc using total neutron and x-ray scattering. The first solvation shell is dominated by strong local structuring via weak C-H to carbonyloxygen hydrogen bonding which directs two adjacent EtOAc molecules into dimers. The proclivity towards forming dimers occludes the carbonyl oxygens, preventing the formation of longer-range ordering, with negligible structure in the second solvation shell underpinning its high volatility. Our work emphasises the relationship between local molecular structuring and liquids macroscopic behaviour, towards the engineering of formulations with targeted properties.
papers.title: The Liquid Structure of Ethyl Acetate and the Origin of Its Volatility

papers.abstract: Thermopower is a key parameter for assessing the thermoelectric performance of conducting polymers and probing their charge transport mechanisms. Although pronounced thermopower anisotropy has been observed in aligned polymer films, its microscopic origin remains incompletely understood. Here, combining tight-binding modeling, first-principles calculations, and Boltzmann transport theory, we identify doping-induced electronic dimensional crossover as an intrinsic mechanism underlying this anisotropy.
