As hole doping increases, the Fermi surface evolves from closed three-dimensional pockets to configurations with quasi-two-dimensional and ultimately quasi-one-dimensional character, without requiring structural changes. These changes in Fermi-surface topology reshape the energy dependence of the directional transport distribution functions, producing pronounced thermopower anisotropy and direction-dependent sign reversals. We further show that this anisotropy can contribute substantially to the Nernst response of aligned conducting polymers. These findings establish a microscopic connection between band filling, Fermi-surface topology, and anisotropic thermoelectric transport.
papers.title: Doping-Induced Electronic Dimensional Crossover and Anisotropic Thermopower in Conducting Polymers

papers.abstract: Top-down proteomics (TDP) data analysis methods are continually evolving to extract increasingly comprehensive information from the highly complex datasets. However, researchers often need to coordinate multiple processing tools, write custom scripts, and rely on expert knowledge to fully interpret experimental results. To streamline the workflows and lower technical barriers, we present TDEaseNexus, an open-source desktop platform that unifies workflow execution, proteoform characterization, and interactive visualization through a natural-language AI agent. Through its AI-native interface and modular structure, researchers can execute adaptable TDP pipelines and perform label-free quantification, post-translational modification characterization, and positional-isomer quantification by stating their analytical goals. Domain-specific Skills and a Rust-based mass spectrometry toolkit provide deterministic calculations for modification searches, precursor-mass calibration, and spectral evidence analysis. The resulting analytical outputs can be inspected through interactive visualizations, while all analysis steps are automatically recorded for data provenance. As an open-source platform distributed with its complete analytical stack (https://github.com/Computational-TDMS/TDEaseNexus), TDEaseNexus facilitates routine TDP data interpretation and record-keeping, with the potential to broaden access to the development of new computational TDP methods.
papers.title: TDEaseNexus: A Traceable, Open-Source AI Agent Platform for Top-Down Proteomics Data Analysis

papers.abstract: Sugar-fatty acid esters were synthesized by incorporating linear saturated fatty acids (C10–C22) into C-1-oxidized maltose (maltobionic acid, 4-O-α-D-glucopyranosyl-D-gluconic acid) via ester linkages. Esterification of C-1-oxidized sugars often triggers β-elimination, yielding C-2/C-3 unsaturated derivatives deoxygenated at C-3. In this study, various reaction conditions were investigated to minimize this βelimination. The resulting fully esterified product, maltobionolactone perpalmitate, gelled various oils at concentrations as low as 3 wt% and substantially enhanced collagen production in human dermal fibroblasts. Furthermore, linear saturated fatty acids were introduced into C-1-oxidized dextrin derivatives. Gelation tests revealed that controlling the degree of fatty acid substitution is critical for optimizing gelling performance. The resulting organogels exhibited superior emulsion and thermal stability compared to dextrin palmitate, a commercial organogelator.
papers.title: Design, dual gelation mechanisms, and bioactive properties of fatty acid esters derived from C-1-oxidized maltose and dextrin

papers.abstract: Functionalized carbazoles are versatile organic building blocks that play pivotal roles in diverse applications, particularly in charge-transfer complexes, hole-transport materials, and interfacial modifiers. In this study, we synthesized 1,8-functionalized carbazole derivatives ( C1 - C5 ) with various aryl substituents that provided extended conjugation via Mizoroki-Heck coupling reaction using our previously developed phosphine ligand-based Pd catalysis. Among them, the di(1-vinylpyrene) derivative ( C4 ) exhibited a unique molecular conformation in which one pyrene unit is nearly coplanar with the carbazole. At the same time, the other is twisted by about 49°, resulting in a bidirectional π-stacking arrangement, as revealed by its single crystal structure. Photophysical, electrochemical, and computational studies collectively supported the influence of aryl substitution on the electronic nature of carbazole by tuning the HOMO-LUMO energy gap. AFM analysis showed that C4 self-assembled into spherical aggregates. In contrast, in the presence of naphthalenediimide ( NDI8 ), it formed a donor-acceptor charge-transfer complex (1:2 ratio) that further self-assembled into a highly ordered, micrometer-long fibrillar structure. This long-range structural uniformity offers promising architectures for emerging applications of organic functional materials.
papers.title: Donor-Acceptor co-assembly of twisted 1,8-difunctionalized carbazole and naphthalenediimide

papers.abstract: Metal-organic framework (MOF) glasses and glass-like materials offer unique advantages including improved flexibility, processability and mechanical stability, yet the rational, mild and scalable synthesis of uniform, large-area glassy MOF thin films remains largely unexplored and highly challenging. Herein, we pioneer the fabrication of homogeneous, ultra-smooth glass-like MOF thin films, which can be readily scaled into large-area coatings via a facile room-temperature immersion strategy. By simply placing diverse substrates into the precursor solution for 0.5 to 3 hours, continuous amorphous MOF films with nanometer-scale flatness and centimeter-to-0.3-meter scale uniformity can be readily prepared, with exceptional mechanical properties including Young’s modulus among the highest reported for typical ZIF glasses. Importantly, this unprecedented glass-like MOF film serves as a versatile guiding layer that enables the nucleation and growth of 15 different types of crystalline MOFs on various substrates, overcoming long-standing limitations of substrate dependence and lattice mismatch. This work not only establishes a facile and scalable synthetic platform for high-performance glass-like MOF thin films, but also extends its capability toward the universal growth of crystalline MOF films, unlocking promising new opportunities for device-oriented MOF thin-film materials for gas and isotope separation, electronic devices, sensing and electrocatalytic applications.
papers.title: Scalable Room-Temperature Synthesis of Glass-like MOF Thin Films on Arbitrary Substrates with Versatile Functionality

papers.abstract: The cell membrane is a highly dynamic biological interface that maintains cellular integrity and mediates critical physiological processes. Owing to its outermost location and involvement in disease onset and progression, the cell membrane has emerged as a prominent therapeutic target. Luminogens with aggregation-induced emission (AIE) characteristics are uniquely suited for cell membrane-targeting bioimaging and therapy. This review makes an across-the-board summary of advanced research in cell membrane-targeting AIEgens from ingenious molecular design to dazzling applications in living system. The targeting principles are systematically classified and illustrated into four main categories. Subsequently, advanced bioimaging applications are highlighted, ranging from the precise discrimination of cancer cells and spatiotemporal imaging of the nervous system to the dynamic monitoring of membrane physiological processes. Furthermore, cell membrane-targeted phototherapy in cancer treatment is discussed, emphasizing its unique ability to bypass multidrug resistance, induce immunogenic cell death, and activate systemic antitumor immunity. Finally, the current challenges and future perspectives are outlined, emphasizing precision material engineering, multimodal theranostics, and the immense potential of these AIEgens in advanced optical imaging, brain science, and clinical translation.
papers.title: Sternstunden der Materialien: Cell membrane targeting AIEgens for bioimaging and therapy

papers.abstract: Organic linker design for reticular materials requires balancing molecular diversity with structural and chemical constraints. Here, we introduce LinkerGen, a compact SMILES-based autoregressive model guided by chemical building unit (CBU) types, numerical property targets, or text descriptions. We train and evaluate two model sizes on approximately 22 million fragment-enumerated carboxylate linkers spanning 2-linear, 2-bent, and 3-planar CBU types. Model size and sampling temperature adjust the balance between validity and novelty, while conditioning increases the yield of distinct, valid, novel candidates satisfying selected requests compared with unconditioned generation followed by filtering. Text conditioning combines molecular requirements in a single natural-language request, although its effectiveness depends on training coverage and prompt formulation. A prospective application connects literature-informed linker generation to metal–organic polyhedron (MOP) assembly and calculated binding energies for 5-fluorouracil, illustrating how chemical design hypotheses can be explored through computational screening. LinkerGen provides a steerable source of candidate building units and a basis for adaptation to other linker families and design objectives through suitable training data and conditioning information. Highlights • Generative model for reticular organic chemical building units (CBUs) widen the chemical linker space available for the design of metal-organic polyhedra. • Conditioning enriches generated populations in linkers with desired properties. • Text conditioning allows complex chemical requirements to be effectively expressed in natural language.
papers.title: LinkerGen: Guided Autoregressive Generation of Organic Linkers for Reticular Chemistry

papers.abstract: The dataset, sourced from the UCI repository, underscores the value of open-source resources in advancing sensor research. In this study, raw sensor data were compressed using polynomial fitting (polyfit), achieving nearly a 100-fold reduction, and subsequently analyzed with the Isolation Forest algorithm to detect anomalies. Python libraries, including scikit-learn, were deployed in an isolated environment to ensure reproducibility and scalability. The workflow was further integrated into Microsoft Copilot, enabling natural language interaction with the AI agent for streamlined big data modeling.
papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Model Implementation for UC Irvine Dataset 322

papers.abstract: Predicting reaction feasibility is essential to organic synthesis, yet models trained on literature records often fail to generalize to laboratory data. Here, we present a two-stage distillation and adaptation framework that transfers reactivity knowledge from large, noisy literature datasets to small, controlled high-throughput experimentation (HTE) datasets, and further leverages this transferable knowledge to enable uncertainty-guided active learning. Literature reactions are curated and augmented with chemical reasoning to post-train reaction-specific language models through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL), producing a compact generalist model. In zero-shot evaluation across Suzuki–Miyaura coupling, Buchwald–Hartwig amination and acid–amine condensation, the generalist model outperforms the strongest baseline by 41.5% in mean accuracy and 29.2% in macro-F1, while surpassing human expert accuracy by 8.9% and macro-F1 by 11.5%. To accelerate active exploration, generalist predictions are transferred into warm priors for Bayesian neural networks. This warm prior reduces the experimental labels needed to reach a held-out macro-F1 ≥ 0.70 by 25.0–42.9% relative to a vanilla Bayesian neural network (BNN). Furthermore, uncertainty-guided acquisition prioritizes informative reactions, enabling the models to approach full-pool training performance using only about oneeighth of the total available reactions. To our knowledge, this work establishes the first experimentally validated literature-to-laboratory paradigm connecting 1 large-scale post-trained language models with active experimental design, providing a practical foundation for data-efficient, privacy-preserving, and autonomous chemical discovery.
papers.title: Bridging the Literature-to-Laboratory Gap with Language Models and Active Learning for Reaction Feasibility Prediction and Autonomous Exploration

papers.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) deliver nucleic acids, yet how the ionizable lipid, phospholipid, and cholesterol organise the membrane at the molecular level remains unclear. Here, we performed atomistic molecular dynamics simulations of flat bilayers of the ionizable lipid cis-ssPalmO-phe (50 mol%) with one of four phospholipids (DSPC, DSPE, DOPC, DOPE) and cholesterol at 40 mol% phospholipid and 40 mol% cholesterol, with the binding free energy of cholesterol calculated using umbrella sampling. In the cholesterol-rich systems, all four bilayers were thicker (from 4.37–5.12 to 5.14–5.80 nm) and more tightly packed (from 2.02–2.27 to 2.60–2.86 lipids nm−2) as compared to the phospholipid-rich system. Also, in cholesterol-rich systems, lateral diffusion was 30 to 40% lower; cholesterol stood more upright. Cholesterol tilt and acyl-chain order became more alike across the four phospholipids, and the spread in the binding free energy of cholesterol narrowed (about 9 to 5 kcal mol−1) while its mean rose only modestly (about 13 to 16 kcal mol−1). Total cholesterol–cis-ssPalmO-phe (IL)interaction energies and hydrogen-bond counts rose roughly three-to seven-fold, in step with cholesterol number. Because the ionizable lipid (IL) fraction was fixed, more cholesterol means less phospholipid, so these effects reflect composition and cannot be assigned to cholesterol alone. Head-group chemistry set the sign of the electrostatic potential, whereas diffusion fell in every system regardless of acyl-chain saturation. These results give a molecular
papers.title: Cholesterol Condensation and Phospholipid Convergence in cis-ssPalmO-phe Bilayers: A Molecular Dynamics Study

papers.abstract: Reliable interpretation of Raman spectra from breast tissue requires evaluation on patients absent from model training. We reanalysed a public ex vivo dataset comprising 641 spectra, 80 tissue samples and 71 donors to assess the effect of validation design on breast cancer classification. In a GNU Octave reproduction of the deposited analysis, an indexing statement caused an average of 56% of testfold spectra also to be selected for training. With the original and corrected indexing operations, four-class support-vector-machine accuracy was 87.6% and 59.1%, respectively; the reproduction used an approximate kernel-scale setting rather than the original MATLAB heuristic. Under donor-disjoint nested validation, five classifiers achieved 55–60% four-class accuracy, with invasive lobular carcinoma sensitivity of only 6–15%. Cancer-versus-normal classification remained more robust (support vector machine accuracy 90.0%; donor-bootstrap 95% confidence interval 83.8–95.3%). A fixed-pipeline analysis gave four-class accuracies of 81.7%, 77.9%, 60.9% and 62.1% when folds were formed at the spectrum, measurement-point, sample and donor levels, respectively. A bandresolved variance decomposition indicated that donor identity accounted for the largest share of within-class variance at the carotenoid bands (1157 and 1525 cm-1; 58–63%), whereas class information was concentrated at the phenylalanine band (1004 cm-1). Donor-level band ratios differed between cancer and normal tissue but not between DCIS and invasive lobular carcinoma. Adding the highwavenumber region, varying preprocessing, or increasing the number of lobular carcinoma training donors from about 2 to 8 did not raise lobular carcinoma sensitivity above 25%. In a simulation of the measurement chain with real fluorescence backgrounds and Poisson shot noise, donor-shared backgrounds and collection gains produced little optimism after preprocessing, whereas donor-specific tissue chemistry did. Donor-separated conformal calibration yielded 91.0% empirical marginal coverage for the four-class task at a nominal 90% target, but coverage was lower for invasive subtypes; class-conditional calibration equalised coverage across classes but returned large prediction sets. These findings identify substantial validation sensitivity in this dataset and underline the need for patient-level evaluation, reproducible code and classspecific uncertainty reporting.
papers.title: Patient-Level Reassessment of Breast Raman Spectroscopy: Data Leakage and Limits of Subtype Classification

papers.abstract: We report the synthesis of a nucleotide diphosphate 4-amino sugar and its late-stage, chemoselective formylation to the corresponding formamide under conditions compatible with highly polar and sensitive, diphosphate substrates. Uridine diphosphate-4-deoxy-4-amino-α-L-arabinose (UDP-Ara4N) was prepared via a convergent phosphate coupling strategy. Selective Nformylation was achieved with formyl–pivalic mixed anhydride under Schotten–Baumann conditions, providing UDP-4-deoxy-4formamido-α-L-arabinose (UDP-Ara4FN, 72%). These results demonstrate that despite the presence of multiple nucleophilic functionalities, chemoselective amine functionalization can be achieved on fully deprotected NDP amino sugars, providing a practical approach to accessing functionalized nucleotide sugar analogues.
papers.title: Chemoselective Formylation of an Amine-Functionalized Nucleotide Diphosphate Sugar under Diphosphate-Compatible Conditions

papers.abstract: External control over click chemistry offers opportunities for the spatiotemporal regulation of bioorthogonal ligation and cleavage, but the limited tissue penetration of light constrains photoactivated approaches. Herein, we introduce a new mechanistic approach to ultrasound-controlled click chemistry based on the direct sonochemical oxidation of dihydrotetrazine (DHTz) precursors. The precursors require no additional cleavable masking group, and low-intensity therapeutic ultrasound activates their oxidation through sonochemically generated hydroxyl radicals without the need for added sensitizers. A pyridinyl-substituted precursor, DHTz2, exhibits limited background oxidation and efficient sonochemical activation, while the resulting tetrazine product shows good stability under ultrasound exposure. The ultrasound-activated tetrazine readily undergoes ligation reactions with TCOs, including a TCO-DOX conjugate in which a bioorthogonal click-to-release cascade releases free DOX and restores its cytotoxic activity against cancer cells. Importantly, ultrasound applied through a chicken breast tissue barrier remains effective in triggering bioorthogonal click-to-release and activating the prodrug. This work establishes a new mechanistic approach that couples the fundamental sonochemistry of acoustic cavitation with the selective activation of click chemistry and bioorthogonal cleavage, providing a new platform for the remote, non-optical control of bioorthogonal ligation and cargo release using tissue-penetrating biomedical ultrasound.
papers.title: Ultrasound-Controlled Activation of Tetrazine-TCO Click-to-release Chemistry Through Sonochemical Oxidation of Dihydrotetrazine

papers.abstract: Hydrogen molybdenum bronzes (H x MoO 3 ) are mixed-valence transition metal oxides whose structural and electronic properties are strongly influenced by their proton behavior. Despite their extensive study under ambient conditions, their structural evolution under compression remains largely unexplored. Here, we report the high-pressure structural behavior of three hydrogen molybdenum bronzes using synchrotron-based powder X-ray and neutron diffraction. Pressure induces structural phase transitions in all three compounds, yet each materials’ evolution is distinct, suggesting a coupling between hydrogen location/concentration and framework stress response. The bronze with the lowest reduction and proton incorporation level ( x ~ 0.36, Type I) exhibits a compression pathway similar to that of α -MoO 3 , whereas at higher hydrogenation levels ( x ~ 0.95, Type II; x ~ 1.68, Type III), distinct pressure-dependent changes in bulk modulus reveal altered elastic response during compression. Complementary in situ neutron diffraction measurements on D 0.36 MoO3 directly locate the hydrogen atom at an equatorial oxygen. Upon compression to 7.8 ± 1.5 GPa, the local hydrogen environment becomes increasingly constrained, exhibiting significant deviation of the O–D···O angle from 180° and shortening of the D···O distance by ca. 0.3 Å. These results establish the structural response of hydrogen molybdenum bronzes to high pressure and demonstrate how proton incorporation governs framework distortions and compressibility.
papers.title: Lattice Evolution and Proton Positioning in Hydrogen Molybdenum Bronzes under Pressure

papers.abstract: The conversion of carbon dioxide into useful or environmentally benign chemicals is currently of great interest to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Yet in spite of numerous efforts effective CO2 conversion still presents a considerable challenge. One of the most promising catalysts for CO2 conversion to hydrocarbons is copper. In this computational study based on density functional theory we have addressed bimetallic PbCu catalysts to elucidate whether there are synergistic catalytic effects through the alloying of Cu with Pb, as suggested experimentally. Using a well-established descriptor for the catalytic activity based on hydrogen and CO adsorption energies, we analyzed the potential catalytic activity of PbCu surface alloys on copper. The computational results confirm that through a combination of strain and ligand effects these surface alloys can act as favorable catalysts for valuable hydrocarbons.
papers.title: Examining Copper Lead Surface Alloys as Potential Catalysts for the Electrochemical Carbon Dioxide Reduction

papers.abstract: Carbon-black-filled nitrile butadiene rubber (NBR) exhibits two maxima in its nonlinear oscillatory response, quantified here by a Fourier-based Nonlinearity Index (NLI). The higher-strain Peak I is inherited from the neat long-chain-branched matrix, whereas the lower-strain Peak II appears only after filler addition and is markedly more sensitive to carbon-black grade. We use a molecular description that separates the intrinsic dynamics of the matrix from those of the dynamically active boundrubber population. Peak I arises from the competition between backbone orientation and delayed arm retraction; matrix–adsorbed constraints shift this maximum to lower imposed strain and attenuate its amplitude without requiring a change in the underlying arm-retraction mechanism. Peak II is assigned to collective memory carried by adsorbed polymer associated with neighboring aggregate environments. Two limiting mechanisms for the loss of this interfacial memory—controlled by local shear rate or by interfacial deformation—predict distinct frequency dependences but are indistinguishable from the available single-frequency measurements. This picture connects the two nonlinear maxima to different molecular populations and suggests direct multi-frequency tests for separating matrix and interfacial contributions in filled NBR.
papers.title: Unraveling Two Nonlinear Rheological Peaks in Filled Rubber: Chain-Arm Retraction and Bound-Rubber Dynamics

papers.abstract: The spin evolution dynamics of the correlated triplet pair (TT) decide the fate of the number of triplet (T1) excitons after photoexcitation in singlet fission (SF) materials, yet accurately resolving its relaxation pathways remains elusive. In this work, we systematically elucidate the spin dynamics of intramolecular SF in covalently linked TIPS-pentacene dimers with different inter-triplet exchange coupling (J) values and their dynamic fluctuations by externally perturbing the total spin Hamiltonian via the solventmediated external heavy-atom effect and the magnetic field effect. Based on transient absorption spectroscopy, we quantitatively demonstrate that the responsiveness to both perturbations is strictly governed by the J regime. While certain geometries facilitate or suppress spin mixing across spin manifolds depending on the J values, non-planar conformations eventually open an irreversible 3TT → T1 kinetic sink, channeling the initial population into a single T1 rather than two uncorrelated triplets (T1 + T1). Our findings reveal the mechanistic origins of spin-state dissipation, establishing a molecular framework for precisely steering spin evolution in exciton-multiplying architectures.
papers.title: Multifaceted Control of Triplet-Pair Spin Dynamics in Intramolecular Singlet Fission at Room Temperature

papers.abstract: Organic active waveguides are emerging as multifunctional photonic materials capable of simultaneously transmitting light and regulating optical signals through wavelength conversion and emission modulation. However, most reported systems rely on high-quality single crystals, doped matrices, or complex fabrication procedures, limiting their scalability and practical implementation. Here, we report a simple copolymerization strategy that introduces efficient clusteroluminescence into poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET)-derived copolyesters, thereby enabling active optical waveguiding in an intrinsically emissive, single-component polymer system. The excitation-dependent emission of the resulting copolyester gives rise to pronounced propagation-distance-dependent spectral evolution. During propagation, wavelength-selective attenuation and reabsorption progressively enrich the long-wavelength fluorescence component, producing emission-peak shift of up to 125 nm over 65 mm. The copolyesters are amenable to scalable synthesis and melt processing, which retain active optical waveguiding in flexible, thick, and geometrically irregular filaments. This work establishes clusteroluminescent PET-derived copolyesters as a scalable platform for active polymer photonics, with potential applications in optical encoding, visual information transmission, and flexible photonic devices.
papers.title: Clusteroluminescence-enabled active optical waveguiding in polyesters

papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer a distinctive capability for chemical problem solving by integrating chemical knowledge and experimental evidence through reasoning expressed in language. Yet how chemical evidence reshapes their predictions and expressed rationales is not self-evident and has received limited examination, particularly for challenging chemical problems. Here, using nucleoside-derived supramolecular gelation as a testbed, we systematically varied the evidence provided to LLMs and quantitatively evaluated their predictions and the mechanistic alignment of generated rationales. Without additional evidence, correct predictions were associated with greater alignment to literature-supported mechanisms than incorrect ones, suggesting that LLMs can draw on intrinsic chemical knowledge despite rationales remain largely general. Structurally similar gelation precedents, thought improved prediction accuracy significantly, reduced this distinction by anchoring rationales to insufficiently discriminative structural features, indicating that similarity-based evidence does not necessarily improve chemical reasoning and that prediction accuracy alone is insufficient to assess LLM performance in chemical tasks. In contrast, condition-constrained references and mechanistic information more consistently directed rationales toward chemically discriminative features, even when prediction accuracy did not improve in tandem. Together, our study highlights the importance of task-specific evidence design and quantitative rationale evaluation for reliable chemical problem solving by LLMs.
papers.title: How Chemical Evidence Shapes Mechanistic Reasoning and Prediction by Large Language Models: Fine-Grained Inference in Nucleoside-Derived Supramolecular Gelation

papers.abstract: We present an autonomous machine-learning model, Conan-MLII, for fast, reproducible contact-angle measurement. The model was trained on >32 million synthetic images generated from Young–Laplace solutions spanning θ = 20◦–180◦, including the effects of gravity, multiple image scales and surface perturbations (roughness, reflection) as well as including sampling offsets to provide contact-point invariance. An improved contact-point identification (CPID) routine is integrated to enable autonomous processing of real images. The model produced results comparable to Young–Laplace (mean systematic underprediction ∼ 2◦) when tested on 172 experimental images drawn from multiple groups, and was much better at predicting asymmetric and low-angle cases where Young-Laplace fitting commonly misconverges. The total analysis time per image for the machine learning approach was three times faster than Young-Laplace fitting, the current best-practice approach. The model is extended to measurement of advancing and receding contact angles, showing excellent agreement with commercial tensiometers over the range 30◦ − 160◦. The model is provided as open-source for use and further development of contact angle measurement.
papers.title: Automated Static and Dynamic Contact-Angle Analysis with Machine Learning

papers.abstract: We develop a method that uses the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to efficiently calculate changes in the solvent accessible surface area (SASA) at many relative translations of two binding partners. For each binding partner, the buried surface area (BSA) is computed using the cross-correlation of a grid-based discretization of its SASA and of a solvent exclusion grid from its binding partner. This approach improves the tractability of exhaustive interface burial calculations by reducing computational complexity, making it particularly valuable for analyzing large biomolecular systems. We implemented an optimized library for Shrake-Rupley SASA by modifying sasa.cpp from MDTraj. Our approach reduces the cost of evaluating BSA at all translations within a rotation from to . One FFT pass costs 0.41–0.68 µs per translation against 0.14–1.70 s per pose for the direct calculation, a speedup of to that appears to grow with system size. Agreement with the direct calculation is close, with a root mean square error of 3.0 Å at 0.5 Å grid resolution. Possible applications of the method include virtual screening, models of biomacromolecular assemblies and aggregates, studies of protein diffusion, and thermodynamic analysis of large conformational ensembles.
papers.title: Fourier Transform Method for Surface Area Burial

papers.abstract: Stochastic autoencoders (SAEs), which omit the Kullback–Leibler prior-matching term of variational autoencoders and are therefore suited to reconstruction rather than generative sampling, offer a nonlinear route to reducing the dimensionality of molecular ensembles, but their behavior across systems of differing size and flexibility is poorly characterized. Training SAEs on molecular dynamics trajectories of oxycodone, deca-alanine, crambin, a bromodomain–JQ1 complex, and HIV-1 protease, we find that reconstruction error plateaus at a system- and model-dependent latent dimensionality, that the effects of dropout and batch normalization are system-specific, and that SAEs yield more distinct clusters than principal component analysis (PCA) at very low dimensionality and reconstruct large data sets more accurately than the deterministic autoencoder CompressTraj at low dimensionality. With two to four latent variables, SAE reconstructions of crambin and HIV-1 protease are as accurate as PCA with 6–18 components, two latent variables span their leading principal subspace as well as 9–15 components, and a single SAE coordinate recovers the end-to-end distance of deca-alanine (R2 = 0.97, versus 0.04 for the first principal component), whereas PCA is more accurate at higher dimensionality and for the near-rigid bromodomain ensemble. Latent-space perturbations show that SAE latent variables encode nonlinear, position-dependent collective motions that vary across the learned manifold.
papers.title: Evaluating the Dimensionality of Molecular Ensembles Using Deep Neural Network Stochastic Autoencoders

papers.abstract: The photochemical behaviour of azobenzene photoswitches is strongly influenced by molecular structure and the surrounding chemical environment, while supramolecular interactions offer an additional means of modulating their switching response. We report the synthesis and photoswitching behaviour of chiral azobenzene derivatives incorporating a BINOL framework and thiourea hydrogen-bonding groups. The thiourea-containing photoswitch 1 undergoes reversible E→Z and Z→E photoisomerization while retaining its chiroptical response. Concentration-dependent NMR and DLS studies indicate self-association of 1, particularly in CDCl3, accompanied by a pronounced retardation of E→Z photoisomerization. Comparison with the thiourea-free analogue 8 suggests that, in addition to general concentration effects, thiourea-mediated interactions contribute to this behaviour. Addition of chloride leads to changes in the thiourea N–H resonances and increases the Zisomer content at the photostationary state from approximately 50% to 70%. Although the effect on the apparent E→Z half-life is modest, chloride binding also increases the thermal lifetime of the Z-isomer. These results show that thiourea-based association and guest binding influence the photochemical and thermal behaviour of the chiral azobenzene system.
papers.title: Supramolecular Control of Photoswitching in a Chiral Azobenzene

papers.abstract: Pressure-temperature vapor-liquid equilibrium (PT-VLE) flash calculations are performed repeatedly in compositional-flow simulations and can dominate runtime. To reduce this cost, we propose three thermodynamically informed GibbsFlashNN models that directly predict phase state, compositions, and vapor fraction. A common allocation decoder algebraically enforces nonnegativity, composition normalization, and component-wise material balance. Training incorporates differentiable conditions derived from phase equilibrium and constrained Gibbs-free-energy minimization, supplied by a fixed equation of state or activity-coefficient model, or by a neural thermodynamic potential trained jointly with the flash network or independently pretrained and frozen. Evaluation spans eleven studies involving petroleum fluids, CO2-containing mixtures, nonideal organic and aqueous systems, and a five-component mixture. Across 3,090 held-out experimental composition values from nine systems, the proposed models achieve pooled major-component mean absolute percentage errors of 6.63–7.63%, compared with 6.62% for classical flashes using equations of state or activity-coefficient models and 8.01% for a supervised balance-preserving baseline with the same architecture. Relative to this neural baseline, the proposed models also reduce the pooled 95th-percentile absolute percentage error from 30.3% to 25.8–29.6%. Across the benchmark cases, median end-to-end inference speed-ups over the corresponding classical flashes range from 5.2 to 241.7 times, including confidence screening and reference fallback. These results support incorporating thermodynamic conditions into neural flash training to reduce aggregate prediction errors while approaching classical-flash accuracy at substantially lower inference cost.
papers.title: Thermodynamically informed and balance-preserving neural networks for direct vapor–liquid flash calculations

papers.abstract: Pressure-temperature vapor-liquid equilibrium (PT-VLE) flash calculations are performed repeatedly in compositional-flow simulations and can dominate runtime. To reduce this cost, we propose three thermodynamically informed GibbsFlashNN models that directly predict phase state, compositions, and vapor fraction. A common allocation decoder algebraically enforces nonnegativity, composition normalization, and component-wise material balance. Training incorporates differentiable conditions derived from phase equilibrium and constrained Gibbs-free-energy minimization, supplied by a fixed equation of state or activity-coefficient model, or by a neural thermodynamic potential trained jointly with the flash network or independently pretrained and frozen. Evaluation spans eleven studies involving petroleum fluids, CO2-containing mixtures, nonideal organic and aqueous systems, and a five-component mixture. Across 3,090 held-out experimental composition values from nine systems, the proposed models achieve pooled major-component mean absolute percentage errors of 6.63–7.63%, compared with 6.62% for classical flashes using equations of state or activity-coefficient models and 8.01% for a supervised balance-preserving baseline with the same architecture. Relative to this neural baseline, the proposed models also reduce the pooled 95th-percentile absolute percentage error from 30.3% to 25.8–29.6%. Across the benchmark cases, median end-to-end inference speed-ups over the corresponding classical flashes range from 5.2 to 241.7 times, including confidence screening and reference fallback. These results support incorporating thermodynamic conditions into neural flash training to reduce aggregate prediction errors while approaching classical-flash accuracy at substantially lower inference cost.
papers.title: Thermodynamically informed and balance-preserving neural networks for direct vapor–liquid flash calculations

papers.abstract: The formation of C–CF3 bonds is an important challenge in organofluorine chemistry. Understanding the factors governing this process is key to develop new synthetic strategies. Here, we report ligand-enabled C–CF3 coupling at tetracoordinate Au(III) centres supported by hemilabile P^N ligands. A series of well-defined Au(III) trifluoromethyl complexes bearing aryl, vinyl or alkynyl groups were prepared and shown to undergo thermal reductive elimination, affording the corresponding C–CF3 coupling products in high yields (86% on average of 17 examples). The reaction accommodates sterically hindered aryl groups and functional groups. Kinetic experiments support a first-order process, while density functional theory calculations identify a concerted reductive elimination pathway involving a three-centre transition state. The calculations further highlight the role of the hemilabile nitrogen donor, which partially dissociates during C–CF3 bond formation. The coupling also extends to a related perfluoroethyl Au(III) complex, demonstrating the potential to forge C–C2F5 bonds. Together, these findings establish P^N-chelated Au(III) complexes as a platform for studying and promoting C–CF3 bond formation, providing mechanistic insight into reductive elimination at gold and a basis for exploring new ligand-enabled transformations.
papers.title: Ligand-Enabled C–CF3 coupling at tetracoordinated Au(III)

papers.abstract: Active learning ideally needs informative and inexpensive features that provide reliable uncertainty estimates. General interaction properties function (GIPF) descriptors, which encode molecular surface electrostatic potential, are informative but usually computed by density functional approximations on individual structures, which is not only costly but also neglects conformational flexibility. In this work, we compute GIPF descriptors efficiently based on force-field point charges over conformer ensembles via an automated pipeline starting from SMILES strings. We benchmark our approach against inexpensive cheminformatics descriptors on three experimental datasets, covering surfactants, peptide catalysts, and supramolecular assemblies. We evaluate prediction accuracy, screening efficiency, and uncertainty calibration. Our results demonstrate that force-field-based GIPF descriptors are complementary to cheminformatics descriptors and lead to better predictions. Additionally, we find that ensemble-based GIPF descriptors improve uncertainty calibration significantly. Accordingly, we recommend force-field-based GIPF descriptors, evaluated over inexpensive conformer ensembles, as affordable and scalable featurization method for active learning campaigns in chemistry.
papers.title: Ensemble Molecular Surface Electrostatic Potential Descriptors as Informative Features for Active Learning

papers.abstract: Human 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A reductase (HMGCR) recognizes statins through a conserved polar binding region, while peripheral chemical differences may alter protein–ligand dynamics. We docked 13 chemically defined statin-related molecular states across six ligand-bound HMGCR crystal structures using three independent searches per state–receptor combination (234 searches). Eight selected states were then evaluated in three independently seeded 50 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations each (24 trajectories; 1.2 μs total). Protein-aligned root-mean-square displacement (RMSD) was analyzed for the entire ligand, a conserved nine-heavy-atom hydroxy-acid motif, and the complementary peripheral atoms, together with residue-level contacts. Top-ranked motif-compatible pose recovery varied between receptor structures, from 15/39 searches for 1HW8 to 38/39 for 1HWK. The G3-001 stereoisomers differed substantially in the persistence of geometric hydrogen-bond criteria involving HMGCR Glu559: median replica occupancies were 8.2% for G3-001 A (R) and 91.0% for G3-001 B (S), with higher occupancy for B in each of the three paired replica comparisons. A separate ether-chain extension (G3-005) exhibited pronounced peripheral displacement in one replica while selected recognition-site proximities remained. These computational observations identify testable relationships among receptor conformation, ligand stereochemistry, and interaction persistence.
papers.title: Conserved recognition and divergent peripheral dynamics of designed statin analogues at human HMG-CoA reductase: ensemble docking and replicated molecular dynamics

papers.abstract: Hydrometallation of polarized alkynes is a powerful technique to access regio- and stereocontrolled vinyl-metal intermediates. The pentafluorosulfanyl (SF 5 ) group, often called "super-CF 3 ", offers a promising, non-PFAS alternative to CF 3 chemistry, combining enhanced electron-withdrawing properties with remarkable stability. While hydrofunctionalization of SF 5 -alkynes has so far been limited to the β-carbon, we report the first regioselective hydrometallation at the α-carbon of SF 5 -alkynes. Palladium- and platinum-catalyzed hydrosilylation, hydrostannylation, and hydrogermylation with Group 14 metalloids delivered α-vinylsilanes, α-vinylstannanes, and α-vinylgermanes in moderate to excellent yields with high regio- and stereoselectivity, outperforming CF 3 -alkynes, whose weaker polarization accounts for their lower selectivity.
papers.title: Regio- and Stereoselective Transition Metal-Catalyzed Hydrometallation of SF <sub>5</sub> -alkynes with Group 14 Metalloids (Si, Ge, Sn)

papers.abstract: The stereocontrolled construction of glycosidic linkages from 2-deoxyglycoside donors remains a major challenge in the synthesis of complex oligosaccharides. Herein, we report catalyst-controlled glycosylation protocols that deliver either anomer on demand from the same glycosyl donor, across a broad range of acceptors through simple variation of the chiral Brønsted acid catalyst. Systematic evaluation of a library of readily accessible chiral Brønsted acids reveals how catalyst, donor, and acceptor jointly govern reactivity and stereoselectivity. Mechanistic studies reveal that the stereodivergence originates from distinct reaction pathways promoted by seemingly similar chiral Brønsted acids. This work establishes a general platform for catalyst-controlled anomeric selectivity and expands the synthetic toolbox for stereoselective complex carbohydrate assembly.
papers.title: Stereodivergent Organocatalytic Glycosylation of 2-Deoxyglycosides

papers.abstract: gem-Difluoroallenes undergo copper-catalyzed defluorinative coupling with alkyl and aryl Grignard reagents to give monofluoroallenes. Using Cu(OAc)2 (10 mol%) in THF at −20 °C, eleven products are obtained in 64–95% isolated yield. The transformation replaces one fluorine atom while retaining the cumulated diene. Catalyst screening and substrate scope are described, together with a tentative carbocupration/β-fluoride-elimination pathway.
papers.title: Copper-Catalyzed Defluorinative Coupling of gem-Difluoroallenes with Grignard Reagents

papers.abstract: The membraneless electrolyzer concept has recently gained significant attention as an alternative electrolyzer design which is potentially more durable, flexible, and inexpensive due to the absence of any fragile membrane or diaphragm. While different conceptual designs have been put forward so far, the literature lacks clear quantitative insights on key design and performance parameters. This work presents a comprehensive analysis of the membraneless design encompassing all the primary design concepts i.e. flow-by and flow-through. The study combines experimentally validated Euler-Euler coupled secondary current distribution model, Euler-Lagrange models, and an analytical mass balance model. First, the self-similarity in the parametric Euler-Euler analysis is exploited to formulate a dimensionless correlation by Buckingham Pi analysis for the average gas fraction in H2 and O2 gas plumes (99%). This correlation is complimentary to the analytical bubble mass balance equation presented here that enables simplified estimation of gas plume contours as well as maximum flow-by electrode height, inline with experimental observations. The same dimensional analysis also yields a correlation for plume contours across different operating conditions. For an operating current density of 0.2 A cm-2, Reynolds number of 1600 and 1000, and interelectrode spacing from 1 mm to 6 mm, the maximum flow-by electrode length has been estimated. It is shown with a strong enough flow i.e. Re>1000, the bulk bubble ohmic resistance can be neglected. The self-similarity of the polarization curves for the flow-through membraneless electrolyzer was also established via a Buckingham Pi dimensional analysis. Finally, the analysis draws an unbiased global comparison to assess the performance limits of membraneless electrolyzer designs quantitatively alongside the conventional alkaline electrolyzer.
papers.title: Performance and Design Limits of Membraneless Flow Electrochemical Cells: A Combined Secondary Current and Multiphase Flow Analysis
Collection Effects Behind Genomic-DNA SERS Classification

papers.abstract: Connecting modules to central nodes is a powerful assembly strategy, as exemplified by DNA/RNA, MOFs, and SuFEx/PFEx chemistry. However, SuFEx and PFEx are largely confined to amine- and phenol-type modules and the alcohol modules could be problematic for SuFEx due to potential dehydroxylative reactions. Silicon‑noded cross-ligation offers an attractive alternative because both alcohols and phenols can serve as reliable modules to form stable silyl ethers, but lacks programmable stepwise ligation hubs comparable to those in SuFEx/PFEx. The most straightforward and common dichlorosilanes are not suitable for this purpose due to unpredictable over‑substitution and moisture‑sensitive intermediates. Herein, we develop moisture‑stable bis(polyfluoroalkoxy)silanes as customizable dichlorosilane surrogates for programmable silicon‑noded cross-ligations. Systematic comparisons established a nucleofugality order for silicon-bound polyfluoroalkoxy groups (perfluoro‑tert‑butoxy >> hexafluoroisopropoxy > trifluoroethoxy) and further demonstrated that polyfluoroalkoxysilanes outperformed chlorosilanes and silyl triflates in both handling and chemoselectivity. A general synthetic platform via dephenylative silyletherification enables efficient construction of symmetrical and unsymmetrical bis(polyfluoroalkoxy)silanes with gram‑scale scalability. The resulting hubs enabled predictable, stepwise cross-ligation of diverse functionalized alcohols and phenols under mild basic conditions with broad functionalgroup compatibility. Notably, streamlined, protecting-group-free iterative assembly of the same type of dihydroxy modules, such as 4-hydroxyphenethyl alcohol, at silicon nodes was further demonstrated, guided by the DNA node–module logic and the high chemoselectivity of polyfluoroalkoxysilanes. Collectively, this work overcomes the limitations of dichlorosilane chemistry and offers a versatile platform for silicon‑noded modular assembly.
papers.title: Silicon‑Noded Cross-Ligation Platform Enabled by Customizable and Moisture-Stable Bis(polyfluoroalkoxy)silanes
Donor-level validation of Raman spectroscopy for breast cancer subtype classification

papers.abstract: Late-stage hydrofluorination provides access to fluorinated bioactive compounds suitable for 19 F NMR monitoring of biological processes. We report Fe(III)-mediated radical hydrofluorination of highly substituted, chiral N -heterocycles containing piperidine, indolizidine and pyrrolidine scaffolds to the Markovnikov products. This method tolerated steric bulky substrates as well as substituents on nitrogen with different electronic effects. Finally, an Fe(III) catalytic system was compared with Co(II) and Ni(II) catalysts.
papers.title: Fe-Mediated Hydrofluorination of Piperidines: Access towards Fluorinated Iminosugars

papers.abstract: Nanographenes and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are promising materials for advanced organic electronics, but their late-stage functionalization remains challenging. Here, we report an ipso-substitution, in which tert-butyl groups, which are usually installed for solubility reasons, are selectively replaced by mesylates on PAHs and nanographenes bearing five-membered rings. The reaction proceeds via an oxidative nucleophilic aromatic substitution mechanism and can be implemented in oxidative cyclodehydrogenation protocols to produce substituted PAH skeletons in one pot. Density functional theory calculations (DFT) support the suggested mechanism. Post-functionalization of the mesylates is possible according to literature-known protocols and is successfully demonstrated by the introduction of ether, alkyne, and aryl substituents. By controlling the amount of oxidant and the reaction time, the method enables the synthesis of asymmetric functional hydrocarbons from symmetric precursors overcoming statistical limitations by other protocols. Selected tert-butyl groups thus act as sites for the late-stage functionalization of nanographenes and PAH dyes.
papers.title: Oxidative Nucleophilic Aromatic ipso-Substitution for the Late-Stage Functionalization of Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons with Five-Membered Rings

papers.abstract: In this work, in silico cyclic-minipeptide candidates were computationally generated aiming to develop antibody-free sandwichbased early-diagnosis of ebola virus (EBOV). Presently there are few approved early-rapid EBOV diagnosis, despite many antibody-based efforts. Cyclic-minipeptides were chosen here because i) their vast sequence numbers facilitate designs fitting the diagnostic sensibility and specificity requirements, ii) they are easy and cheaper to scale-up for production, and iii) their rigidity could be more resistant to denaturing-buffers for EBOV early disinfection during assay. In this work, the earlier most abundant biomarker for EBOV infections soluble glycoprotein sGP were computationally targeted. Hundreds of ~ 100-1000-fold 9- and 12-mer candidates predicting higher affinities than previously reported antibodies were proposed here combining Boltzgen/ Prodigy with our newly developed evolutionary-mutations. By targeting complementary sGP cavities with cyclic-minipeptide candidates, possible sandwich-pairs would still require experimentally-guided explorations. Additional computational screening work may also be possible to select the best candidates for possible pan-EBOV diagnosis.
papers.title: In silico cyclic-minipeptides predicting antibody-free early-diagnosis of Ebola virus

papers.abstract: We extend FROST (Fock radial orbital shooting with Taylor series) from atoms whose occupied orbitals are all s orbitals to closed-shell atoms with p and d shells, and report rigorous upper bounds on the Hartree–Fock (HF) energies of the closed-shell atoms from neon to xenon. Their leading digits are correct to 504 significant figures for neon, 103 for magnesium, 105 for argon and 103–106 for the heavier atoms, against previous records of 30 and 25. Three changes to the method make this possible. First, exchange with multipoles k ≥ 1 gives every canonical orbital the exponential tail of the outermost one, so all orbitals must share one wall; this also makes them exactly orthogonal. Second, over that common wall the inner shells are extremely stiff: the growing mode of the krypton 1s orbital rises by 10^1701. The equations are therefore solved by multiple shooting, with Taylor-series segments short enough that no mode grows by more than 10g, coupled by continuity conditions and solved by Newton’s method with a sparse LU factorization, so that the working precision grows with the target accuracy rather than with the stiffness. Third, a homotopy in the electron–electron coupling, from hydrogenic orbitals, supplies a starting point that converges to the ground state. The exact-rational certificate carries over to any angular momentum. Writing each radial function as P = rl+1f with f piecewise polynomial, the triangle rule k ≤ la + lb cancels the factor r−k−1 of every multipole, so all overlap, one-electron and Slater integrals are exact rationals. All 25 published digits of the quadruple-precision energies of Cinal are reproduced, as are his positions of the exchange-induced nodes of inner orbitals, which we locate to about 100 significant figures.
papers.title: FROST II: certified Hartree–Fock limits of the closed-shell atoms from neon to xenon

papers.abstract: Molecular crystal structure prediction (CSP) has radically evolved over the last two decades from a niche research topic to a tool for solid form prediction and derisking. The Control and Prediction of the Organic Solid State (CPOSS) project led by Professor Sarah (Sally) Price has developed CSP over more than two decades of research, generating a large number of deeply researched landscapes, populated by alternative crystal packings for a given chemical system, including structures and systems that have not been observed experimentally. Here we present the CPOSS Database of Computed Crystal Structures, a public collection of CSP landscapes developed within the CPOSS project. This public inventory contains 310 documented searches for 234 molecular systems, comprising 190 single-component and 44 multicomponent systems, with 517,594 archived structure files across 508 energy-model archives. Structures are accompanied by search and computational-method descriptions, tabulated properties, and connections to experimental structures and the original literature where available. The collection’s principal contribution is its depth of candidate packing arrangements for individual systems, together with the provenance needed to interpret successive searches and energy refinements. We describe the construction, coverage, access routes, and limitations of the public release, and discuss its use in physical chemistry, crystal structure prediction, and atomistic model development. The database is released together with an interactive CSP Landscape Navigator under CC0 1.0.
papers.title: The CPOSS Database of Computed Crystal Structures

papers.abstract: Published closed-loop self-driving laboratories (SDLs) are described in prose, so what their records could predict about a new platform has not been tested. I release sdl-workflows , a database of 237 SDL papers coded by a language model as ordered steps, each with an operation and the type of module performing it, and as connections between modules, each with a transfer mode such as fixed tubing, a robot arm or a person (2610 steps and 1681 connections). On 30 held-out papers, the records agreed with an independent coding by a second model (micro-F1 0.891 to 0.905). The release includes the timing data the papers state and an explorer for comparing platforms. A model fitted to papers up to 2023 assigns each connection the most frequent mode among earlier connections between the same operations in the same field. It predicted the recorded transfer mode of 424 connections in papers from 2024 better than the most frequent mode per pair of operation families (accuracy 0.512 against 0.441; 95% confidence interval of the difference 0.016 to 0.125). A model of the same kind did not predict the module type of 1189 steps better than the most frequent module type per operation. A discrete-event simulation predicted reported throughput no better than the median throughput reported by other papers in the same field. Its inputs are rarely stated: 23 of the 237 papers give the duration of every step. The prediction of module types and transfer modes is released as a benchmark.
papers.title: What Can the Records of Published Self-Driving Laboratories Predict About a New Platform? A Step-Level Database and Explorer

papers.abstract: Why can AI agents operate reliably in digital environments such as software development yet still struggle to achieve autonomous scientific discovery? We argue that this gap reflects not only limitations in model capability but also differences in how agent capabilities are externalized and how reliably environments can verify the consequences of agent actions. In this survey, we trace the technical evolution of AI agents and propose a three-stage framework of capability externalization: reasoning externalization makes knowledge, memory, and intermediate inferences inspectable; execution externalization makes tool use and long-horizon workflows governable; and world-interaction externalization integrates environmental evidence into hypothesis revision and action selection. Materials discovery provides a demanding testbed for all three stages, spanning literature-grounded hypothesis generation, computational design, automated experimentation, and iterative knowledge updating. Although agents can increasingly complete predefined research workflows, workflow automation alone does not constitute scientific discovery. Sustained autonomy requires agents to assess whether new observations support or challenge a hypothesis and to select subsequent experiments accordingly. We therefore identify environmental verifiability as a central systems constraint on agent autonomy: the extent to which an environment can translate actions into timely, attributable, reproducible, and affordable evidence. This perspective positions physical verification capacity as a key scaling dimension for autonomous scientific discovery.
papers.title: From Execution to Discovery : Physical Verification as the Key Gap in AI Agents for Science

papers.abstract: Metal oxide nanoislands offer a localized source of metal centers for the on-surface assembly of coordination networks. Here, we investigate the adsorption and thermal evolution of 4,4'-biphenyldicarboxylic acid (BDA) on CoO nanoislands supported on Au(111) under ultrahigh vacuum using infrared reflection absorption spectroscopy (IRAS), scanning tunneling microscopy (STM), and density functional theory (DFT). At 400 K, BDA forms two coexisting populations: carboxylate species anchored to CoO and a predominantly flat-lying, hydrogen-bonded molecular layer on Au(111). Heating to 500 K removes the IR signatures of intact carboxylic acid groups and changes the relative intensities of the out-of-plane C-H modes. STM reveals a rectangular two-dimensional Co–BDA coordination network, for which DFT supports a structural model containing paired Co centers. These observations support a pathway in which Co species are supplied by partial dissolution of the oxide nanoislands. Annealing to 600 K produces arrays of coordination chains with single-Co nodes, while the IR spectra remain consistent with predominantly flat-lying biphenyl units. These results demonstrate that supported metal oxide nanoislands can serve as precursors for the formation of surface-confined 2D MOFs and provide an alternative route to thermally controlled metal–organic assembly on metal surfaces. TOC Graphic Thermally controlled MOF growth. CoO nanoislands on Au(111) serve as a metal precursor for the formation of a surface-confined Co–BDA network. Annealing at 500 K produces a rectangular 2D MOF with paired Co centers, while further annealing to 600 K induces a transformation into 1D Co–BDA arrays with single-Co nodes. This oxide-mediated approach provides a new route to surface-supported 2D MOF synthesis.
papers.title: CoO Nanoislands as Metal Oxide Precursors for Surface-Supported Co–BDA Coordination Networks

papers.abstract: IrO2 is the state-of-the-art catalyst for oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in acid. Previous theoretical investigations are largely based on the (110) surface, with undercoordinated Ircus sites being considered as active centers under reaction conditions, whereas coordinated Irbr sites are considered spectators. Using a combination of density functional theory and ab initio molecular dynamics, we demonstrate that the Irbr sites reconstruct under anodic polarization leading to the formation of single-atom catalyst (SAC)-like centers. These SAC sites exhibit higher activity for OER than Ircus sites and are identified as durable under anodic polarization using a stability analysis based on a Born-Haber cycle. This work provides a framework for understanding how surface reconstruction fundamentally alters the catalytic function of known oxide surfaces by transforming spectator sites into primary active centers for energy conversion and storage.
papers.title: Surface Reconstruction Activates Bridge Sites of Rutile IrO2(110) for Oxygen Evolution Reaction

papers.abstract: Herein, we report the first enantioselective total syntheses of bousigonine A and bisleuconothine B, two heterodimeric monoterpenoid indole alkaloids. The requisite quebrachamine-type and aspidosperma-type alkaloid units were prepared divergently from a common intermediate and subsequently coupled with an eburnan-type alkaloid through bioinspired coupling reactions. The benzyl protecting group on the nitrogen played a crucial role in controlling the regioselectivity of these reactions, enabling selective bond formation at C10. Subsequent chemoselective oxidations of the coupling products furnished the characteristic quinone and N,O-acetal moieties, completing the total syntheses of both natural products. Furthermore, these synthetic studies led to a revision of the absolute configuration of bousigonine A.
papers.title: Enantioselective Total Syntheses of Bousigonine A and Bisleuconothine B

papers.abstract: The prevailing way to model a many-body system is to encode every component and then let a module capture interaction. We show that the explicit interaction module is harmful when the number of components increases. We use a simple interaction-carrying encoder that compresses a component’s interaction contribution into its representation, and combine the representations by linear aggregation. This modelling approach is simple in form yet delivers unexpectedly excellent performance: it matches the prevailing explicit route under most conditions and exceeds it when a mixture carries more components than the training set covered. Moreover, an encoder produced this way has a clear advantage over per-component descriptors when it is transferred to a similar task: it greatly reduces the data requirements.
papers.title: Interaction without an interaction module
DolphinQCT: The Light-Weighted, Python Based Quasi-Classical Trajectory Setup Tool for ORCA
Tension-Limited Leaflet-Asymmetry Budding Predicts the Size and Rate of Tumour Ectosome Shedding

papers.abstract: The state of affairs of multidimensional gas chromatography (MDGC) at present is no more than an implementation of a two-dimensional form (2D-GC) reducing its scope to the setup known as GCxGC. Introduced in 1991 with great expectation, however, GCxGC still happen to fall short of realizing the anticipated capabilities despite continuous efforts made over the elapsed 35 years. This got quantitative formulation in regard of separation performance as early as 2008, proving that it failed to be competitive with a well-governed 1D-GC. The present paper highlights further limitations of GCxGC: inadequate operation burdened with shortcomings are presented via examples taken from GCxGC literature; crowning the list with the inability to meet fundamental requirement that if a compound can be analyzed by 1D-GC it must remain analyzable by MDGC. The repertoire of the intertwining issues, each of which unavoidably rigs or even hamstrings the others, highlights that GCxGC has a built-in self-limiting feature. Attempts to overcome confinements via loosening the binding conditions turned GCxGC back to the form it emerged from decades ago, yet without getting rid of the hampering curbs. The unfavorable overall picture forces to consider viabilities of other concepts, with focus on avoiding errors and pitfalls of GCxGC while fulfilling basic requirements of MDGC. In our view, there are two alternatives. One is ZGC, principle of which was introduced in 1989, requirements and potential of which are presented here in more detail; the other is a concept called Quantum-GC, which is presented as an introductory approach.
papers.title: Treatise on Present Practice and Perspectives of MDGC

papers.abstract: We report the first catalytic phosphorus-based hydrogen atom transfer system operating under redox-neutral conditions. Using an iridium photocatalyst and 10 mol% diphenylphosphine sulfide, we achieve decarboxylative reduction of diverse carboxylic acids—including peptides and pharmaceuticals—to C–H products in up to 95% yield, without stoichiometric reductants. Mechanistic studies reveal an unprecedented anionic relay: a phosphoryl radical is reduced to a phosphinoyl anion, which upon protonation regenerates the P–H catalyst. This work establishes redox-neutral catalytic turnover in phosphorus-based HAT and identifies a new elementary step in main-group radical chemistry.
papers.title: Catalytic Phosphorus-Based Hydrogen Atom Transfer via a Phosphinoyl Anion Relay

papers.abstract: Accurate estimation of protein-ligand binding affinities remains central to structure-based drug design. Classical force fields neglect important quantum-mechanical effects, while quantum mechanical and semi-empirical methods remain impractical for large biomolecular systems. Machine-learned force fields (MLFFs) offer an alternative, but their performance may be inflated by training on protein-ligand complexes. Here, we introduce SO3LR-SF, a physics-based scoring framework that can be instantiated with any of the four pretrained SO3LR MLFF models, combining an equivariant message-passing network for semi-local interactions with physically motivated terms for short-range repulsion, electrostatics, and long-range dispersion. On PLA15 (15 active-site models), SO3LR-SF attains a relative interaction error of 2.1-5.8% against DLPNO-CCSD(T) references depending on the underlying SO3LR model, with SO3LR-T-M reaching 2.1%, the lowest of all tested methods. On the FEP benchmark (8 targets, 264 ligands), all SO3LR-SF variants achieve an average Spearman correlation of around 0.50, on par with the best semi-empirical quantum-mechanical method tested (0.47, GFN-FF) and with MMGBSA (0.44), and surpassing Glide (0.27). On the Wang dataset (8 targets, 199 ligands), the SO3LR-SF models reach around 0.59, matching the 0.59-0.62 range of molecular dynamics-based free-energy methods at a fraction of their cost. Each complex is scored in 3 s to 47 s on 12 CPU cores. An 8 Å trimming protocol reduces runtime threefold without loss of accuracy, and a restrained geometry optimization recovers ranking accuracy for targets with strained input structures. A multi-level explainability framework adds energy decomposition, per-atom energy contributions reported either for ligand or as 2D protein-ligand interaction maps, and 3D binding site visualization. We found that the polar SASA ratio of the binding pocket is predictive of electrostatic scoring performance, enabling estimation of ligand-ranking accuracy before scoring (r = 0.74-0.81 across models). Together, SO3LR-SF presents a fast, interpretable, and competitive scoring function for drug discovery that requires no experimental binding-affinity data for training.
papers.title: Explainable ML force-field for evaluating protein–ligand binding energy using SO3LR

papers.abstract: Zeolites have been proposed as carrier materials for the storage and controlled release of the anticancer drug 5-fluorouracil (5-FU). Containing both hydrogen-bond donor and acceptor groups, 5-FU molecules can form relatively strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds. Prior work on zeolite beta has shown that guest-guest interaction between co-adsorbed 5-FU molecules reduce their diffusivity at high loadings. However, a systematic assessment of the influence of 5-FU oligomer size and zeolite pore topology is so far lacking. Aiming to fill this gap, the present study employs atomistic simulations at different levels of theory to elucidate the strength of 5-FU−5-FU interactions as well as their impact on diffusion in all-silica zeolites. In the first part, adsorption energies of 5-FU oligomers in four zeolites (FAU, BEA, MOR, MFI frameworks) are computed with dispersion-corrected density functional theory (DFT) calculations. In all four zeolites, 5-FU dimers are considerably more stable than individual 5-FU molecules due to attractive guest-guest interactions. However, an additional stabilisation of larger oligomers is prominent only for FAU, where the large supercages impose less constraints on molecular orientation compared to zeolites with channel-type pores. In the second part, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with classical force fields are used to investigate the diffusion of 5-FU in zeolites FAU and MOR. For single molecules, the computed self-diffusion coefficients are on the order of 1 to 2∙10 −9 m 2 /s for FAU and 3 to 6∙10 −9 m 2 /s for MOR. Dimers and larger oligomers diffuse more slowly. While 5-FU dimers and trimers remain mobile in MOR, trimers and especially tetramers in FAU become nearly immobile on the nanosecond timescale. These findings highlight that the diffusion of molecules that can form strong hydrogen bonds can be significantly impeded by attractive guest-guest interactions, even at very low loadings. Besides, the low mobility of larger 5-FU oligomers could indicate that kinetic effects are responsible for the large discrepancy between experimentally reported 5-FU uptakes in FAU-type zeolites and theoretical predictions.
papers.title: Guest-guest interactions and their impact on molecular mobility: a simulation study of 5-fluorouracil adsorption and diffusion in hydrophobic zeolites

papers.abstract: The development of “transition metal-like” reactivity using earth-abundant p-block elements is one of the most prominent and challenging goals of contemporary main group chemistry. This difficulty is exemplified by the key, catalytically relevant bond-forming step of reductive elimination which, while often facile for transition metals, is very difficult to achieve for most main group elements. Efforts to bridge this gap have typically focused on delicate tailoring of electronic structure, supporting ligands, and coordination geometry, a task that is conceptually difficult and synthetically demanding. Herein, we demonstrate an alternative approach. We show that photocatalytic reductive elimination from an already well-known P(V) complex can be achieved rapidly and under mild conditions, via a transient oxidation strategy analogous to “oxidatively induced reductive elimination”. This concept has previously been applied only to transition metal complexes but is now extended to the field of main group chemistry. These results demonstrate a simple, easily accessible, but potentially very powerful new strategy for ‘turbocharging’ transition metal-like reactivity at a main group centre. Thus, it provides a valuable new tool for the ongoing pursuit of transition metal-like catalysis using main group elements.
papers.title: Photocatalytic Reductive Elimination From A Main Group Centre

papers.abstract: Sintering deactivates supported catalysts, yet how mobile support defects couple to crystallographic transport anisotropy during nanoparticle coalescence remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a ternary Ce–O–Pd machine-learning interatomic potential (Ce–O–Pd MLIP) by fine-tuning a pre-trained large atomic model and validate it against density functional theory (DFT) calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD). Large-scale deep potential molecular dynamics (DPMD) simulations resolve early-stage coarsening of Pd 62 /Pd 287 nanoparticle pairs on CeO 2–x (110) and reveal direction-selective coalescence: [11̅0]-aligned pairs exhibit higher probabilities and shorter onset times than [001]-aligned pairs. CI-NEB calculations identify complementary transport anisotropies, with Pd adatom diffusion favored along [11̅0] and oxygen-vacancy migration favored along [001], enabling dynamic defect redistribution within the interparticle region. Statistical trajectory analysis shows that increasing the interparticle oxygen-vacancy fraction from 10% to 30% raises coalescence probability and accelerates bridge and neck nucleation, including along the kinetically less favorable [001] alignment. Time-resolved metrics further show that transient low-coordinated bridge-Pd intermediates precede complete particle merging. Together, these results establish defect–transport coupling as a microscopic mechanism for direction-selective sintering on reduced ceria and suggest that suppressing vacancy enrichment and connectivity in interparticle gaps can improve the stability of oxide-supported metal nanoparticles.
papers.title: Dynamic vacancy redistribution shifts Pd nanoparticle coalescence from orientation-gated to defect-enabled on reduced CeO2(110)

papers.abstract: A copper-catalyzed retro-allylation of homoallylic alcohols has been developed as a strategy for the stereoselective methallylation of carbonyl compounds. High-throughput experimentation (HTE) was employed to rapidly screen chiral phosphine ligands and Cu–NHC complexes across seven representative aldehydes and ketones, enabling the identification of effective catalytic systems. Subsequent batch experiments provided the corresponding chiral homoallylic products in high isolated yields (up to 90%) and with enantioselectivities of up to 83% ee. The reactivity was further explored with an oxime ether and an α,β-unsaturated diester, providing preliminary evidence for the extension of the retro-allylation strategy beyond carbonyl compounds.
papers.title: HTE-Guided Development of an Asymmetric Copper-Catalyzed Retro-Allylation for Stereoselective Methallylation †

papers.abstract: We report the use of Fe–Ag bimetallic nanoparticles supported on α-Al₂O₃ as tunable highly active and selective catalysts for the semihydrogenation of acetylene in ethylene rich streams. The addition of silver enhances the ethylene selectivity. Experimental evidence was supported by DFT calculations predicting Gibbs free energies and adsorption energies as a function of catalyst composition. Comprehensive characterization was carried out using ICP, XRF, XRD, N₂-physisorption, TPR, STEM-EDX, and XPS. This work is inspired by the need for more sustainable catalysts beyond Pd for the removal of trace amounts of acetylene from the ethylene under front-end conditions downstream of industrial steam crackers for olefin production. Conventional Pd-based catalysts, though highly active, suffer from limited selectivity, high cost, and environmental concerns. Iron emerges as a sustainable alternative due to its abundance, low toxicity, and favorable hydrogenation activity. Incorporation of silver into iron catalysts leverages synergistic effects that allow to tune the performance of the catalysts. These effects result in enhanced catalytic activity and improved selectivity towards ethylene. The present work demonstrates a promising approach for developing cost-effective, sustainable, and highly active catalysts for industrial acetylene hydrogenation.
papers.title: Tuning supported Fe-Ag catalysts for selective acetylene hydrogenation: A combined experimental and computational study

papers.abstract: Selecting multistep synthetic routes remains a major bottleneck in computer-aided synthesis planning because high-quality negative data are scarce and no single reported route can completely define route quality. We introduce an expert-augmented framework that combines large-scale reference-based route learning with expert-defined chemical feasibility assessment. Large-scale pre-training on literature-derived reference routes yields 60.3% top-1 reference-route recovery on held-out targets. The model’s rank-1 recommendations were feasible in 88.4% of assessed cases, comprising reported literature routes and expert-endorsed novel proposals. Expert assessment shows that disagreement with the literature reference does not necessarily imply chemical failure: 75.4% of novel rank-1 proposals were judged feasible. The pre-trained model already captures a measurable expert-feasibility signal (Spearman |ρ| = 0.46), which increases to 0.78 ± 0.05 after expert fine-tuning. On an independent multi-expert dataset, agreement with the expert majority increases from 48.0% before fine-tuning to 64.0% afterwards, compared with 64.8% agreement between a held-out expert and the majority of their peers under the same metric. Together, these results show that large-scale proxy supervision can provide scalable route prioritization, while limited expert supervision substantially improves alignment with chemical feasibility.
papers.title: An Expert-Augmented Deep Learning Approach for Synthesis Route Evaluation

papers.abstract: Histatin 5 (Hst5) is one of the most potent antifungal members of the salivary histatin family, exhibiting activity against the opportunistic fungus Candida albicans, with reported intracellular localisation to mitochondria and effects on mitochondrial function. This localization, together with Hst5's ability to bind redox-active Cu(II) ions, suggested that Cu(II)-Hst5 complexes could catalyze ROS production via Cu(II)/Cu(I) cycling. The high stability of the primary Cu(II)-Hst5 complex engaging the ATCUN motif and its high resistance to the reduction call into question the feasibility of such a mechanism. Employing electrochemical methods and spectroscopic measurements, we investigated how copper coordination influences redox reactivity in Hst5 and its N-terminal fragments, examining two possible sources of redox activity in Cu(II)/Hst5 mixtures.
