The first involves either incomplete Cu(II) coordination within the ATCUN motif or Cu(II) ions not bound to Hst5. The second is the binding of excess Cu(II) to additional Cu(II)-binding sites in the Hst5 sequence. We also utilized electrochemical techniques to investigate the interactions of Hst5 and its Cu(II) complexes with DMPC-based lipid layers, revealing stronger perturbation by full-length Hst5 than by its N-terminal fragments.
papers.title: Electrochemical Insights into Histatin 5 Antimicrobial Activity: Cu(II) Redox Chemistry and Model Lipid Layer Interactions

papers.abstract: Crystallising two-dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) from irreversible bonds is hindered by the absence of error correction and out-of-plane disorder. Here, we establish linkage-sparing assembly (LSA) as a novel strategy for overcoming this limitation: preformed oligomeric motifs encode part of the target lattice, reducing the number of new irreversible C–C bonds required for framework growth. Combined with kinetic control through temperature and water content, LSA yields micrometre-scale single crystals of a phenylene-linked COF (HPPCOF) formed by ketone cyclotrimerisation. Electron diffraction resolves its honeycomb (hcb) structure and reveals local disorder and unreacted defects, providing insight into the real structure of an irreversibly formed 2D network. The heteroatom-free polyphenylene COF photocatalyses oxygen reduction to H2O2 via the oxygen reduction reaction, with activity comparable to heteroatom-containing COFs and without sacrificial electron donors. These results identify preassembly and kinetic control as complementary tools for crystallising robust COFs and broaden design opportunities for irreversible linkages.
papers.title: Linkage-sparing Assembly of Single-crystalline Phenylene-linked Covalent Organic Frameworks

papers.abstract: Frozen embeddings from pretrained chemical language models (cLMs) are widely used as features for ADMET and drug-delivery prediction, often with a linear probe and little validation of what the representation actually contributes. We audit two small public cLMs (ChemBERTa-77M-MLM and ChemBERTa-77M-MTR, 3.4M parameters each) on three delivery-relevant endpoints from openly licensed sources: blood–brain barrier penetration (B3DB, CC0), PAMPA permeability (NCATS via PubChem), and Caco-2 permeability (OpenADMET, CC-BY-4.0). For each endpoint we compare frozen mean-pooled embeddings with (i) Morgan-fingerprint linear probes with train-only tuned regularization, (ii) the same architecture with random weights (five initialization seeds), and (iii) scaffoldconstant control tasks in the style of Hewitt and Liang that quantify how much a linear probe can score by memorizing scaffold identity. On observed means, tuned fingerprint probes are slightly ahead of frozen embeddings on all three endpoints (paired per-split differences of 0.016–0.032 in AUROC or R2, smaller than split-to-split variation); trained embeddings exceed random-initialization controls by 0.04–0.10; endpoint probes are selective above scaffold-memorization controls, and the memorization ceiling rises with layer depth in the primary MLM model. Decodability of bulk physicochemical descriptors (molecular weight, TPSA, fraction sp3, aromatic rings) is largely preserved under random initialization, indicating an architectural rather than learned origin for those signals; learned increments appear for logP, hydrogen-bond donors, and rotatable bonds. We quantify three practitioner pitfalls: pooling choice changes endpoint AUROC by up to 0.05; tuning the fin- gerprint baseline’s regularization changes it by up to 0.03 AUROC or 0.20 R2; and scaffoldsplit construction details change means by up to 0.04, exceeding seed standard deviations. The source datasets are public and cited; all curation scripts, pipeline code, and per-seed results are included in the accompanying package. The study is compute-bounded to CPU and small models, which limits the generality of the conclusions to that regime.
papers.title: Auditing frozen chemical language model embeddings for drug-delivery screening: fingerprint baselines, random-initialization controls, and scaffold-memorization control tasks

papers.abstract: Lithium-based all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) are attracting increasing attention as nextgeneration energy storage systems. However, maintaining intimate solid–solid contact within NMC-based composite cathodes during repeated lithium extraction and insertion remains a major challenge. Because the stability of these contacts is largely determined by the electrode microstructure established during manufacturing, advanced pressing strategies are increasingly being explored to reduce residual porosity and promote homogeneous particle packing. Here, we compare warm isostatic pressing with conventional cold uniaxial pressing and investigate how the two processing routes affect electrochemical performance and the spatial distribution of mechanical stresses through a combined experimental and numerical approach based on 3Dresolved electrode manufacturing simulations and a fully coupled mechano-electrochemical model. Warm isostatically pressed cathode produces a denser and thinner cathode with reduced porosity, enhanced active material-solid electrolyte contact, improved ionic and electronic transport, and lower geometric. While both cathodes show comparable behavior at C/10, WIP maintains higher accessible capacity and more homogeneous active material utilization at C/2, supported by a more spatially distributed ionic current network. In contrast, hydrostatic-stress differences between WIP and CUP remain comparatively modest. These results establish a
papers.title: Warm Isostatic vs. Cold Uniaxial Pressing in All-Solid-State Battery Cathodes: Linking Microstructure, Transport, and Mechano-Electrochemical Response

papers.abstract: Automated workflows are rapidly accelerating discovery across the chemical sciences, yet the throughput of such platforms remains bottlenecked by the high cost and slow operation of traditional analytical hardware. 1 While digital colorimetry offers a ubiquitous, low-cost alternative for reaction monitoring, current techniques rely on the linear approximations of the Beer–Lambert law. 2, 3 This constraint causes data degeneracy, severely limiting analytical accuracy. Here we present quantitative Colorimetric Analysis of Molecules (qCAM), a methodology that bypasses the Beer–Lambert law by retaining the full dimensionality of digital colorimetric data. When applied to the quantification of metals in solution, qCAM matches the accuracy of inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS), the current gold-standard tool, while reducing equipment costs 100-fold and accelerating analysis time from hours to minutes. We demonstrate the versatility of qCAM as compatible with both high-throughput workflows and automated flow-synthesis platforms for chemical, environmental, and medical monitoring, producing results within 0.20 ppm of current analytical methods.
papers.title: Transcending the Beer–Lambert Limit with Full-Dimensional Digital Colorimetry

papers.abstract: Microporous materials are promising adsorbents for gas separations, but their adoption has been limited by the energy requirements of vacuum or heat used to regenerate the material. Lower energy swing triggers have been explored (such as light, magnetism, electricity, and humidity) to desorb gases; however, these alternative processes can also use large amounts of energy at scale. Hydrogen bonded organic frameworks (HOFs) are molecular microporous materials that exhibit solution processibility and polymorphism. We show that a HOF, MeTBAP‑α, can switch between its porous crystalline α‑phase and a dense, non‑porous salt phase via deprotonation with amine vapour. This process is then reversed via alcohol exposure. By cycling between these porous and non‑porous states, we demonstrate a vapour assisted phase swing adsorption (VAPSA) process where CO2 can be repeatedly adsorbed and desorbed. VAPSA is unique in requiring near‑zero direct energy input, paving the way to gas separations with dramatically reduced energy footprints.
papers.title: Near‑Zero Energy CO2 Capture Using Vapour Assisted Phase Swing Adsorption (VAPSA)

papers.abstract: Withdrawn at the authors' request because it did not comply with journal policies.
papers.title: WITHDRAWN

papers.abstract: Extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectroscopy can be used to observe the local environment around absorber atoms. Provided high enough time resolution can be achieved, this would open the possibility of tracking nonequilibrium solvation dynamics in photoreactions in real time. Here we simulate an electron detachment process from aqueous Cl−, Br−, and I− using quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics molecular dynamics simulations and analyze the following solvation dynamics. We show how femtosecond-resolved EXAFS spectra, calculated using an effective dissipative theory, capture the solvation dynamics around nascent Cl0, Br0, and I0. The atomistic simulations reveal that, after instantaneous electron detachment, the rotation of water molecules in the solvation shell as well as the following formation of a halogen-atom–water complex happens more slowly for smaller halogen species. Here the initially tighter and more ordered solvation shell around the smaller halogen ions hinders the nonequilibrium rearrangement of the water molecules, in response to the change in charge state, compared to the larger halogens. Even though directly recovering atom distributions during the solvation process by Fourier inversion of EXAFS spectra was not possible, the time-dependent EXAFS spectrum is sensitive to nonequilibrium dynamics, taking into consideration that the phase shifts experienced by the EXAFS photoelectron before and after photodetachment from halide anions are different. In addition we demonstrate that it is possible to discern the nonequilibrium solvation dynamics for different nascent halogen atoms using time-dependent EXAFS.
papers.title: EXAFS probing of nonequilibrium solvation dynamics of nascent halogen radicals

papers.abstract: The rate at which batteries can be charged is limited by the transport of the working ion through the electrolyte. In polymer electrolytes, the selective transport of Li+ ions is dependent on the solvation cage surrounding the Li+ ion. In this work, we measure cation and anion self-diffusion coefficients using pulsed field gradient nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (PFG-NMR) in electrolytes containing poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) or poly(pentyl malonate) (PPM) mixed with lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI). We utilize molecular dynamics simulations to explore the connection between self-diffusion and the solvation cage structures of the Li+ ions. Decomposition of solvation cage dynamics allows for identification of two Li+ hopping mechanisms: interchain and intrachain hopping. We find that interchain hops are extremely rare in PEO/LiTFSI (i.e., back-and-forth intrachain hops are dominant). In contrast, inter- and intrachain hops in PPM/LiTFSI occur at similar rates. Interchain hopping is necessary for selective Li+ transport between battery electrodes and greater interchain hopping efficiency in PPM/LiTFSI results in improved Li+ transport.
papers.title: Ion Transport Dynamics in Poly(ethylene oxide) and Poly(pentyl malonate) Electrolytes for Lithium Batteries

papers.abstract: Here we introduce MC-xDH5, the first doubly hybrid functional within the multiconfiguration pair-density functional theory (MC-PDFT) framework, completing the top rung of the MC-PDFT Jacob’s ladder. Introducing perturbative correlation into MC-PDFT raises two challenges: double counting and reference selection. MC-xDH5 overcomes both through the cross-entropy of the natural orbital occupations, which subtracts an estimate of the correlation already contained in the reference and defines a saturation active space (SAS) for the perturbative step. With five optimized parameters, MC-xDH5 reaches mean absolute errors of 2.5 kcal·mol−1 on the training sets, 1.2 kcal·mol−1 on unseen GMTKN55 subsets, and 1.0 kcal·mol−1 across vertical excitation energies and singlet–triplet gaps for ten thermally activated delayed fluorescence molecules. MC-xDH5 thus brings chemical accuracy for multiconfigurational problems within reach at a computational cost comparable to its second-order perturbation theory.
papers.title: Completing the Jacob’s ladder of multiconfiguration pair-density functional theory with a doubly hybrid functional

papers.abstract: All-iron redox flow batteries are attractive candidates for large-scale energy storage owing to their use of earth-abundant and low-cost active materials. In this work, additively manufactured architected electrodes were developed to investigate the influence of electrode composition and architecture on cell performance. Stainless-steel electrodes were fabricated by laser powder bed fusion, while iron-containing carbon (Fe-C) electrodes were fabricated by digital light processing followed by carbonization. Gyroid and body-centered cubic (BCC) architectures were evaluated and benchmarked against commercial electrodes. Electrode composition was found to exert a greater influence on performance than architecture or electrode thickness. The Fe-C gyroid electrode achieved the highest peak power density (96.5 mW cm-2), outperforming both the stainless-steel gyroid electrode (74.2 mW cm-2) and commercial stainless-steel mesh (71.5 mW cm-2). Within the Fe-C electrode family, the gyroid architecture consistently outperformed the BCC structure, whereas only minor architectural effects were observed for the stainless-steel electrodes. Galvanostatic cycling further demonstrated stable long-term operation and distinct electrochemical behavior for the Fe-C electrodes, including unusually large first-discharge capacities and unique multi-step discharge profiles, suggesting the presence of additional electrochemically accessible iron species within the Fe-C framework. These results demonstrate the potential of combining additive manufacturing and resin engineering to create architected Fe-C electrodes for all-iron redox flow batteries. The distinct electrochemical behavior of the Fe-C electrodes, together with their superior polarization performance, suggests that architected iron-containing carbon electrodes represent a promising new electrode platform for iron-based flow battery systems.
papers.title: Architected Iron-Carbon and Stainless-Steel Electrodes Fabricated by Additive Manufacturing for All-Iron Redox Flow Batteries

papers.abstract: A calibration standard can satisfy the chromatographic system suitability parameters monitored in routine use and still be an order of magnitude from its nominal concentration. This report documents two such events in a single method development exercise on coenzyme Q10 (ubidecarenone), together with the solubility measurements that explain them. A stock solution prepared at 1 mg/mL in methanol:ethanol 65:35 (v/v) — approximately five times the equilibrium solubility of coenzyme Q10 in that diluent — was forced into solution by sonication and warming to approximately 36–37 °C, then held overnight. Calibration levels prepared from it the following morning were approximately ten-fold low, with a response-factor relative standard deviation of 14.9% and a coefficient of determination of 0.985. Throughout that sequence the instrument reported plate counts of 2,489–2,641, tailing factors of 1.272–1.296, injection repeatability of 0.23% across a four-fold concentration range, and carryover of 0.000%. No chromatographic parameter indicated a fault. Apparent equilibrium solubility was subsequently determined by saturation against a gravimetrically prepared calibration curve, both values lying above its highest level and so obtained by extrapolation: approximately 206 µg/mL at 24.5 °C and 119 µg/mL at refrigerator temperature, a decrease of 42%. Dissolution from the solid was found to require approximately 20 hours at 88 µg/mL and approximately 40 hours at 150 µg/mL at 24.5 °C, while crystallisation on cooling occurred overnight. A second and differently arising discrepancy was identified in the same study: a solution prepared below the solubility limit, judged visually clear after 20 hours, assayed at 82.3% of its nominal concentration. If the deficit is attributed entirely to incomplete dissolution, it corresponds to approximately 0.78 mg of the 4.4 mg weighed, a quantity not visible in the flask. The present data establish the deficit but do not independently establish its mechanism. Two minor peaks sharing the analyte's chromophore, at relative retentions of 0.745 and 1.373, are consistent with coenzyme Q9 and coenzyme Q11 on the compendial relative retention and on homologous-series behaviour, and showed relative peak-area percentages threefold and 1.3-fold higher in the saturated solution than in an undersaturated one, the direction solubility predicts. Both failures are invisible to inspection and undetected by system suitability. Practical recommendations are given.
papers.title: When the standard is not the standard

papers.abstract: Before innovative computational instruments are incorporated into regulatory research and scientific practice, a thorough presentation of their computational reproducibility is fundamental. This study thoroughly benchmarks ReleaseKinetix. ReleaseKinetix is an independent, browserbased platform. It is used for comparison of in vitro dissolution profiles and release-kinetic modeling. The study benchmarks ReleaseKinetix (for comparing in vitro dissolution profiles and modeling release kinetics) against two independently written nonlinear least-squares reference engines. These are Python/scipy and R/minpack.lm. The study also benchmarks ReleaseKinetix against the third-party R package bootf2, published DDSolver Excel add-in values. The study also benchmarks ReleaseKinetix against data from the published literature. Seven datasets were used. Six came from the literature. One was synthetic with high variability. Agreement was judged against a predefined absolute tolerance of 0.01, corresponding to the two decimal places with which the similarity factor f2 is commonly reported. The 288 compared values covered similarity and difference factors, dissolution efficiency, mean dissolution time, and the parameters and goodness-of-fit statistics of six kinetic models. Of these, 272 were reproduced exactly (with a difference of less than one millionth), and the remaining 16 (all nonlinear model parameters) differed only at the level of solver tolerance, with none of them exceeding 0.01. The largest difference (0.00026) was smaller than the difference between the two reference engines (0.00047). The platform and the reference engines selected the same candidate kinetic models using the Akaike information criterion and reached the same conclusion based on similarity for every dataset. An apparent discrepancy in the Akaike values between the software tools was caused by a constant offset resulting from two different formula conventions, not a calculation error. The benchmark also revealed two errors in the platform, both of them corrected before the reported results. First, small decreases of the mean profile on the dissolution plateau were ignored in the mean dissolution time calculation, which resulted in an overestimation of 0.022 min. Second, the European Medicines Agency's 85% truncation rule was triggered by the reference product alone, whereas the guideline requires truncation as soon as either product exceeds 85%. This misreading was also observed in the in-house reference engines and was only detected through comparison with bootf2. No similarity conclusions changed after correction. The expected f2 had similar bootstrap confidence intervals across the platform and the reference engines. For the published data, bootf2 had similar confidence intervals within random sampling variation. However, near the similarity limit of 50, the lower confidence bound depended on the random seed. ReleaseKinetix reproduces standard dissolution calculations as precisely as independent implementations. This verified computational core forms the basis of the platform’s rule-based regulatory decision support layer, the interpretive reliability of which remains to be established in future studies.
papers.title: Benchmarking ReleaseKinetix: Numerical Equivalence of a Web-Based Platform for Dissolution Analytics and Regulatory Decision Support

papers.abstract: Summary. Therapeutic peptides occupy a chemical and pharmacological space between smallmolecules and biologics, offering extended recognition surfaces and access to targets that resist conventionalmodalities. Their discovery, however, requires the simultaneous optimization of activity, selectivity, stability, permeability and synthetic feasibility across a conformationally complex and chemically heterogeneous search space. Artificial intelligence (AI) andmolecular simulation address complementary aspects of this problem: AI learns structure–property relationships and explores large candidate libraries, whereas simulation interrogates conformational ensembles, target recognition and membrane-associated behaviour within an explicit physical model. We organize the field around a single, more discriminating question: under which chemical, biological and decision-making conditions does adding molecular simulation to an AI workflow improve peptide discovery outcomes enough to justify its cost? To answer it, we introduce a decision framework linking peptide chemistry and discovery endpoint to the decision beingmade, the uncertainty limiting that decision, the evidence that computation or experiment can provide, the cost of obtaining that evidence and the criterion for proceeding or stopping. Recent advances in biomolecular structure prediction, protein language models, generative design andmacrocycle engineering supply powerful enabling capabilities, but their transfer to short, flexible, cyclic and chemically modified peptides remains unevenly validated. Critically, a structured survey of 15 integrated studies shows that none (0 of 15) included a matched-budget comparison against an AI-only or conventional baseline, a scarcity we treat as a central empirical finding rather than an inconvenience. We outline reporting, benchmarking and prospective-validation standards by which genuine progress should be judged, and define what ‘developable’ must mean at the hit, lead and candidate stages.
papers.title: Integrating artificial intelligence and molecular simulation for peptide discovery: limitations, validation and decision-centered workflows

papers.abstract: Mechanical action of plastic particles on the cell membrane is repeatedly proposed as a route to cellular damage and to depletion of ATP, but the energy budget of that route has never been evaluated. Here I assemble it from four channels and from measured membrane constants. The bending work of engulfing one spherical particle is 8πκ ≈ 503 kBT ≈ 26 ATP and is independent of particle radius. Converting measured tissue burdens (33.7–47 730 µg per gram) into particle numbers gives 6×102 to 7×106 particles per cell; engulfing all of them costs at most 1.8×108 ATP, which is 0.18 s of the cell’s ATP turnover. The membrane-repair channel is bounded from above and cannot reach 10−3 s of turnover at any realistic lesion count. By contrast, a single pore of 5 nm radius admits a diffusion-limited flux of 1.9 × 107 Ca2+ per second, which at the 1:1 stoichiometry of the plasma-membrane Ca2+-ATPase consumes 0.2–2 % of the cell’s entire ATP turnover from one hole, and over 30 s consumes 16 % of the cell’s standing ATP pool. The largest channel, however, does not lie on the demand side at all: the measured fall in mitochondrial ATP production in primary human monocytes exposed to polystyrene particles reaches 50–60 %, equivalent to 5–6×108 ATP per second of lost supply, or 26–31 times one open pore, and unlike a pore it is persistent. The budget implies that the mechanical cost of taking particles in is negligible across the entire measured exposure range, and that the energetic weight sits in the ionic consequence of membrane failure and in the loss of ATP-producing capacity. The decisive mechanical quantity is therefore the probability of failure, governed by the classical wrapping criterion Rmin = √ 2κ/(w − σ), in which the chemical state of the particle surface enters through a single quantity—the adhesion energy w. For membrane tensions of 0.01–0.05 mN m−1 and adhesion energies of the same order there exists a regime of frustrated wrapping that is the mechanical candidate for breach. The adhesion energy of weathered nanoplastic on a membrane has never been measured; together with number-based rather than mass-based dosimetry, these are the two quantities that would close the budget.
papers.title: Uptake is cheap, breach is not: an ATP budget for nanoplastic–membrane interaction

papers.abstract: A proportion of ions travelling through a time-of-flight analyzer inevitably suffer collisions with background gas, resulting in unwanted transmission losses. As collision probability depends upon the ions’ collision cross section, it has been considered that measurement of ion transmission with variation of pressure, or flight path in the case of some multi-reflection analyzers, allows cross section to be determined. A theoretical model is presented, and practical evaluations performed upon a Thermo Scientific Orbitrap Astral mass spectrometer.
papers.title: Collision Cross Section Measurement within a Time-of-Flight Mass Analyzer

papers.abstract: Language models increasingly serve as the reasoning core of agents for chemistry and materials science, where they must interpret molecular structure before planning syntheses or proposing materials. Yet their outputs show only what they say, not what they know. Given a prompt such as “The primary functional group in 1-Fluorobutane (CCCCF) is”, a small general-purpose model may answer “the alkyne group” instead of an alkyl fluoride. The output alone cannot tell whether the model failed to recognize the fluorine or recognized it and failed to say so. We address this by reading the internal representations of five open-source models (a general-purpose base, three chemistry-trained models, and a reasoning-distilled model) on prompts covering 92 molecules and 20 functional groups. Even without chemistry training, the models organize functional groups by chemical family, and they encode chemical differences as consistent directions. The shift from thioether (R−S−R′) to thiol (R−SH), added to ether (R−O−R′), lands nearest alcohol (R−OH). This structure emerges abruptly in the middle layers, where representations shift from tracking the wording of the prompt to tracking the functional group. The base model names the correct functional group in only 58.5% of prompts, the lowest of the five, yet it encodes functional-group families and preserves chemically meaningful patterns. Its errors are mostly failures to answer rather than wrong answers. Functional-group knowledge is structured in the model before it is spoken. Chemistry fine-tuning acts less by adding this knowledge than by reorganizing it, making functional groups rather than prompt wording dominate the representation. These results suggest that evaluating chemical language models through outputs alone can underestimate the chemical information they encode. Representation analysis can distinguish a lack of knowledge from a failure to express it, which matters when choosing or adapting models for chemical agents.
papers.title: Functional-Group Knowledge Is Structured in Language Models Before It Is Spoken

papers.abstract: Protein kinase CK2 acts through two catalytic isoforms, CK2α (A1) and CK2α′ (A2), whose ATP-binding sites differ at only two hinge positions, making isoform-selective inhibition difficult. We tested whether a standard structure-based pipeline can design and rank CK2α′-preferring compounds. In a paired benchmark of 140 compounds measured against both isoforms, none of the five docking-derived criteria, computed with GNINA and convolutional neural network rescoring, correlated with measured selectivity (ρ = −0.19 to +0.12), and for matched pairs differing by a single linker methylene, the scoring reversed the experimental order. The only reliable determinant of preference, a two-carbon linker within the benzo[c][2,6]naphthyridine scaffold, was obtained from the measured activities rather than from any computed score. Molecular-dynamics ensembles of the two isoforms overlapped (0.88 Å between versus 0.72–0.96 Å within), placing the selectivity signal below the resolution of the methods. From an enumerated series, EV043 showed the largest end-point free-energy preference for CK2α′ (ΔΔGb -7.74 kcal/mol), although this value remained sensitive to the starting pose in CK2α, while the non-selective inhibitor CX-4945 was reproduced correctly (+0.08 kcal/mol). Distinguishing CK2α′ from CK2α therefore requires alchemical free-energy methods supported by experimental validation.
papers.title: Design and Benchmarking of CK2α′-Preferring Inhibitors for Huntington’s Disease: The Limits of Structure-Based Isoform Selectivity

papers.abstract: Thietanes, often considered as “oxetane analogs”, offer complementary physicochemical properties and, along with their oxidized derivatives, are attracting increasing interest in medicinal chemistry. Their exploration, however, remains limited, partly due to the restricted availability and structural diversity of appropriate building blocks. The variety of methods available for preparing oxetanes with diverse substitution patterns makes their conversion into thietanes an appealing strategy for both building-block synthesis and late-stage diversification. However, existing O-to-S exchange methods mostly rely on the sulfurization of a 1,3-diactivated intermediate, require forcing conditions, and, importantly, provide very limited access to C(2)-substituted thietanes. We report herein a one-pot, two-step sequence for the mild and efficient O-to-S exchange in oxetanes. The approach relies on an autoactivation via a group-transfer strategy that bypasses the need for diactivated intermediates and provides access to thietanes with unprecedented substitution patterns, thus expanding the range of building blocks available for molecular design. Extensions to the formal O-to-SO, O-to-SO 2 and O-to-S(O)NH exchanges are also reported.
papers.title: Swapping O for S: Converting Oxetanes into Thietanes and their Oxidized Derivatives

papers.abstract: IrO2 is the state-of-the-art catalyst for oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in acid. Previous theoretical investigations are largely based on the (110) surface, with undercoordinated Ircus sites being considered as active centers under reaction conditions, whereas coordinated Irbr sites are considered spectators. Using a combination of density functional theory and ab initio molecular dynamics, we demonstrate that the Irbr sites reconstruct under anodic polarization leading to the formation of single-atom catalyst (SAC)-like centers. These SAC sites exhibit higher activity for OER than Ircus sites and are identified as durable under anodic polarization using a stability analysis based on a Born-Haber cycle. This work provides a framework for understanding how surface reconstruction fundamentally alters the catalytic function of known oxide surfaces by transforming spectator sites into primary active centers for energy conversion and storage.
papers.title: Surface Reconstruction Activates Bridge Sites of Rutile IrO2(110) for Oxygen Evolution Reaction

papers.abstract: The oral absolute bioavailability of 2- to 4-kDa peptides remains near 1%. We constructed a mechanistic Monte Carlo model of a colocalized, reversible permeation-enhancer and efflux-modulator architecture (Dual-Lock) with explicit mass balances and evidence-graded, correlated priors and asked when it would increase bioavailability to at least 4% with predicted reversible epithelial exposure. The arms shared random draws so that the ablations and negative controls isolated each component. Global sensitivity, benefit-risk and falsification analyses, spatial and uptake-constrained transport models, reversibility-endpoint scenarios, observation-conditioned analysis and an out-of-sample evaluation of an optimized design tested robustness. With the reference calibrated to 1.2%, Dual-Lock reached a median of 5.0% at half the enhancer dose and met the target in 45% of draws against 15% for the reference. Confinement caused most of the benefit: a matrix-only control gained 8-fold over peptide alone, from thinning the niche (3.3-fold) and the protease shield, and the gain survived stagnant-layer and solubility limits. In the uptake-constrained model success was 54% (reference 9%); it was 21% to 34% if the reference performs like oral semaglutide, and the upper tail stayed beyond published values. The advantage survived damage at the efficacious concentration but not below it. A credible release-rate optimum added 8 to 12 points out of sample. The transport structure is not independently validated; failure boundaries define the first experiments. Results are conditional on author-assigned priors.
papers.title: Mechanistic Monte Carlo assessment of colocalized permeation enhancement and efflux modulation for oral peptide delivery

papers.abstract: Enantiopure N -heterobiaryls are valuable motifs in medicinal chemistry and asymmetric catalysis. Yet, their atroposelective synthesis via Pd-catalyzed Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling remains challenging as Lewis-basic heterocycles can coordinate to the Pd catalyst and inhibit catalysis. Herein, we report an artificial Suzukiase based on a biotinylated dialkylbiarylphosphine-Pd cofactor embedded within a streptavidin scaffold (Sav). Anchoring of the Pd cofactor minimizes unproductive coordination by N -heterocycles, enabling atroposelective cross-coupling of otherwise challenging heteroaryl substrates. Chemo-genetic optimization was achieved by screening six biotinylated dialkylbiarylphosphine ligands combined with a 400-member double-site saturation Sav library. The resulting Suzukiases catalyze the atroposelective synthesis of diverse axially chiral N -heterobiaryls, including (iso)quinoline, pyridine, pyrimidine, and other pharmaceutically-relevant heterocyclic scaffolds. Stereodivergent access to either atropisomer was achieved through variation of the protein scaffold and the Pd cofactor. This study highlights how an engineered protein environment can minimize substrate-induced catalyst deactivation while providing tunable stereocontrol in asymmetric Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling.
papers.title: Highly tunable artificial Suzukiase catalyzes the atroposelective synthesis of N -heterobiaryls

papers.abstract: Photocatalytic carbonylation has emerged as a powerful approach for the synthesis of carboxylic acid derivatives under mild reaction conditions. However, translating these transformations to industrially relevant scales remains a significant challenge because reaction performance is intrinsically linked to e?icient photon delivery and gas–liquid mass transfer. Continuous-flow processing provides a promising platform to address these limitations, yet its e?ective implementation requires a quantitative understanding of the complex interplay between photon flux, CO mass transfer and reaction kinetics. Herein, the photocatalytic aminocarbonylation of 1-bromo-4-fluorobenzene catalysed by dicobalt octacarbonyl was systematically investigated under flow conditions. A conventional gas-liquid segmented flow regime was found to be limited by gas-liquid mass-transfer, whereas the use of a microstructured reactor incorporating enhanced mixing elements significantly improved mass transfer and resulted in substantially increased reaction rates. Light-intensity studies identified distinct light-limited and lightunlimited regimes. Increasing temperature led to higher reaction rates up to 110 °C, the operational limit of the system. A temperature-dependent induction period was observed, and in situ flow-IR studies revealed the formation and subsequent consumption of an active cobalt carbonyl intermediate. Collectively, these findings provide mechanistic insight into photocatalytic carbonylation in flow and establish practical guidelines for reactor design, process optimisation, and future scale-up of photocatalytic carbonylation technologies.
papers.title: Cobalt Photocatalyzed Carbonylation Reactions in Flow: From Mass-Transfer to Light-Limited Regimes

papers.abstract: Characterization records in organic chemistry link a compound's name with its NMR, high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) and, where available, elemental analysis data. These values are often transferred manually into the Supporting Information (SI). An analysis of Organic Letters SI files found errors of concern in about one in ten compounds with accurate mass data. Here we present checkSI, an open-source tool that checks reporting conventions and consistency among characterization fields. It reads SI files and manuscripts in text-based PDF or Word (DOCX) format. checkSI extracts characterization records in supported formats and checks their completeness. With name-to-structure conversion enabled, it compares the derived molecular formula with HRMS or elemental analysis formulas and NMR signal counts with those expected from the derived structure. Optional DP5q scoring assesses the compatibility of the proposed structure with the reported 13 C NMR data. In 83 published documents, manual review confirmed at least one data inconsistency in 188 of the 2572 recognized compound descriptions (7.3%). Because checkSI runs locally, authors can check unpublished data and correct errors before submission.
papers.title: checkSI: Computer-Assisted Pre-Submission Checking of Characterization Data for Organic Compounds

papers.abstract: Understanding how metal-ligand covalency evolves across the actinide series and compared to the lanthanide series remains a central challenge in f-element chemistry because subtle changes in both the energies and radial extension of the 5f and 6d orbitals can profoundly influence chemical bonding. Here, we employ a redox-active bipyridyl ligand platform to isolate trivalent actinide and lanthanide complexes of the form Cp* 2MIII(tBu2bipy•−) (1-M; Cp* = pentamethylcyclopentadienide; tBu2bipy•− = 4,4′-di-tert-butyl-2,2′-bipyridine radical anion; M = An = Np, Pu; M = Ln = La, Ce, Pr), including the second structually-characterized examples of Np and Pu complexes with organic radicals and the first examples with the metals in the trivalent state. Comparing their structural, electronic, spectroscopic, and electrochemical properties with those of the previously reported Am congener, 1-Am, and lanthanide counterparts 1-Nd and 1-Sm suggests a consistently greater degree of metal-bipyridyl bond covalency in 1-An relative to 1-Ln, which is reflected by shorter M–N distances as well as subtle ligand-based spectroscopic and electrochemical changes. Electronic structure calculations reveal that this enhanced covalency is driven by both increased σ-covalency—primarily involving the 6d orbitals in 1-An relative to 1-Ln—as well as ligand radical-to-metal 5f π-donation, which is absent in 1-Ln. Interestingly, the interplay of these bonding interactions leads to covalency trends that do not decrease monotonically across the actinide series. Instead, computational analyses suggest that while σ-covalency decreases across 1-An, π-covalency reaches a maximum in 1-Am before then decreasing again within a hypothetical curium(III) analog, 1-Cm. This energy-matching driven enhancement of 5f π-covalency amplifies otherwise subtle differences among ions with similar sizes and coordination preferences. More broadly, these orbital-specific trends across 1-An (Np–Cm) underscore the combined roles of spatial overlap and orbital-energy matching in soft donor radicalmediated actinide bonding.
papers.title: A Ligand-Centered Radical Reveals Orbital-Specific Bonding Differences Between Near-Isoradial Transuranium-Actinide and Lanthanide Complexes

papers.abstract: Turning a scientific idea into an experiment often requires researchers to build, configure and repeatedly adapt the laboratory around it. This work demands resources and specialized expertise that can place ambitious experiments beyond reach. Here we introduce a self-evolving laboratory framework that connects computation, physical experiments and AI models through persistent cycles of observation and revision. GPT Astra uses camera observations and physical feedback to adapt robotic actions, digital twins and CAD designs. These changes are retained as reusable skills and infrastructure, allowing the laboratory to develop alongside its scientific tasks. In a fume-hood prototype, GPT Astra identified the need for a beaker holder and storage stand and generated successive designs for on-demand 3D printing. Four holder generations and two stand generations culminated in parts integrated into the robotic workflow with operator assistance. A photoresist campaign proposed by Raven connects this platform to materials fabrication. Exposure to a 405 nm continuous-wave laser in the two-photon polymerization setup produced circular features that survived development; optical microscopy and reduced acrylate-band absorbance in ATR–FTIR support polymerization and qualitative double-bond conversion. An accompanying evaluation protocol relates the retention and transfer of capabilities to the time, cost and expertise needed to establish them. By making laboratory capabilities reusable and adaptable, this approach offers a path towards broader participation in experimental science, empowering researchers to build and extend the tools their ideas require. Project website: https://ai4ssi.github.io/self-evolving-superintelligence-lab/.
papers.title: Self-Evolving Laboratories Through Persistent Digital and Physical Adaptation

papers.abstract: This study compares the alternating-magnetic-field (AMF) heating of Fe3O4-, MnFe2O4-, MgFe2O4-, and SrFe12O19-targeted nanoparticle preparations and of their sequentially silica-modified, aminated, Aufunctionalized, and PEG-treated forms. The compositions are identified by their nominal synthesis precursors. Temperature–time curves and the times required to reach 42 °C were measured in water and in nominally 1% agar phantoms under identical induction-generator settings (132 kHz; 5 kW rated output). Among the untreated preparations, the Mg-labeled series reached 42 °C fastest (145 s in water and 187 s in agar), whereas the Srlabeled series was the slowest (222 and 293 s, respectively). For the Mg-labeled particles, increasing the concentration from 2.5 to 10 mg mL 1 shortened the time to 42 °C from 394 to 77 s in water and from 381 to 112 - s in agar. In water, the aminated Mn-, Mg-, and Sr-labeled samples heated fastest within their respective surfacetreatment series (139, 124, and 209 s), whereas the unmodified Fe-labeled core was fastest within the Fe series (171 s). The PEG-treated specimens exhibited the longest times in all four water-based series. FTIR, SEM, and EDX analyses characterized the successive surface-treatment stages, including the detection of Au after functionalization. Together, these findings clarify how precursor-defined ferrite composition, concentration, surface treatment, and surrounding medium influence magnetic heating under matched apparatus conditions.
papers.title: Comparative Magnetic Heating of Surface-Modified Ferrite Nanoparticles in Water and Agar Phantoms

papers.abstract: This work focuses on developing new earth-abundant metal complexes to be used as eAicient near-infrared (NIR) absorbers and photosensitizers for applications in photocatalysis, bioimaging, and photodynamic therapy. By modifying ligand types coordinated to a W(0) center, we aim to enhance NIR absorption and reduce nonradiative decay pathways in turn. Through collaboration with experimentalists in Dr. Wenfang Sun’s group, they were able to synthesize new W(0) complexes coordinated with four carbonyl’s and one 2-(pyrid-2-yl)(benz)imidazole ligand. Where it was found that these complexes exhibit strong absorption at 580-600 nm spectral range in dichloromethane. Our calculations based on time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) predict that employing diamine-based ligands with varying conjugation positions or pyridocarbazoletype ligands, can significantly redshift the absorption bands into the NIR region up to 700 nm range. Furthermore, replacing 1-2 of the carbonyl groups with pyridines or bipyridines in these complexes extends the spectra from 500-700 nm up to 800-1100 nm and significantly enhances the optical activity of the lowest energy transitions, indicating promising avenues for eAicient emission. It was also found that this overall increase in conjugation on the molecules has increased the amount of mixing in singlet and triplet states in comparison to the 4 carbonyl cases. This indicated promising avenues for eAicient inter-system crossing for applications such as photodynamic therapy. Our results demonstrate a promising pathway toward the rational design of W(0) complexes with optical response in the NIR range, advancing the development of cost-eAective, earth-abundant NIR emitters for application in photocatalysis, bioimaging and photodynamic therapy.
papers.title: Design Of Earth-Abundant W(0) Complexes For Near-Infrared Absorbance Via Ligand Optimization

papers.abstract: We report here a boron-iodane exchange reaction that occurs between aryl boronic acids and 1-hydroxybenzoiodoxoles at extremely mild conditions, that is without the need for using strong Lewis acids or pyrophoric/toxic reagents. Our approach enables selective arylation of a variety of 1-hydroxybenzoiodoxolones with electronically-diverse aromatic boronic acids that is facilitated only by hydrogen-bond donating HFIP, eventually giving rise to a wide range of 1-arylbenzoiodoxolones in good to excellent yields.
papers.title: Hydrogen-Bond Network-Enabled Access to Aryl Benzoiodoxolones via Mild, HFIP-Mediated Boron-Iodane Exchange

papers.abstract: We present an audited measurement record of three phosphine-oxide hosts for deep-blue thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF), with provenance metadata and benchmark tasks for machine learning. A scripted audit converted a 5276-file archive into 1662 files (1639 instrument files and 23 instrument-side fit tables) in ten record families, identifying 44 files stored under incorrect material or medium labels and retaining parsed settings, provenance tiers and quality flags. Colour recomputed from the spectra agrees with instrument reports, while gradient-boosted trees detect Raman-scattering artefacts in single emission spectra with a grouped ROC AUC of 0.92. Within-host interpolation is feasible, but three materials do not support broad property prediction for unseen hosts; the released scripts, manifest and task tables provide a reproducible baseline and a schema for adding materials.
papers.title: An Audited Open Record of Three Deep-Blue TADF Host Materials with Benchmark Tasks for Machine Learning

papers.abstract: Candidozyma auris (formerly known as Candida auris hereafter , C. auris ) is an emerging healthcare associated fungal pathogen. Which is associated with multidrug resistance, environmental persistence, and invasive infections in vulnerable patients. Reduced proneness to established antifungal agents has induced investigation of unorthodox strategies. One approach is antifungal chemosensitization, in which a compound with restricted or no direct antifungal activity enhances the effect of a prevailing antifungal. Preclinical studies have investigated chosen human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) protease inhibitors, including lopinavir, ritonavir, atazanavir, and saquinavir, in cooperation with azoles or amphotericin B against C. auris . Reported findings include in vitro synergy, enhanced fungal killing, and reduced fungal burden in experimental infection models. Intended clarifications include altered drug efflux and changes or modifications in cellular physiology, but the underlying/fundamental mechanisms remain incompletely established. Significantly, limitations include combination and isolate dependent effects, use of selected strains in some infection models, incomplete pharmacokinetic and toxicity data, and no demonstrated clinical efficacy. This Perspective evaluates the evidence and determines the independent validation, exposure response studies, drug interaction assessments, and safety studies needed before clinical application can be considered.
papers.title: Repurposing HIV Protease Inhibitors as Antifungal Chemosensitizers Against Multidrug Resistant Candida auris: Promise, Limitations, and Translational Challenges

papers.abstract: Extending bond-delocalization analysis to correlated one-particle density matrices requires separating fractional occupations from the projector structure underlying determinant-based algorithms. We define the electron density of delocalized bonds (EDDB) by combining bond-orbital projection (BOP) results for cumulative spectral projectors with occupation-gap weights. A structural bound on the raw BOP matrix ensures a positive semidefinite density layer bounded by its parent density. The construction recovers determinant limits, provides consistent spin conventions under stated conditions, and uses an orbital-pair population matrix consistent with the parent orbital populations. An analytic three-center model distinguishes this construction from direct substitution of a fractionaloccupation density into BOP. We further distinguish full-space spectral resolution from subsequent working-space reduction, and numerical occupation grouping and representability preprocessing from the exact definition. The resulting formulation extends EDDB analysis beyond single determinants while making its mathematical properties and limitations explicit. The proposed method is fully implemented in the latest release of runEDDB.
papers.title: Electron Density of Delocalized Bonds from Correlated One-Particle Density Matrices

papers.abstract: The modular synthesis of N-protected L-DOPA(acetonide) derivatives from readily available H-L-DOPA-OH is reported. A consecutive protecting group strategy and a partial hydrogenolytic removal affords H-L-DOPA(acetonide)-OH as key intermediate. Subsequent N-protection provides Fmoc-, Boc-, Cbz-, and Alloc-protected derivatives in excellent yields (95–99%). The key intermediate was further converted into the corresponding N-carboxyanhydride – a building block for polypeptide synthesis.
papers.title: Synthesis of N-Protected L-DOPA(acetonide) Derivatives

papers.abstract: A combined computational -experimental strategy was applied to accelerate the identification of deep eutectic solvent (DES) candidates for CO 2 capture applications. A diverse group of hydrogen bond acceptors (HBA) and hydrogen bond donors (HBD) was selected and screened as potential DES constituents. Subsequently COSMO-RS was used to predict solid-liquid equilibrium (SLE) phase behavior and CO 2 infinite dilution activity coefficients. Based on this screening, selected mixtures were experimentally investigated using differential scanning calorimetry and visual observation of SLE measurements. The experimental results confirmed the formation of stable liquid phases for several systems, including Bet:TEA. In contrast, the Bet:MEA system, predicted to be liquid at ambient conditions, did not form a stable liquid phase experimentally and showed signs of decomposition. For L-tryptophan:MEA, an offset of approximately 2 K between predicted and experimental liquidus temperatures was observed, which is below the experimental uncertainty of 3 K. These findings demonstrate that COSMO-RS is an effective screening tool for identifying promising DES candidates, significantly reducing experimental effort, while highlighting the necessity of experimental validation to account for unexpected effects such as decomposition and metastable behavior. This iterative workflow can offer a time-efficient route for identifying solvents with favorable melting behavior over a broad temperature range and facilitates the development of organic-based DESs for CO 2 capture applications.
papers.title: COSMO-RS screening and experimental solid-liquid equilibrium validation of eutectic solvent candidates for CO2 capture

papers.abstract: Herein, we report the first enantioselective total syntheses of bousigonine A and bisleuconothine B, two heterodimeric monoterpenoid indole alkaloids. The requisite quebrachamine-type and aspidosperma-type alkaloid units were prepared divergently from a common intermediate and subsequently coupled with an eburnan-type alkaloid through bioinspired coupling reactions. The benzyl protecting group on the nitrogen played a crucial role in controlling the regioselectivity of these reactions, enabling selective bond formation at C10. Subsequent chemoselective oxidations of the coupling products furnished the characteristic quinone and N,O-acetal moieties, completing the total syntheses of both natural products. Furthermore, these synthetic studies led to a revision of the absolute configuration of bousigonine A.
papers.title: Enantioselective Total Syntheses of Bousigonine A and Bisleuconothine B

papers.abstract: Acyl-Coenzyme A derivatives are a valuable family of metabolic intermediates with many applications, such as building blocks on biosynthetic routes, protein labeling, or potential therapeutics. However, their synthesis is limited to highly activated molecules (i.e. anhydrides) or carboxylic acids. In this work, we developed two multifunctional heterogeneous biocatalysts, capable of synthesizing acyl-CoA thioesters from primary alcohols or amines using free Coenzyme A via two different stepwise enzymatic cascades. The first enzymatic cascade involves an alcohol and CoA-acylating decarboxylase that catalyzes the oxidative thioesterification of primary alcohols through consecutive oxidation of alcohols to thioesters. In the second cascade, a transaminase enables the deamination of primary amines to aldehydes, which are concurrently oxidized to acyl-CoAs by a CoA-acylating dehydrogenase, using pyruvate as the amine acceptor. In both cases, the redox cofactor (NAD+) regeneration is carried out with a water-forming NADH oxidase that thermodynamically drives the reaction. Both systems exhibited broad substrate scopes, accepting a variety of aliphatic and aromatic primary amines and alcohols. Through rational co-immobilization designs coupled to post-immobilization steps using glutaraldehyde, we achieved highly active and operationally stable multifunctional heterogeneous biocatalysts. Specifically, the system to transform propyl amine into propyl-CoA exhibited excellent performance over five consecutive reaction cycles. Finally, the oxidative thioesterification cascade was successfully coupled with the immobilized promiscuous lipase Novozyme 435, allowing the hydrolysis of the one-pot transformation of alkyl esters into acyl-CoA thioesters. These findings broaden the range of non-activated substrates for acyl-CoA biosynthesis beyond conventional carboxylic acids and create new opportunities for integrating these biocatalysts into CoA-dependent biosynthetic pathways relevant to chemical biomanufacturing and synthetic biology.
papers.title: Biosynthesis of acyl-CoA thioesters from simple amines, alcohols and esters enabled by co-immobilized multi-enzyme systems

papers.abstract: In this work, we explore the effect of small molecular species such as air, iodide, iodine, and triiodide species on the charge transport behavior of fullerene electron transport layers and the concomitant effects on performance and stability of perovskite solar cells. First, we show that without SnOx buffer layers, two-step vapor deposited perovskites have notable losses upon air exposure while spin-coated perovskites have minor losses. We hypothesize that these effects are caused by intrinsic organohalide excess in the CSS perovskite film, leading to an enrichment of mobile halide species such as iodide, iodine, and polyiodides, coupled with a deterioration of C60 charge transport properties. We show that the fill factor losses found in two-step vapor-deposited devices upon air exposure can be induced in spin-coated perovskites by treating their surface with potassium triiodide solutions, further implicating polyhalide species in these losses. Drift-diffusion simulations support the hypothesis that this may be explained by deep electron traps in the C60 formed by polyhalides, while O2 may form shallower traps that have more minor effects on device performance in isolation. Critically, we identify that common ammonium halide surface passivation treatments can lead to performance losses with similar current-voltage signatures during operation in time periods as short as 30 minutes. This may be caused by in situ iodine and polyhalide generation from photolysis of residual lead iodide reducing charge extraction in these solar cells. This work has important implications for the design of stable perovskite solar cells with fullerene charge transport layers.
papers.title: Negative effects of oxygen and halogen species on charge extraction in perovskite solar cells with fullerene electron transport layers

papers.abstract: In this work, we explore the effect of small molecular species such as air, iodide, iodine, and triiodide species on the charge transport behavior of fullerene electron transport layers and the concomitant effects on performance and stability of perovskite solar cells. papers.abstract: Boronic acids have emerged as powerful catalysts for amidation reactions. Based on a previously identified orthobenzoxy phenylboronic acid motif, a systematic structure-activity study was performed. A catalyst library spanning F, Cl, Br, and I substitution on the ortho-benzoxy substituent was synthesized and evaluated as catalysts in amidation reactions. Catalytic activity increased in the order F < Cl < Br < I and followed the substitution pattern ortho < para < meta, with the meta-iodo derivative showing the highest conversion. This systematic comparison established structure-activity relationships within the catalyst library and provides a basis for the design of more efficient amidation catalysts
papers.title: Systematic Evaluation of Halogen Substitution in ortho-Benzoxy Phenylboronic Acid Catalysts for Amidation Reactions

papers.abstract: Identifying low-energy atomic arrangements is central to the design of multicomponent materials such as high-entropy cathodes and perovskites, but the number of possible arrangements grows combinatorially with the number of elements. Calculating each arrangement with density functional theory (DFT) is impractical, and many machine-learning models require relaxed structures that become available only after such calculations. This study presents a site-resolved voxel three-dimensional convolutional neural network (SiVox) that maps each crystallographic site of a known prototype onto a voxel and encodes the occupying element by its physicochemical properties, so that only the site assignment is required as input. The model was evaluated on 1,287,000 configurations of high-entropy Li-rich layered oxides (HE-LLOs) and 18,928 cubic ABX3 perovskites. For HE-LLOs, it reached configurational R2 values of 0.989 for new configurations of training compositions and 0.993 for compositions excluded from training, compared with 0.92–0.93 for descriptor-based models. For perovskites, site assignment alone lowered the formation-energy MAE from 0.432 to 0.133 eV/cell relative to composition descriptors, and screening about 6% of the candidates recovered 90% of the lowest-energy 5%. Relaxed lattice parameters and atomic displacements reduced the error further and mattered most when the most stable of seven anion variants had to be identified. These results indicate that site assignment on a known framework is sufficient to narrow a large candidate space before structural relaxation.
papers.title: Materials Property Prediction with a Site-Resolved Three-Dimensional Voxel Convolution Neural Network

papers.abstract: Parameterized bonded metal sites represent the lowest cost option for molecular dynamics (MD) studies of metalloproteins. However, their quality depends entirely upon the underlying quantum computation and validation. Here, we have asked whether it is possible to generate reliable AMBER force field parameters for a rubredoxin Fe-S4 active site from an extended tight-binding (xTB-family) Hessian. The Hessian derived from a 49-atom cluster was projected using the Seminario method to give parameters for Fe-S and S-Fe-S interactions. The active site was then solvated explicitly, and three 100 ns trajectories were generated. The entire process was performed end-to-end. The trajectories all maintained the protein secondary structure (RMSD Cα mean 1.2-1.6 Å). Two of the trajectories maintained a tetrahedral iron site, while one did not. At around 31.4 ns, the mean Fe-S bond length increased from 2.41 to 2.63 Å, and the deviation from tetrahedral geometry increased from 8.8 to 43.5°. Two cysteine sulfur atoms also approached each other to a bond length of 2.04 Å. None of these issues were identified using global measures. The parameters are reported along with the cause of failure, likely reasons, and missing provenance, meaning this is merely a proof of concept, not a validated force field.
papers.title: From a Tight-Binding Hessian to an AMBER Iron-Sulfur Site: A Rubredoxin Stress Test

papers.abstract: Bottom-up self-assembly of two-dimensional (2D) sheets is rare. We present in situ reaction driven self-assembly for semithroughput synthesis of imine based 2D materials. Easily tuneable molecular structures and reaction kinetics allow for up to seven sheet forming systems.
papers.title: Macroscopic two-dimensional sheets by chemically triggered self-assembly.

papers.abstract: Applying magnetic fields to electrodes has been reported to enhance electrochemical reactions, leading to numerous studies and the hypothesis that externally applied magnetic fields manipulate direct spin exchange at the electrode–electrolyte interface to control reaction kinetics. However, a closer analysis suggests that this mechanism is unlikely to play a significant role, whereas the influence of magnetic gradient forces on ion migration is well established. Here, we provide experimental evidence supporting the latter mechanism for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) on nickel. Moderate magnetic fields increase the electrochemical current density by up to 20%. For pristine samples, the enhancement is both field-and time-dependent. We demonstrate that the magnetic field effect does not arise from direct spin alignment at the electrode surface or from the magnetic domain structure of the underlying ferromagnetic film. Instead, the external magnetic field indirectly enhances the electrochemical performance through magnetic gradient forces that promote the growth of the electrocatalytically active nickel oxyhydroxide surface layer by driving the exsolution of paramagnetic Ni species during the OER. With the structure of the passivation layer of Ni and its evolution being common in similar d-metal (alloy) electrode materials, the magnetic field effect by ion migration is likely to be generally valid.
papers.title: Inverse magneto-ionics enhances oxygen evolution reaction

papers.abstract: C–N axially chiral biaryl amines constitute privileged scaffolds in drug discovery and asymmetric catalysis, yet they remain synthetically challenging due to low rotational barriers and inherent conformational flexibility. While biocatalysis presents an attractive avenue for constructing chiral amines, the lack of mirror-image enzymes has historically limited access to all stereoisomers. Here, we develop an unconventional biocatalytic platform leveraging dynamic kinetic reductive amination to synthesize C–N axially chiral biaryl amines in both enantiomeric forms. Through systematic screening and enzyme engineering, we achieved the synthesis of diverse aryl indole atropisomers with exceptional yields and enantioselectivities (up to 99% yield and 99% ee). Strikingly, we uncovered a unique stereo-divergent behavior wherein a single biocatalyst switches its stereochemical outcome solely by toggling the amine partner between alkylamines and arylamines. Mechanistic investigations using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations unveiled the origins of the high enantioselectivity, the substrate-dependent stereochemical reversal, and the catalytic enhancement imparted by a single point mutation. This study not only provides a robust platform for accessing elusive C–N axial chirality but also exemplifies the synergy between enzyme engineering and computational modeling in achieving stereo-divergent synthesis.
papers.title: Enantio-Complementary Synthesis of Atropisomeric C–N Biaryl Amines via Imine Reductase-Mediated Dynamic Kinetic Resolution

papers.abstract: Microdroplets drive small-molecule activation reactions that are difficult in bulk solution. Recent studies have demonstrated that microdroplets activate inert N2 under ambient conditions to generate multiple nitrogencontaining compounds. However, there are still many controversial issues regarding the transformation of nitrogencontaining compounds in water microdroplets. Here, we combine online high-resolution mass spectrometry on two instrument platforms with 15N and 18O labeling to investigate nitrogen-containing species in pneumatically generated water microdroplets. Ammonium-containing water clusters, nitrite, and nitrate ions were detected on both instruments, whereas a signal assigned to NO+ was observed only on the Agilent 6224 TOF MS. Nebulization with
papers.title: Transformation of Nitrogenous Compounds in Water Microdroplets

papers.abstract: Qualification of plastic pyrolysis oils for steam cracking requires measurements that connect product recovery, composition, and operating performance. This critical narrative review examines 96 selected full-text publications through reconstructed comparisons of analytical coverage, calibration, uncertainty, and material inventories. In individual studies, GC-assigned species represented approximately 11% of total silicon, and olefin estimates differed by 7.4 percentage points despite a pooled coefficient of determination above 0.99. A cracking comparison showed approximately 2.4 times the coke formation rate for an untreated-oil/naphtha blend alongside a small ethylene-yield gain. A claim–evidence framework connects these findings to purification, usableproduct recovery, and feed qualification. Priorities are paired bulk and species measurements, independently measured phase recoveries, matrix-relevant validation, and matched upgrading and cracking tests. The synthesis provides guidance for process assessment while distinguishing results for tested streams and conditions from industrial operating reliability.
papers.title: Analytical Evidence for Assessing Plastic Pyrolysis Oils as Steam Cracker Feedstocks

papers.abstract: Endpoint free-energy calculations combine low computational cost with reasonable accuracy and are widely used to rank protein–ligand affinities, yet describing charge polarization in these calculations remains a challenge. Here we introduce a machine learning/molecular mechanics (ML/MM) framework that incorporates polarizationcorrected mechanical embedding (PCME) and electrostatic embedding (EE) into endpoint calculations, using binding-state-and conformation-dependent ML charges in both the gas-phase energy and polar solvation terms. On a benchmark of 15 targets from the JACS and Merck sets, the PCME and EE routes of ML/MM-PBSA rank affinities better than classical MM-PBSA, raising the median Spearman ρ from 0.216 to 0.343 and 0.329, respectively, at an acceptable computational cost. A charge-source control and the analysis of a representative PTP1B complex show how conformationdependent ML charges resolve asymmetric local electrostatic environments and contribute to the improved ranking of ML/MM-PBSA(PCME) over MM-PBSA. By incorporating charge redistribution into both interaction and solvation energies, this work provides a practical ML/MM endpoint framework for protein–ligand affinity ranking and analysis of the underlying electrostatic contributions.
papers.title: Incorporating Polarization into ML/MM Endpoint Calculations for Protein–Ligand Affinity Ranking

papers.abstract: Facile ion transport in layered battery cathode systems require (11x) terminating facets. However, the facets that provide accelerated transport also amplify deleterious phase transitions and chemical reactions. The coupling between initial intercalant ion content (nominal lithium-ion stoichiometry), ionic mobility and phase transformations along the fastest diffusing facets remain understudied. Here, the coupling is elucidated using electrodeposited highly textured <11x>||(sample normal direction, ND) LiCoO2 (LCO) electrodes with controlled texture, facet presentation, and initial lithium content. Contrary to powdered systems with untextured particles, here we show that minute variations in lithium content drive distinct interphase formation at (110) terminating facets and impact ion diffusivity in cathodes possessing identical <110>IIND texture, indicating the unique importance of control of lithium content in highly oriented systems. While Lithium-poor <110>IIND LCO cathodes provide initial good ion diffusivity, they exhibit accelerated interfacially originated degradation along <110> directions via rapid rocksalt formation. Lithium-rich <110>IIND LCO electrodes exhibit elevated interfacial degradation due to the poorly conducting Li2CO3 on the surface. Lithium-balanced textured LCO electrodes suppress kinetically driven degradation pathways, even at (110) terminating facets, and provide both good ion diffusivity and structural stability. The dual control of lithium content and crystallographic orientation along the fastest diffusing directions provided by the textured electrodeposited cathodes enables deterministic design of energy-dense cathodes with good ion transport kinetics and low surface reactivity, both in thin and thick electrode formats, a combination which is difficult to achieve in untextured slurry systems presenting a range of surface facets.
papers.title: Revealing the role of Li content on the structural stability of textured LiCoO <sub>2</sub> battery electrodes along fast diffusing <11x> directions

papers.abstract: The atomic-level mechanisms governing solvent-driven single-crystal-to-single-crystal (SCSC) topotactic transitions are notoriously difficult to capture, as transient, symmetry-broken intermediates (Z′ > 1) rarely survive structural collapse. Here, we map the complete molecular trajectory of a cooperative solid-state transition within a heavily hydrated di-iron-µ-O-2'-cytidine monophosphate complex, [Fe2(µ-O)(TPA)2(2′-CMP)](ClO4)2·xH2O. By tuning crystallization kinetics, we isolated two distinct solvatomorphic pathways: a thermodynamically stable Z′ = 1 phase and an elusive, kinetically trapped Z′ = 2 interphase. In the reversible Z′ = 1 pathway, the host lattice maintains volumetric invariance across 120–298 K while undergoing a continuous, entropically driven internal hydrogen-bond toggle. Conversely, the metastable Z′ = 2 solvatomorph physically bridges the transition pathway by co-crystallizing incompatible 'open' and 'closed' conformations of two chemical latches. These two chemical latches are the two kind of hydrogen bonds-the cytosine C6-H6 to sugar C5′-hydroxyl oxygen (C6-H6···O5′) and sugar C3′-hydroxyl to phosphate P=O oxygen (O3′-H3′···O=P) contacts within a single asymmetric unit. Fine-sliced variable-temperature X-ray diffraction (150–310 K) reveals that prior to collapse, one of the molecules in the asymmetric unit, acts as a dynamic shock absorber. This molecule reversibly breaking and reforming of its C6···O5′ latch (3.22-3.65 Å) drives a ~ 31° glycosidic swing and bimodal occupancy shifting, while the competing O3′···O=P contact contracts (3.11 to 2.90 Å) to buffer thermal strain. Crossing a 280 K kinetic threshold triggers an abrupt, monotropic 50% volumetric collapse (Z′ = 2 → Z′ = 1), subjecting the merged nucleotide site to severe structural shock before permanently clamping both frustrated latches into a sterically jammed, statically disordered state (C6···O5′at 3.26 Å; O3′···O=P at 2.76 Å). Strikingly, the sheer mechanical force driven by this frustrated latch clamping violently expels few crystallized water near the freezing point of bulk water (273-280 K)- while the collapsed matrix retains permanent microporosity to dynamically resorb and order guest water upon cooling.
papers.title: From Dynamic Frustration to Steric Trapping: The Microscopic Mechanism of a Monotropic Phase Transition

papers.abstract: Agentic and automated drug-discovery workflows increasingly call molecular docking as a black-box subroutine and act on its ranked output, typically from a single run under software defaults. We ask a narrow, operational question: if the same default pipeline is re-run with a different random seed, a slightly displaced search box, or a different input protomer, which decisions-the top-k compounds a downstream agent would advanceactually change? Using AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 on the LIT-PCBA MTORC1 target (PDB 4jsx) with a fixed, score-blind panel of 60 ligands (20 actives, 40 inactives), we predeclared the decision rule and the seed and box-placement perturbation axes against a baseline, added a protomer arm whose selection criterion was amended during execution (disclosed with dates), and compared top-12 decision sets as symmetric differences (exits and entries), Jaccard indices, and binary decision changes, with pose quality checked by PoseBusters against the exact receptor used for docking. A positive control (redocking the co-crystallized ligand, symmetry-corrected RMSD 0.647 Å) validated the setup. Changing only the random seed replaced 3 of 12 top-12 members (6/60 binary decisions changed); a 2 Å box shift along x replaced 2, along y replaced 4; protomer changes at pH 7.0 replaced none. Eight ligands accounted for all flips, and the single PoseBustersinvalid pose was also a recurrent flipper. A threeseed majority-vote consensus cost 3× compute, dropped the invalid recurrent flipper, and still disagreed with every individual run; we report it as a priced mitigation with measured residual disagreement, not as certified stabilization. All results concern decision repeatability only: nothing here establishes that any decision set is correct, and a consensus can stabilize a wrong answer. All code, inputs, checkpoints, and negative results are provided in an accompanying archive prepared for the author; no public release has been made.
papers.title: Decision stability of a default docking pipeline: a seed, box-placement, and protomer audit on LIT-PCBA MTORC1

papers.abstract: Large conjugated molecules feature small gaps between occupied and virtual orbital spaces, which results in complex electronic structure patterns in their low-lying states. These orbital near-degeneracies also challenge quantum chemistry methods. Mixed-reference spin-flip TDDFT (MRSF-TDDFT) and density-matrix-based analyses provide useful tools to interrogate electronic structure in large conjugated molecules. This paper investigates one such family—polyacenes. Following our recent study of the ground and low-lying excited states of all-trans polyenes, we track this evolution from benzene to dodecacene using MRSF-TDDFT and densitymatrix-based analyses. In polyacenes, the ground state acquires diradical character as the number of rings increases, while the doubly excited state dominated by the HOMO2 → LUMO2 configuration drops steeply in energy and falls below the La state between nonacene and decacene. MRSF-TDDFT reproduces the experimental La/Lb crossing, which standard linear-response TDDFT misses, and gives singlettriplet gaps close to high-level wave-function benchmarks and singlet-fission energetics consistent with experiment. The analyses show that La remains predominantly singly excited throughout the series and we attribute the strong decrease in its oscillator strength to the growing diradical character of the ground state. The doubly excited state evolves from mixed character in naphthalene, similar to the 2 1Ag− state of the polyenes, to a nearly closed-shell doubly excited state in pentacene and hexacene, and finally to a state with natural orbital occupations resembling those of the ground state in the longest acenes. From heptacene onward, doubly excited states
papers.title: The Evolution of Electronic Structure in Conjugated Molecules Revealed by Mixed-Reference Spin-Flip Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory and Density-Based Analyses: II. Polyacenes

papers.abstract: Experimental spectroscopy is central to molecular characterization, yet conventional quantitative analysis often compresses rich structural and electronic information into a few calculated observables, leaving much of the experimental context and expert interpretation reported in the literature underused. Here, using molecular 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy as a representative case, we reconstructed more than 300 publications into FeMössDB, a site-resolved dataset containing 502 Fe complexes and 624 Fe sites with linked structural, experimental, and interpretive information. Using FeMössDB, we developed FeMössML for three complementary aspects of Mössbauer analysis: isomer-shift/quadrupole-splitting (IS/QS) prediction, electronic-state interpretation, and analysis of structure–state–spectroscopy relationships. FeMössML reduces IS/QS prediction errors by about 30% relative to a single global density functional theory (DFT) calibration and achieves cross-validated electronic-state accuracies of up to 92%, while correctly assigning several challenging low-valent and electronically delocalized Fe complexes. Feature analysis further recovers established relationships between Mössbauer parameters and oxidation state, spin state, and Fe–L geometry from the literature-scale dataset. FeMössML can also use geometries rapidly generated by Universal Models for Atoms (UMA) or experimental X-ray structures without target-specific DFT hyperfine calculations, reducing wall-clock time by more than three orders of magnitude. More broadly, this work points to a new paradigm for spectroscopic analysis, moving from compound-by-compound quantum-chemical calculation and expert interpretation toward literature-scale reuse of experimental and interpretive data for prediction, interpretation, and systematic relationship analysis.
papers.title: Literature-Scale Mössbauer Data Enable Prediction, Electronic-State Interpretation, and Chemical Insight in Molecular Iron Chemistry

papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of molecular electronic energies is essential yet remains challenging for strongly correlated systems, where conventional coupled-cluster (CC) methods break down.
