Here we present a generalized valence bond-based block-correlated coupled‑cluster (GVB-BCCC) framework to overcome this limitation. In contrast to standard CC approaches built upon a single-determinant reference, our method employs a multi‑determinantal GVB reference paired with a cluster operator that consistently captures both static and dynamic electron correlation effects, while retaining computational efficiency comparable to single-reference CC theory. With its O ( N ⁷) scaling, GVB‑BCCC delivers chemical accuracy for global potential energy surfaces, reaction barriers, and singlet‑triplet gaps across diverse biradicals and transition-metal complexes. GVB-BCCC thereby enables routine, black-box quantum-chemical predictions for a wide variety of strongly correlated systems, ranging from transition-metal catalysts and organic radicals to functional molecular materials.
papers.title: Bringing coupled‑cluster theory to the strong-correlation frontier

papers.abstract: The increase in anti-PEG antibodies (APAs) as well as PEG-related adverse effects have questioned the benefits of PEGylated nanotherapeutics. Growing awareness of the safety and efficacy of PEGylation has prompted research into countermeasures, including alternative polymers. Among these, randomized PEG (rPEG) was established as a fundamentally new approach that preserves the polyether structure while preventing antibody recognition through isomerization. Here, rPEG was incorporated into polymeric micelles (PMs) for immunodrug delivery to assess its suitability as a PEG replacement. Amphiphilic rPEG polycarbonate block copolymers were synthesized via chain extension using rPEG macroinitiators with primary hydroxy end groups. The respective PMs self-assembled via solvent-exchange evaporation, encapsulating the hydrophobic TLR7/8 agonist CL075 as the immunodrug. rPEG-based PMs demonstrated size distributions and encapsulation efficiencies similar to those of PEG. In vitro assays confirmed that rPEG-PMs had comparable cellular uptake, no cellular toxicity, and similar drug-delivery efficiencies to PEG-PMs. Notably, competitive ELISAs revealed markedly decreased antigenicity of rPEG-PMs towards backbone- and end group-specific APAs. In a fiveday biodistribution study, rPEG-PMs showed whole-body and organ distribution patterns comparable to mPEG-PMs, as would be expected for a stealth polymer. Strikingly, despite the immunostimulatory payload, serum ELISA after a single dose detected anti-rPEG IgM in one of five mice, compared with anti-PEG IgM in three of five mice receiving mPEG-PMs, suggesting lower immunogenic potential for rPEG-PMs, though this remains to be confirmed in repeat-dose studies. Overall, these results position rPEG as a highly promising alternative to PEG for polycarbonate-based PMs and next-generation nanotherapeutics.
papers.title: Randomized PEG-Based Polycarbonate Micelles with PEG-like Stealth Properties and Biodistribution

papers.abstract: The emergence of generative AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini is reshaping research, education, and industry. Recent workforce data indicate a widening gap between declining junior-level opportunities and rising demand for senior-level expertise, underscoring the urgent need to adapt undergraduate chemistry curricula to prepare students for an AI-enabled workforce. To address this challenge, we designed a series of Python-based laboratory experiments for General Chemistry that integrate generative AI with instructor guidance to enhance student learning. The modules focus on (1) using AI tools to support conceptual understanding, (2) applying AI-assisted coding for data visualization and analysis, and (3) introducing machine learning workflows to solve real-world chemistry problems. All activities are implemented in Google Colaboratory, a cloud-based programming platform now integrated with Gemini, which helps students, particularly those without prior programming experience, complete coding tasks with step-by-step instructor guidance. We compare student attitudes toward the use of AI and programming at the beginning and end of the semesters, observing a more positive attitude toward AI use and increased confidence in programming. To demonstrate scalability, three PhD graduate students, two of whom had no prior programming background, successfully led the laboratory sessions using these AI-supported materials, confirming that instructors across a wide range of computational skill levels can teach the experiments. This work demonstrates how generative AI can create more prosperous and equitable learning experiences, equipping students with transferable skills essential for research and industry careers, as well as the evolving STEM workforce.
papers.title: Integrating Generative AI and Data Science into General Chemistry Laboratories

papers.abstract: Oyster-shell powder is promoted as a low-carbon cement substitute, but joint carbon and durability benefits are usually asserted rather than tested. This paper asks when shell-derived concrete (shell replacing cement) delivers a carbon cut with non-inferior service life relative to ordinary Portland cement (OPC) concrete. A coupled hydration–transport–damage–carbon model is run through paired Monte Carlo analysis of a pavement, a dam and a marine culvert. Published data reject the original inert-filler strength model. An effective strength-efficiency coefficient k_f calibrated on one scallop-shell dataset does not generalize to independent oyster-shell data (mean absolute error 0.12 against 0.15 for the inert model; root-mean-square error 0.17 against 0.15), and k_f ranges from -0.40 to 1.36 across four studies, so the primary results use a pooled random-effects distribution. At 25% replacement and constant water-to-binder ratio the median carbon change is −21% with strength 0.88 of OPC; with strength matched it is −15% (P10–P90 −22 to +10%). In the primary configuration (pooled strength-only k_f, sampled diffusivity mapping, OPC reference) the probability of a carbon cut of at least 5% with non-inferior life is at most 0.21 for the pavement, 0.14 for the dam and 0.03 for the marine culvert, and zero against a 50% slag blended cement; other, equally unmeasured transport assumptions give 0.18 to 0.68 for the pavement. All probabilities are conditional scenario results, not empirical probabilities for real infrastructure, and the study is a falsifiable computational screening framework, not a validated service-life model.
papers.title: A Coupled Chemo-Mechanical and Life-Cycle Framework for Oyster-Shell-Derived Cementitious Materials in Aggressive Infrastructure Environments

papers.abstract: Host mobilities are usually quoted from one technique without saying what that technique can actually pin down. Using single-carrier devices of three deep-blue phosphine-oxide hosts, we credit impedance spectroscopy (IS), admittance and steady-state current–voltage (J–V ) data each with what they can fix. Documented rules for point selection, dispersion and transport onset make the published IS mobilities reproducible. Quality-gated admittance pins down the electrostatic state of the films: its ac conductance exceeds the dc conductance of the corresponding device types by up to several hundred times, and no transit feature is resolved in the clean band. Gated J–V sweeps locate a high-slope onset consistent with trap filling under stated assumptions, and the spread between successive sweeps of one device sets a built-in check before hosts are ranked. The result is a constraint map that assigns each technique its role and makes host-transport claims auditable.
papers.title: Impedance, admittance or current–voltage? What each measurement really tells about charge transport in deepblue hosts

papers.abstract: Deep-blue thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) OLEDs stand or fall on their host, yet hosts are still chosen from a handful of single numbers: triplet energy, singlet–triplet gap, frontier levels, glass transition and carrier mobility. We compiled these descriptors for sixteen hosts and cohost components from six chemical families, tracing the source, method and condition behind every value, and find that most are protocol-dependent observables rather than material constants: published triplet energies of one molecule differ by up to 0.12 eV, and five analyses of the same devices place one host’s electron-to-hole mobility ratio anywhere between 0.77 and 3.1. A one-protocol calculation of 50 molecules shows that computed-gap rankings depend on functional choice and require validation against measurement. We review how exciplex-forming, mixed and sensitised hosts share the host’s tasks and what limits operational stability, and propose a minimum reporting standard and a roadmap toward protocol-locked, multi-descriptor host selection.
papers.title: Beyond single numbers: how to choose host materials for deep-blue TADF OLEDs

papers.abstract: Optical gaps, Urbach energies, oxidation potentials, surface correlation lengths, diffraction order and thermal transitions are used to rank organic semiconductor films, yet each number is the output of an analysis whose discretionary steps are rarely fixed. Here a protocol card is introduced in which every descriptor is extracted by a locked rule and accepted only if it passes a stated test; otherwise it is reported as “not determined”. Each rule is stress-tested against the choices it fixes. Applied to the archived raw data of three deep-blue phosphine-oxide host films, a free choice of fit window lets the Urbach energy of the same spectra range from 0.21 to 0.94 eV, whereas the locked rule returns 0.22–0.24 eV for all three hosts on glass. The same protocol dependence appears in onset versus peak oxidation potentials, AFM correlation lengths, diffraction baselines, the mass basis of weight-loss temperatures and the functional used for computed orbital energies. Ten locked rules with their stress tests make every reported value auditable and every missing value explicit, and propose a reporting protocol for molecular semiconductor films.
papers.title: Same Raw Data, Different Numbers: Locked Analysis Rules Make Film Descriptors of Organic Semiconductors Reproducible

papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) can implement scientific software, but useful development also requires executable comparisons, inspectable results and a record of scientific decisions. This case study examines the tooling that enables semi-autonomous electronic-structure software development under expert direction. VIBE-QC supplies molecular and periodic calculations; vibe-scheduler queues and manages calculations across clusters and a fleet of workstations; vibe-viewer and the Quantum Visualization Format (QVF) connect numerical outputs to portable inspection and reproducible figures. Retained development records illustrate how these tools preserve failed attempts, distinguish changes in physical conventions from implementation errors, and separate measured differences from expert-selected acceptance criteria. Publication-specific calculations were run with VIBE-QC 0.18.x and use formaldehyde to connect controlled numerical comparisons with visual inspection; diamond and lithium hydride provide periodic Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof (PBE) examples with explicit convergence checks. The expert sets the physical problem, selects diagnostic controls and interprets the evidence; AI agents implement and execute those tasks. The resulting account identifies practical requirements for sustained AI-assisted scientific development. It establishes a traceable process within one project, without claiming autonomous scientific judgment or a measured productivity advantage.
papers.title: vibe-qc: expert-directed agentic engineering for scientific software development

papers.abstract: Deep-blue host design relies on a textbook rule: join the donor and the phosphine-oxide acceptor through a meta-phenylene link to break conjugation and keep the triplet energy high. Tested against experiment, the rule alone does not explain the measured photoluminescence-yield ordering. In a prespecified test on 36 deep-blue emitters, none of the tested radiative descriptors passes all four film-yield ranking criteria, and the meta-linked S1 host and the para-linked S4 host have overlapping apparent radiative-rate brackets yet differ 18-fold in apparent non-radiative rate. One calibrated excited-state protocol, applied to the hosts, their all-meta isomers and emitter pairs, shows that a meta break raises the vertical triplet energy and narrows the singlet–triplet gap, but the gain is lost on relaxation, and the vibronic displacement of the S1 state follows the measured yields. Screens for deep-blue hosts should therefore rank link positions by relaxed triplet energies, estimate non-radiative loss, and read a 1-eV computed gap as a property of locally excited states rather than as evidence against delayed fluorescence.
papers.title: The Meta-Link Rule Revisited: Relaxed Triplets and Non-Radiative Loss Decide Deep-Blue Phosphine-Oxide Hosts

papers.abstract: Deep-blue thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) materials are screened by a single figure of meritquantum yield, singlet–triplet gap, colour shift or activation energy—on the assumption that a material robust under one stress is robust under others. Here we show that this assumption fails. For three related phosphineoxide hosts, the host whose emission colour moves least on heating is the one whose colour moves most when the excitation wavelength is changed: an 8-to 17-fold reversal, read directly from instrument chromaticity coordinates. Solvent response, spectral dimensionality, quantum yield and delayed-fluorescence kinetics each add a different ordering, and no host is best on every axis. A thermal screen would therefore advance precisely the most excitationsensitive material. We replace the stability score with a four-axis descriptor vector—environment, excitation, temperature and time—that keeps each vulnerability visible and lets the intended application decide which tradeoff is acceptable, before a material is committed to devices.
papers.title: Colour-Stable When Heated, Colour-Shifting When Excited: Deep-Blue TADF Hosts Need Vector, Not Scalar, Screening

papers.abstract: Electrocatalytic processes are essential for a sustainable global economy, yet conventional catalyst synthesis often relies on hazardous reagents and insulating binders that impede performance. Here, microbial extracellular electron transfer for nanoparticle synthesis is integrated with the controlled pyrolysis of microbial monolayers to generate nanoparticle-embedded carbon electrodes. Surface immobilization of Shewanella oneidensis using DNA "Velcro" yields uniform single-microbe-thick layers that are readily patterned and converted into conductive, turbostratic carbon films at temperatures between 800 °C and 1,100 °C. These bio-derived films exhibit progressive graphitic ordering and reach a minimum sheet resistance of 1.49 kΩ/sq, approaching the performance of pyrolyzed synthetic photoresists. Moreover, by leveraging the intrinsic biosynthetic capabilities of S. oneidensis, 3-5 nm palladium nanoparticles are formed directly on the cell surface and seamlessly integrated into the carbon matrix upon pyrolysis. These composites reduce the hydrogen evolution reaction overpotential by 100 mV. This bottom-up bioengineering approach is anticipated to enable the sustainable, programmable fabrication of next-generation electrocatalysts for diverse energy conversion applications.
papers.title: Microbial Pyrolysis for the Sustainable Synthesis of Nanoparticle-Embedded Carbon Electrocatalysts

papers.abstract: Literature-derived results on reverse water–gas shift (RWGS) catalysts contain extensive information about catalyst design, yet their fragmentation makes systematic, data-driven exploration difficult. Here, we establish a framework that connects a curated RWGS literature dataset to interpretable machine-learning (ML) models and a flexible catalyst-search algorithm. We compiled 607 experimental records from 42 publications on supported metal and metal oxide catalysts evaluated at 300–450 °C, integrating catalyst compositions, preparation and reaction conditions, and CO yields. By systematically comparing nine regression algorithms and nine input representations, we obtained mean cross-validated test R2 values of 0.80, 0.73, and 0.58 for models optimized for the full, 300 °C, and 400 °C datasets, respectively. SHAP analysis identified compositional and experimental features contributing to model predictions, while leave-one-out validation exposed substantial prediction errors in some literature records. In offline sequential-search simulations repeated 100 times, ML-guided search identified high-yield literature entries more efficiently than random selection. Importantly, our newly developed Local-search algorithm jointly explored elemental combinations, loadings, support materials, and experimental conditions without exhaustive enumeration, generating candidates beyond the compositions represented in the training data. The 300 °C search favored Pt–Na/ZrO2-containing candidates, whereas Pd–Na/CeO2-containing candidates predominated at 400 °C. Although these predictions await experimental validation and some violate RWGS equilibrium constraints, this integrated framework provides a reusable data resource and a practical route from accumulated literature knowledge to testable catalyst-design hypotheses.
papers.title: Construction of a Curated Literature Dataset and Machine Learning-Guided Exploration of Supported Metal Catalysts for Low- to Intermediate-Temperature Reverse Water–Gas Shift Reaction

papers.abstract: Diphenylacetylene (DPA) rotates almost freely around the acetylene axis with rotation mainly restricted by steric repulsion or covalent tethers. We report intermeshed diphenylacetylenes, in which bent π-conjugated units attached to DPA termini cause two donor–acceptor pairs to overlap with each other on opposite sides of the axis. Density functional theory calculations showed that a twisted, stacked conformation with a 36–40° dihedral angle was the most stable for all four molecules. The estimated P/M interconversion barriers (12.8–21.4 kcal/mol) increased with donor and acceptor strength. Upfield shifts in 1H NMR spectra and long-wavelength absorption bands assigned to intramolecular charge-transfer transitions indicated that the stacked conformation predominated in solution. Because rotation was restricted rather than fixed, the molecules exhibited dynamic axial chirality. In a derivative bearing pyridyl groups as acceptors, acid–base interaction with (+)- or (–)-camphorsulfonic acid biased the P/M equilibrium and gave mirror-image induced circular dichroism spectra.
papers.title: Intermeshed Diphenylacetylenes with Axial Rotation Restricted by Intramolecular Donor–Acceptor Interactions

papers.abstract: Language models are increasingly used as research assistants in chemistry, but their quantitative work insurfactantscience hasnotbeen measured.We introduce Surfactant-Toolkit, an MIT-licensed Python library and Model Context Protocol (MCP) server with 123 validated tools for micellization, mixed micelles, adsorption, emulsions, micelle structure and transport,andSurfBench-200,200graduate-levelquestionswhosereferenceanswersare computed by the toolkit and graded field by field by deterministic scripts. Without tools, five frontier models passed 52.5% to 66.0% of the questions; with the toolkit, the four models run in both conditions passed 92.0% to 98.5% (exact McNemar p < 0.0001 for each), and the open-weightDeepSeek (92.0%) outscored every modelwithouttools.Remaining failures shifted from wrong magnitudes tochoices ofmodelorconvention:toolslargely remove calculation errors, not errors of judgement. Asked the same questions again, every model changed some answers and at least once stated something the data did not support. Used for new findings, the toolkit and two augmented models produced five results on seven research problems that we could not find in the literature. Used for error finding, it showed that five recent papers each contain a value or conclusion that does not follow from their own printed data, from a reversed interaction-parameter sign to a physically impossible molecular area; two frontier models given the same values recomputed nearly all of these without tools but called an undetermined result contradicted. All questions, transcripts, graders and code are released, with SurfactantKit-Studio, a local application for researchers. 1. Introduction Surfactantsunderpindetergency,enhancedoilrecovery,emulsionpolymerisation, pharmaceutical solubilisation and personal-care formulation.[1] The routine computations of thefield,suchasextractingaCMC from tensiometryorconductivitydata,[2,3] mixedmicellethermodynamics,counterion binding,Gibbs and Szyszkowskiadsorption analysis
papers.title: Surfactant-Toolkit and SurfBench-200: an open computation toolkit and a benchmark of tool-augmented language-model reasoning in surfactant science

papers.abstract: Aliphatic alcohols were installed with proposed leaving groups for reaction with well defined, 1,3-diketiminesupported (NacNac)iron(I)-(η6-PhMe) metalloradical, indicating a redox-active 2-isoquinolinyl ether substrate to undergo reductive homolytic C(sp3)–O bond cleavage concomitant with alkyl radical generation as determined by PBN spin trap. The optimal isoquinolinyl ether was employed as substrate in Kumada cross-coupling catalyzed by 10 mol% (NacNac)iron(II) chloride, yielding the deoxygenated, arylated product following homolytic C(sp3)–O β-scission. Hexenyl radical clock experiments and catalyst speciation determined by 19F NMR spectroscopy were consistent with intermediacy of alkyl radicals captured by (NacNac)iron(II)–monoaryl resting state, accessing deoxygenated cross-coupled products derived of naturally occurring aliphatic alcohols such as β-sitosterol and isosorbide.
papers.title: Redox-Active Leaving Group Enables the Deoxygenative Arylation of Unactivated Aliphatic Alcohols by Thermal, Homogeneous Iron(I)-Catalyzed Cross-Coupling

papers.abstract: Extending transition-metal-like organometallic redox chemistry to indium remains a challenge in molecular main-group chemistry. Here, we report a zwitterionic indylene supported by an anionic bis(N-heterocyclic carbene)borate ligand that displays diverse redox reactivity. Computational and structural analyses reveal a relatively narrow HOMO–LUMO gap together with a stabilizing arene–In interaction involving a vacant indium p orbital, endowing the In(I) centre with complementary donor and acceptor character. This ambiphilicity is expressed experimentally through coordination and reactivity, with a broad range of bond-forming and redox processes, including cycloaddition and the direct oxidative addition of unactivated aryl–halogen bonds. These results expand the accessible reactivity of molecular In(I) and establish bis(NHC)borate ligands as a powerful platform for the development of indium redox organometallic chemistry.
papers.title: A Zwitterionic Indylene with Ambiphilic Redox Reactivity

papers.abstract: A Pourbaix diagram maps which species of an element (metal, ion, oxide or hydroxide) is thermodynamically stable in water as a function of potential and pH, at fixed temperature, pressure and composition. Constructing one requires the Gibbs energies of formation of the participating phases and species. Obtaining reliable values, however, remains difficult: competing phases and species can differ by only a few kilojoules per mole, while published compilations may disagree and are not always freely reusable. Density functional theory (DFT) offers an alternative, but its errors can exceed the energy differences that determine phase stability. We introduce pourbase, an open, source-linked thermodynamic database with a Python package and desktop application for constructing Pourbaix diagrams. Individual reported values, their provenance and a configurable selection policy are accessible and configurable to users even while the database expands as agent-guided literature searches collect new data. We show that replacing a single formation energy can substantially change a predicted stability region and that established thermodynamic compilations can yield conflicting oxide stability boundaries. By making thermodynamic data accessible, traceable, and revisable, pourbase enables reproducible Pourbaix diagrams built directly from experimental evidence, as well as a platform for benchmarking computed values, as we demonstrate for the Materials Project, against experimental values. Ultimately, accurate phase stability predictions need not depend on increasingly complex models, but on getting the formation energies right.
papers.title: Formation Energy is All You Need

papers.abstract: The controlled adsorption of DNA origami nanostructures (DONs) at oxides surfaces is an important step in many applications, ranging from lithographic patterning to sensor fabrication. It is usually facilitated by divalent cations, which screen electrostatic repulsion between the DONs and the surface and may even form salt bridges that firmly immobilize the adsorbed DONs. Here, we investigate DON adsorption at TiO2(110) surfaces mediated by Mg2+, Ca2+, and Sr2+. DON surface coverage is found to increase with cation species in the order Mg2+ < Ca2+ < Sr2+, while cation adsorption at the TiO2(110) surface follows the opposite trend. At the same time, these three cations interact differently with DNA. While Mg2+ undergoes strong coordinative binding with the backbone phosphates, Sr2+ shows weaker binding and forms a large ion cloud around the DNA duplex. Exposing the adsorbed DONs to EDTA leads to the chelation of the bound cations and thus to rapid DON denaturation. However, even for complete DON denaturation, the denatured scaffold remains adsorbed at the TiO2 surface, which suggests that electrostatic repulsion between DON and the surface is overcompensated by additional attractive interactions such as van der Waals interactions. Our results thus provide new insights into the complex interplay of cation-DNA, cation-surface, and DNA-surface interactions and their roles in DON adsorption at TiO2 surfaces, which may result in surprising and counterintuitive behaviors.
papers.title: Influence of divalent cations on the adsorption of DNA origami nanostructures at TiO2 surfaces

papers.abstract: Carboxylates are ubiquitous additives in Cp*Co III -catalyzed C–H functionalization, yet their influence on catalyst speciation and catalytic performance remains poorly understood. Herein, we demonstrate that carboxylate choice can markedly improve reaction efficiency, particularly for substrates bearing weakly coordinating directing groups. Combining high-throughput experimentation (HTE) and reaction optimization, we identified mesitoic acid (MesCO 2 H) as an effective additive for hydrogen isotope exchange (HIE), outperforming conventional carboxylates. We then examined the influence of mesitoate and acetate on Cp*Co III speciation, isolating the corresponding dinuclear complexes. Catalytic studies in HIE revealed that both dimers are catalytically competent, but their activity depends on carboxylate identity and substrate coordination ability, with the mesitoate derivative exhibiting higher activity toward weakly coordinating substrates. We also report the first crystal structure of a direct analogue of the mononuclear κ 2 -carboxylate Cp*Co III species proposed as a putative intermediate prior to C–H activation. The isolated mesitoate-bridged dimer enabled C–H deuteration of pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals and proved effective beyond HIE in three distinct C–H functionalizations. Together, these findings highlight that carboxylate selection can play a decisive role in fine-tuning Cp*Co III catalysis, offering new opportunities for rational reaction optimization. KEYWORDS: Cp*Co III catalysis; C–H activation; catalyst speciation; carboxylates
papers.title: Exploiting Carboxylate Effects to Enhance Cp*Co <sup>III</sup> -Catalyzed C–H Functionalization

papers.abstract: Bioelectrochemical systems, in which electroactive microbes transfer electrons across biological-abiotic interfaces, represent a vital technology for sustainable energy production, chemical synthesis, and environmental remediation. However, these systems are constrained by a two-dimensional design paradigm, with reactors achieving power densities 10–100-times lower than theoretical limits because conventional architectures restrict electron transfer to a single layer at the electrode surface. Here, we establish quantitative design rules that govern three-dimensional bio-electrochemical function driven by small-molecule electron transfer mediators. Through integrated theory, simulation, and engineered biofilm validation, we identify two distinct scale-dependent transport regimes: a macroscopic regime where bulk mediator availability governs active layer expansion and a microscopic regime where microbial packing geometry controls local redox cycling, both of which are fundamentally constrained by mass transport. We validate these scaling laws experimentally using agarose-encapsulated Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 and demonstrate that rational mediator loading and cellular packing can elevate current densities beyond 0.5 A m-2, exceeding two-dimensional performance ceilings. These design principles provide a generalizable blueprint for engineering high-performance biocatalytic systems and offer researchers studying natural biofilms a mechanistic framework to decode internal transport architecture.
papers.title: Multi-Scale Continuum Modeling of Mediated Electron Transfer in 3D Living Bio-Anodes

papers.abstract: Language-model agents can coordinate computational drug discovery, but adapting a campaign to new evidence requires scientific software that supports flexible workflows, consistent modeling, and continuity across research sessions. Here we present ETALON, a harness that equips a general-purpose coding agent with an integrated environment for computer-aided drug design. Three independently usable systems supply its scientific operations: MolQuarry for chemical and biological evidence, MolCascade for molecular preparation, screening, and docking, and PRISM for molecular generation and physical modeling. Each exposes configurable procedures with explicit scientific requirements, so the host can revise its research strategy while retaining consistent preparation and evaluation practices. Operations registered with a common execution layer are checked before dispatch, and their outputs carry separate records of completion, verification, and admission, so that an incomplete computation is not recorded as an unfavorable molecular result. A persistent research graph links evidence, judgments, experiments, and results across sessions, and candidate method revisions are compared with frozen baselines under criteria declared in advance.
papers.title: ETALON: Verified Execution and Persistent Research Memory for Agentic Computer-Aided Drug Design

papers.abstract: Colloidal 2H-MoSe 2 nanosheets combine solution processability with electronic properties attractive for photocatalytic water splitting, yet the electrochemical stability of the excited state remains poorly understood. We combine potential-modulated absorption spectroscopy and complementary electrochemical methods with transient absorption spectroscopy to investigate charge injection and excited-state dynamics in few-layer 2H-MoSe 2 nanosheet films. We determine the electron affinity, ionization potential and exciton binding energy and predict an overpotential of +0.6 V for the photocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction. Prolonged exposure to electrochemical operating conditions reduces the lifetime of the excited state, which scales with the overpotential, and which is particularly pronounced under anodic conditions. Our work establishes absorption spectroelectrochemistry as a powerful probe of colloidal transition-metal dichalcogenides and identifies solution-processable 2H-MoSe 2 nanosheets as promising photocathode components for S-scheme heterostructures.
papers.title: Impact of Electrochemical Doping on the Excited State Decay of 2H-MoSe <sub>2</sub> Nanosheets

papers.abstract: Peptidyl-prolyl cis–trans isomerase NIMA-interacting 1 (Pin1) plays vital biological roles in vivo and has been studied as a therapeutic target for a variety of human diseases. Covalent inhibitors represent the mainstream strategy in current Pin1 drug discovery, however, existing covalent molecules still rely on known affinity scaffolds or direct screening. Herein, we developed an innovative cascade DNA-encoded library (DEL) strategy that integrates photo-crosslinking with covalent targeting, enabling the de novo design of novel Pin1 covalent inhibitors. Photo-crosslinking DEL (PDEL) selection was first used to identify low-affinity binding fragments. These fragments then served as the beginning for covalent focused DELs (Co-FDEL) construction. Finally, covalent DEL selection led to the identification of two hits, LWH-1 and LWH-2, which covalently modify Pin1 at Cys113, with IC50 values of 447.4 nM and 273.7 nM. This strategy facilitates the rational evolution of low-affinity fragments to potent covalent inhibitors, offering an accelerated pathway for targeting challenging proteins.
papers.title: From Photo-crosslinking to Covalent: A Cascade DNA-Encoded Library Strategy for Pin1 Inhibitor Discovery

papers.abstract: Odor emissions from cannabis cultivation have been described as “skunky”, a sensory characteristic recently associated with the compound 3-methylbut-2-ene-1-thiol (3MBT). However, the biosynthetic origin of this key odor-active compound in Cannabis sativa remains unknow. This study investigated the occurrence of the S-cysteine and S-glutathione conjugates of 3MBT (Cys-3MBT and GSH-3MBT) in CBD- and THC- dominant cannabis flowers and proposed them as possible precursor of the odor-thiol 3MBT. Both conjugates were identified for the first time in Cannabis sativa in CBD and THC cultivars by HPLC-QTOF-MS/MS and confirmed with reference standards. In vitro release experiments showed that GSH-3MBT generated 3MBT under moderate thermal conditions, whereas both conjugates released substantial amounts of 3MBT during fermentation with S.cerevisiae. Cys-3MBT and GSH-3MBT were quantified by HPLC-MS/MS at two stages of flower maturation in both cultivars, showing a decrease in their quantity during maturation. The THC-cultivar sample contained higher levels of both precursors at the earliest stage of maturation (Cys-3MBT: 13.01± 0.061 mg/kg ; GSH-3MBT 10.98 ± 0.14 mg/kg) than the CBD-cultivar (Cys-3MBT: 0.85 ± 0.057 mg/kg ; GSH-3MBT 2.96 ± 0.044 mg/kg) sample. Higher levels of the precursors in the THC-cultivar were also correlated with higher levels of free 3MBT (1.79 ± 0.19 mg/kg in THC and 0.075 mg/kg in CBD). These findings identify Cys-3MBT and GSH-3MBT as potential precursors of 3MBT and provide the basis for elucidating the biochemical origin and evolution of this odor-active thiol during Cannabis sativa maturation.
papers.title: Insights into the formation of 3-Methyl-2-butene-1-thiol in Cannabis sativa flowers through the identification of its glutathionylated and cysteinylated precursors

papers.abstract: M-type barium and strontium hexaferrites are the most widely produced permanent-magnet materials, and their structural and magnetic properties are commonly tuned by cationic substitution. The experimental data on doped hexaferrites are dispersed over hundreds of articles and reported with heterogeneous notation, units and descriptors. Here we present HexaMagDB, a manually curated dataset of 4388 records extracted from 662 peer-reviewed articles on doped Ba-and Sr-based M-type hexaferrites. Each record corresponds to one experimentally characterized sample and contains the chemical formula, the dopant elements, their amounts and substituted sites, the synthesis method and procedure, the calcination and sintering conditions, the lattice parameters, crystallite and particle sizes, phase purity and secondary phases, and the saturation and remanent magnetizations, coercivity, squareness ratio, Curie temperature and magnetocrystalline anisotropy field and constant, together with the measurement temperature and maximum applied field. The dataset covers 48 dopant elements in 251 combinations. An interactive online tool for visualization and navigation through the data has also been developed. This dataset can serve as a comprehensive benchmark for predicting the magnetic properties of doped hexaferrites.
papers.title: Dataset of magnetic properties, structure and synthesis of doped barium and strontium M-type hexaferrites

papers.abstract: Microbial metabolism provides critical ecosystem functions, yet characterizing microbial metabolic activity in environmental systems remain challenging. Since phosphoryl-transfer reactions are central to energy metabolism, biosynthesis, and metabolic regulation, they have been proposed as a proxy for overall metabolic activity. Some phosphoryl-transfer reactions are known to contribute to the oxygen isotope fractionation between phosphate and water, leaving an isotopic signature of metabolic activity. Although these reactions are well characterized at the level of individual enzymes, their dynamics within the phosphoryl-transfer network remain difficult to resolve, limiting their use for assessing metabolic activity in the environment. Here, we present an 18 O stable isotope labeling-based metabolomics workflow to trace phosphoryl-transfer reactions in Escherichia coli . Cells are grown in labeled medium containing ∼10 atom% H 2 18 O under optimal and heat-stressed conditions, and 18 O incorporation into ATP and other phosphate-containing metabolites is quantified from isotopologue distributions. ATP is labeled within one minute of label introduction and approaches the enrichment of intracellular water in stationary phase, indicating ATP turnover as the main entry point of 18 O into the phosphoryl-transfer network. The label rapidly propagates to other nucleotides, sugar phosphates, redox cofactors, and all other measured phosphate-containing metabolites within three hours of label introduction. Normalizing metabolite enrichment to ATP enrichment reveals phosphoryl group turnover that changes with growth phase, indicating net phosphoryl flux through gluconeogenesis into the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) during exponential growth. Heat stress induces moderate effects on growth and central carbon metabolism, but transiently accelerates label accumulation in the non-oxidative PPP and the turnover of NAD + and NADP + . These results show that 18 O-informed metabolomics provides a systematic view of phosphoryl-transfer dynamics and reveals microbial metabolic adaptation under stress, with implications for tracking microbial stress responses and phosphorus cycling in changing environments.
papers.title: <sup>18</sup> O-Informed Metabolomics Reveals Microbial Phosphoryl-Transfer Dynamics and Stress-Induced Changes

papers.abstract: The function of the glycyl radical enzyme (GRE) PFL2 from the hyperthermophilic archaeon Archaeoglobus fulgidus has remained unresolved since its discovery. Structural and sequence analyses initially suggested that PFL2 was a B12-independent glycerol dehydratase (GDHt), whereas subsequent structural and transcriptional evidence implicated it as a methylalkylsuccinate synthase involved in anaerobic alkane activation. Difficulties in reconstituting active PFL2 in vitro prevented either assignment from being established biochemically. Here, genome mining identified soluble activating enzymes that enabled us to demonstrate that PFL2 catalyzes glycerol dehydration to 3-hydroxypropionaldehyde (3-HPA). This reaction initiates the reductive glycerol pathway, in which 3-HPA is subsequently reduced to 1,3-propanediol (1,3-PD), an industrially important precursor to polymers and other materials. Although characterized in bacteria, this pathway has not previously been experimentally established in archaea. Motivated by this knowledge gap, we identified three oxidoreductases encoded in the A. fulgidus genome that catalyze the reduction of 3-HPA to 1,3-PD in vitro. Microscale thermophoresis revealed nanomolar-affinity binding between PFL2 and one of these oxidoreductases, AF0339 (apparent Kd = 70–90 nM), and AlphaFold-Multimer modeling predicted a continuous tunnel connecting their active sites, suggesting a possible route for intermediate transfer. Notably, PFL2 and AF0339 exhibited melting temperatures of 80.5 and 85.2 °C, respectively, revealing a thermally stable pair of enzymes catalyzing both steps of the pathway. Together, these findings establish PFL2 as an archaeal GDHt and provide experimental support for a reductive glycerol pathway in archaea. The thermostability of these enzymes further highlights their potential utility in biocatalytic 1,3-PD production.
papers.title: Functional characterization of a hyperthermophilic glycyl radical enzyme reveals a reductive glycerol pathway in archaea

papers.abstract: We introduce an integral-direct, linear-scaling, local explicitly correlated (F12) coupled-cluster (CC) singles, doubles, and perturbative triples [CCSD(T)] approach building on our established local natural orbital (LNO) CCSD(T) [J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2018, 14, 4193] and local second-order Møller–Plesset F12 [J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2026, 22, 2946] techniques. By generating and transforming all the required integrals on-the-fly, the algorithm eliminates integral storage requirements, resulting in asymptotically constant memory usage and negligible disk I/O. A key strength of the implementation is the application of the CCSD(F12*) ansatz alongside our (T+) triples correction—currently the most comprehensive scheme incorporating F12 approximations — which delivers rapid basis set convergence. Benchmark tests show that, under default truncation settings, the method recovers over 99.9% of the canonical explicitly correlated CCSD(T) correlation energy, achieving reaction energy errors under 1 kJ/mol. Compared to the complete basis set limit of CCSD(T), the average deviation of reaction energies remains around 1 kJ/mol. Overall, our results demonstrate that combining LNO-CCSD(T) with explicit correlation provides an efficient strategy for high-accuracy calculations on large molecular systems using modest basis sets.
papers.title: A linear-scaling explicitly correlated local natural orbital CCSD(T) approach

papers.abstract: Binary transition-metal bismuth compounds offer a new class of solid-state materials with emergent properties such as magnetism, superconductivity, thermoelectricity and nontrivial topology. Under ambient conditions, Bi shows immiscibility with many other elements. High-pressure can offers an alternative thermodynamic landscape for Bi-based intermetallic systems. Herein, we computationally explore the energy landscape for the immiscible Cr-Bi systems under high-pressure. At 60 GPa, CrBi2 having a CuAl2-type structure with -Cr-Cr-Cr- chains and Bi2 dimers is found to be thermodynamically stable with respect to the elemental solids. The structure is dynamically stable and exhibits ferromagnetic character. Furthermore, electronic structure calculation reveals notable Cr-Cr and Bi-Bi bonding interaction, along with distinctive Cr 3d and Bi 6p bonding interaction. Apart from homoatomic interactions, Cr 3d and Bi 6p hybridization plays a critical role in stabilizing CrBi2 under pressure. This finding provides a viable route towards discovery of new binary intermetallic compounds and extend the compositional space for chemical synthesis at high-pressure.
papers.title: Pressure-Induced Formation of Intermetallic CrBi2

papers.abstract: Metabolic and bioprocess engineering aim to achieve high fermentation titer, rate and yield (TRY), yet no general framework connects these interdependent metrics to facility-scale economics. We introduce NSKinetics, an agile computational framework embedding biochemically structured kinetic models within facility-scale process simulation, techno-economic analysis, uncertainty analysis, global sensitivity analysis, and optimization. We find that for yeast-based ethanol and isobutanol production in a corn biorefinery, cost uncertainty for today's technology is governed by scale, feedstock price, and co-product value rather than ethanol fermentation kinetics. Nonintuitively, while eliminating ethanol inhibition enables a 3.7-fold increase in ethanol productivity, it makes the facility unprofitable by diverting too much carbon to cell growth. Across eight Bayesian optimization campaigns over 12 enzyme-expression, tolerance, and substrate-feeding decisions, TRY-optimized strains were poorly profitable, and a profitability-only campaign stalled at an ethanol-only optimum (15.8% internal rate of return, IRR). However, combining the approaches with a profitability campaign informed by the TRY campaigns' exploration revealed the potential to engineer an ethanol-isobutanol co-producing strain with 27.3% IRR. Fermentation metrics are therefore insufficient proxies for profitability, but valuable guides across the rugged profitability landscape.
papers.title: Coupling kinetic and techno-economic models reveals hidden biodesign targets

papers.abstract: A tripodal squaramide–quinoline– tris(2-aminoethyl)amine (TREN) chemosensor, TSQAQ, was synthesised in good yield using diethylsquarate, 8-aminoquinoline and tris(2aminoethyl)amine as starting materials. The chemosensor was evaluated as a dual-mode colorimetric platform for the selective naked-eye detection of Cu2+ in DMSO and Cd2+ (precursor was cadmium acetate, CA) in acetonitrile. TSQAQ exhibited sensitivity towards Cu2+ via the ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) mechanism, producing an absorption peak at 450 nm and a distinctive colour change from colourless to bright yellow, irrespective of the Cu2+ counteranion screened. In contrast, the addition of CA yields an absorption peak at 420 nm and a colour transformation from colourless to pale yellow, with confirms the cooperative binding of Cd2+ by the squaramide moiety through hydrogen bonding. The limits of detection (LODs) were determined to be 97 nM (Cu2+) and 3 nM (Cd2+). Binding constants of 2.51 × 104 M-1 and 1.97 × 104 M-1 were determined using the Benesi-Hildebrand equation. The binding stoichiometry of TSQAQ with Cd2+ was established as 1:1 using the Job plot method. FTIR and 1H NMR titration studies indicated the involvement of TREN nitrogen, quinoline imine nitrogen, and squaramide carbonyl oxygen atoms in metal-ion coordination. Cu2+ sensing was reversible upon the addition of EDTA, with 94% signal recovery maintained over five cycles, enabling the implementation of an INHIBIT molecular logic gate. For practical applications, TSQAQ-coated paper strips were employed for the naked-eye detection of Cu2+ ions in real environmental water samples, including river water, seawater, and tap water.
papers.title: Squaramide-based ultrasensitive and reversible colourimetric dual sensor for the detection of copper and metal-ion-assisted acetate anion

papers.abstract: Many advanced imaging techniques, such as super-resolution microscopy, rely on photoinduced transformations of fluorescent proteins. In photoinduced decarboxylation, light absorption triggers loss of CO 2 from an acidic residue near the chromophore, often accompanied by a change in chromophore protonation that switches the protein to a fluorescent form, as in PA-GFP. Evidence from proteins in which this reaction has been observed indicates that the decarboxylating residue must be present in its deprotonated form. Because protonation states are difficult to determine experimentally, here we perform constant-pH molecular dynamics (CpHMD) simulations on a set of fluorescent protein variants, and find that the predicted protonation states are consistent with the observed photoinduced properties. This includes superfolder GFP, which does not decarboxylate, and its T203D mutant, in which two residues undergo decarboxylation. CpHMD therefore offers a practical route to predicting which variants are capable of photoinduced decarboxylation and to designing new photoactivatable proteins.
papers.title: Constant-pH Molecular Dynamics Rationalizes Photoinduced Decarboxylation in Fluorescent Proteins

papers.abstract: We introduce Radial Kernel Attention (RKA) for long-range modeling in polymer machine learning force fields. Local neighbor graphs constrain communication across polymer chains and their surrounding environments, while explicit all-pair attention incurs quadratic cost. RKA maps atomic distances from the cluster centroid to learned radial features and combines their overlap with content-dependent queries and keys. Factorized aggregation and readout enable global feature exchange at linear cost in atom count for fixed feature dimensions. We insert the invariant scalar update between EquiformerV3 local blocks and obtain conservative forces by differentiating the total energy, including its radial coordinate dependence. We evaluate energy and force prediction for finite polymer-derived clusters in OPoly26. Our models are trained on the official training split for 12 epochs and evaluated directly after training on the complete official validation split. A matched 5M comparison shows that RKA reduces per-atom energy and force MAEs by 67.4% and 36.3%, respectively. The 20M RKA model is compared with UMA-S-1.2 and UMA-S-1.2.1 on the same validation structures. The 20M model attains a total-energy MAE of 15.81 meV and a force MAE of 2.619 meV/Å; its per-atom energy MAE is 0.1182 meV/atom. RKA provides a compact global communication pathway that improves energy and force prediction on the evaluated polymer-derived clusters.
papers.title: Radial Kernel Attention for Long-Range Modeling in Polymer Machine Learning Force Fields

papers.abstract: The development of functional porous materials from renewable resources offers a promising strategy to reduce reliance on fossil-derived feedstocks and advance sustainable materials technologies. Here, we report the facile synthesis of bio-based porous organic polymers (bioPOPs) through the polycondensation of vanillin-derived organic dialdehydes and inexpensive diamine monomers. The synthetic approach demonstrates good generality, enabling vanillin-derived monomers bearing different functional substituents (H, OH, CH3, OCH3, and NO2) to be converted into bioPOPs with high specific surface areas of up to 523 m2/g and abundant microporosity. Furthermore, cellulose nanofibers (CNF) were employed as templates for the in situ interfacial polymerization of bioPOPs on their surfaces, allowing the resulting hybrid nanofibers to be processed into freestanding composite films. Benefiting from their rich microporosity and abundant nitrogen-containing functional groups, both pristine bioPOPs and CNF@bioPOP composite films exhibited efficient [AuCl4]- capture from aqueous solutions, with adsorption capacities of up to 1093 mg/g, rapid adsorption kinetics, and excellent selectivity over competing metal ions. More importantly, the materials demonstrated highly efficient and selective gold recovery from real electronic waste leachate, highlighting their potential for preciousmetal recovery from secondary resources. The freestanding composite films further offer advantages for practical separation applications through their processability and potential integration into continuous flow systems. Overall, this work demonstrates the transformation of renewable resources into functional porous materials for precious-metal recovery from secondary waste streams, establishing a fully sustainable and circular approach to resource utilization.
papers.title: Synthesis and Engineering of Bio-Based Porous Organic Polymers for Gold Recovery

papers.abstract: Complete-basis-set (CBS) extrapolation is widely used to estimate electronic energies beyond finite-basis calculations. However, students may encounter it primarily as a formula or automated correction, which obscures how a CBS value is constructed from a sequence of finite-basis energies. We describe a scaffolded Excel activity that makes this process visible by linking energy tables, component extrapolations, and convergence plots. Students first examine Hartree-Fock and correlation-energy convergence in the hydrogen chloride heteronuclear diatomic molecule, compare CBS estimates obtained from alternative extrapolation choices, and then apply the same workflow to the hydrogen fluoride molecule HF. The activity culminates in the calculation and justification of CBS-derived atomization energies and comparison to experiment. This activity is implemented in an upper-division computational chemistry course, and was evaluated through a pre-activity quiz and rubric-based analysis of completed student work. In general, students executed the component extrapolations successfully, yet evaluating sensitivity and justifying a final reported value proved more challenging. The activity offers a transparent and adaptable approach for teaching students to evaluate, rather than merely obtain, computational chemistry results.
papers.title: Making Complete-Basis-Set Extrapolation Visible: A Spreadsheet-Based Activity for Upper-Division Computational Chemistry

papers.abstract: The rational design of catalysts capable of efficiently utilizing CO2 is critical for sustainable chemical processes. The Super-dry reforming of methane (Super-DRM), which couples dry reforming of methane (DRM) with the reverse water gas shift (RWGS) reactions, offers a promising route to maximize CO2 conversion. Modulating the crystal phase of nanocatalysts offers a powerful strategy to enhance catalytic performance, yet the relationship between bulk phase and catalytic behavior remains poorly understood. A significant obstacle in resolving this issue is obtaining atomic-level insights on the surface structure of phase-controlled catalyst under reaction conditions. In this study, we employ in-situ gas cell transmission electron microscopy to investigate the surface structure of faceted PtNi nanoparticles during Super-DRM at moderate temperatures (550 ℃). Atomic-resolution in-situ observations reveal that the reaction environment induces a pronounced nickel segregation and subsequent coke formation on the surface of disordered A1-PtNi nanoparticles. In contrast, the ordered L10 phase exhibits remarkable resistance to such segregation on its {111} facets. This structural rigidity effectively suppresses coke formation and lowers the kinetic barrier for CH4 activation by 27 kJ/mol compared to the disordered phase. Complemented by in-situ spectroscopy and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, our findings demonstrate that the bulk crystal ordering acts as an anchor for surface structures, governing the catalytic behaviors. This study unveils a direct atomic-level link between crystal ordering, surface reconstruction, and catalytic performance, offering valuable design principles for robust intermetallic catalysts in CO2 utilization.
papers.title: Revealing Phase-Controlled Surface Structure in PtNi Nanocatalysts via In-situ Gas Cell Transmission Electron Microscopy

papers.abstract: A constrained ternary mixture design (Design of Experiments, DoE) was applied to four magnesium aluminosilicate (MAS) glass series to evaluate the predictive capability of Scheffé mixture polynomials for the specific Young’s modulus (spE = E/ρ), the key figure of merit for lightweight glass-fibre reinforcements. Two base compositions (V, Al2O3-rich; T, MgO-rich) were each modified with a 14 wt.% Y2O3–ZnO–CeO2 or La2O3–ZnO–CeO2 block. Linear, quadratic and special-cubic models were fitted to ten design points per series and ranked by R2, R2(adj) and the leave-one-out coefficient R2(pred). Three distinct regimes emerge: the V-series requires a special-cubic model with a dominant ternary Y2O3·ZnO·CeO2 term (β = −47.2, p = 0.001; R2(pred) = 97 %); the T-series is strictly linear (R2(pred) = 55 %), higher orders overfitting; and both La-series show a significant La2O3·CeO2 interaction absent in their Y-analogues. Three additive property models (Makishima–Mackenzie, an extended variant, and Yamane–Sakaino) deviate systematically from measured spE (absolute errors 6.9–12.2 × 106 N·m·kg-1, negative R2), most strongly where DoE detects interactions. The study delineates where additive approaches suffice, where binary synergy dominates, and where genuinely ternary cooperative effects must be resolved.
papers.title: Systematic Evaluation of Mixture-Design for Multi-Oxide Magnesium Aluminosilicate Glass Development: Model Comparison, Modifier Interactions, and Predictive Limitations

papers.abstract: The fragment molecular orbital (FMO) method enables quantum chemical calculations on large biomolecular systems and provides interaction energies between their fragments. Its further development and wider adoption would benefit from software in which new methods can be prototyped rapidly, every stage of a calculation can be inspected, and both developers and users can contribute to extending the method. Here we present PyFMO, a Python framework for FMO calculations that uses PySCF as its electronic-structure backend. An FMO calculation is expressed as a pipeline of interchangeable steps that share a common context, and all results are collected in a serializable container that can be analyzed independently of the calculation. PyFMO supports Hartree–Fock, density functional theory, and correlated methods at the FMO1–FMO3 levels, as well as continuum solvation and pair interaction energy decomposition analysis (PIEDA), including directional charge-transfer and three-body terms. Proteins, nucleic acids, polysaccharides, and glycoproteins are fragmented automatically using rule-based substructure matching. For production calculations, density fitting accelerates both the fragment calculations and the evaluation of electrostatic couplings, while node-level shared memory and cost-model-based load balancing are designed for execution on platforms ranging from laptops to high-performance computing clusters. Benchmarks and an application to a theophylline-binding RNA aptamer, where PIEDA provides a detailed picture of the ligand recognition, demonstrate these capabilities. By combining the flexibility of Python with the performance required for large systems, PyFMO makes the development, testing, and application of new FMO methods for biomolecular problems accessible to a broad community.
papers.title: PyFMO: A Python Framework for Fragment Molecular Orbital Calculations

papers.abstract: The LINE-1 retrotransposon is a virus-like genomic element that can activate in diseased cells. It has been implicated in cancer, autoimmunity, developmental disorders, infectious disease and neurodegeneration. LINE-1 can be inhibited by reverse transcriptase inhibitors, small molecules originally developed for HIV. The correlation between HIV and LINE-1 inhibition is ∼0.9 on a log scale, in spite of >450 Mya of evolutionary history since retroviruses diverged from retrotransposons. Suppression of HIV requires prevention of a completed 9.7 kb virus insertion into the genome in immune cells. However, every cell in the body already contains >100 copies of LINE-1 that can potentially activate. Even incomplete LINE-1 mediated insertions can cause damaging mutations and genome instability. Furthermore, partial HIV and LINE-1 products in the cytoplasm of cells can contribute to an inflammatory immune response. Preclinical studies have shown LINE-1 inhibitors slow the progression of otherwise unrelated diseases. LINE-1’s contribution to these diseases can potentially be quantified using single-nucleus whole-genome sequencing on diseased tissue, enabling prioritization of disease selection for therapeutic development. Furthermore, LINE-1’s ORF1p protein can be measured in the blood of individuals with certain cancers. LINE-1 inhibitors could therefore be extended to various diseases. Potentially used both as an anti-inflammatory and prophylactically to help preserve genome integrity. Reverse transcriptase inhibitors are available at low cost for HIV, and higher doses of some could be used to inhibit LINE-1. However, reverse transcriptase inhibitors do not prevent DNA cutting by LINE-1’s endonuclease. Novel inhibitors may therefore be required. This, combined with novel diagnostics opens up possibilities for inhibiting LINE-1 therapeutically in disease
papers.title: Inhibiting LINE-1 retrotransposons therapeutically in disease

papers.abstract: Self-driving laboratories plan well but react slowly: a failing run, finished conversion or odd reading needs a call within seconds, at the instrument. We built that reflex stage by stage from the fruit-fly odor circuit. Raman bands become odor channels; a fixed number of cells fire, keeping shape, not strength. An output compartment learns to stop after one failed and one good run, and keeps learning. In simulated selenization and argon-ion irradiation of 2D semiconductors (20 repeats), one fixed-setting layer made four calls. It needs no retraining over a campaign and its memory does not grow, yet a rare phase from one burst was recognized on an early return. The stop cut flakes lost from 7.75 to 3.55 of 30, level with tuned tools. In a simulator from four published spectra, three flakes gave it slightly lower dose error than an equal-memory raw-spectrum lookup. Ending furnace runs at the instrument lost 0.10 flakes, against 11.0 waiting an assumed 60 s for a planner. Engineered specialists, one per call, are smaller, flag odd readings better and run 24-fold faster. Laboratories can split decisions in two: the planner keeps the recipe; a small fly-circuit layer at each instrument makes the fast calls.
papers.title: How the fruit fly mushroom body can help autonomous materials discovery

papers.abstract: High-entropy alloy nanoparticles (HEA NPs) offer compositional and structural tunability for applications, like water splitting, H 2 O 2 production, or magnetocaloric technologies. Therefore, the interplay between composition, structure, and functionality is of significant interest for materials´ functionality optimization. Microparticle laser fragmentation in liquid flow (MP-LFL) is an emerging scalable method for nanoalloy production, but remains underexplored for HEA NPs. Here, we investigate CrFeCoNiX (X = Ga, Cu, Mo) HEA NPs fabricated by MP-LFL in ethanol and examine how compositional variations affect elemental homogeneity, size, phase structure, and magnetic properties. Microscopy, diffraction, size analysis, and magnetometry reveal particle sizes of 6-7 nm and pronounced differences in phase structures, ranging from single-phase fcc and biphasic fcc/bcc to amorphous structures, partially contrasting the initial feedstock microparticle structures. The low saturation magnetization (M s ) of the as-synthesized superparamagnetic NPs increases strongly after in situ annealing by approximately 4-, 3-, or 24-fold for Ga-, Cu-, and Mo-containing NPs, respectively, coinciding with structural and elemental rearrangements. In contrast, the feedstock microparticles show no comparable increase, highlighting the role of the initial phase constitution in determining magnetic properties. Moreover, MP-LFL enables production of ~0.4 g/h, with a record picosecond MP-LFL mass yield of ~60%, leaving room for further optimization and high throughput.
papers.title: Nanoscale Phase Engineering and Magnetic Property Enhancement in High-Entropy Alloy Nanoparticles by Continuous Microparticle Laser Fragmentation in Liquid

papers.abstract: Aromaticity underpins molecular stability in fields ranging from pharmaceuticals to organic semiconductors, yet existing prediction methods are either too computationally costly for large-scale screening or too empirically restricted for broad applicability. This work introduces the molecular sheaf, a cellular sheaf model free of empirical parameters for chemical bonding that generalizes standard molecular graph theory. From this the frontier eigengap Δ_F is derived as a spectral approximation of the HOMO-LUMO gap requiring only molecular topology and electron count. Δ_F correctly classifies the aromaticity and antiaromaticity of the full annulene series, including benzene and cyclobutadiene, exactly recovering Hückel theory for regular hydrocarbon systems. At scale, it accounts for 62.5% of the variance in DFT HOMO-LUMO gaps across 17,523 structurally diverse polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and 21.7% across 52,000 heteroaromatic systems, with the reduction reflecting the deliberate cost of parameter freedom. This confirms that aromatic character can be approximated from molecular connectivity and electron count alone, suggesting that cellular sheaves offer a largely unexplored mathematical framework for the modeling of chemical bonding and structure. All calculations run at under 1 ms per molecule, over seven orders of magnitude faster than corresponding DFT calculations. The molecular sheaf thus also enables rapid, parameter-free pre-screening of aromatic character from structural data alone.
papers.title: A Cellular Sheaf Model for Aromaticity in Discrete Molecular Systems

papers.abstract: The prevailing way to model a many-body system is to encode every component and then let a module capture interaction. We show that the explicit interaction module is harmful when the number of components increases. We use a simple interaction-carrying encoder that compresses a component’s interaction contribution into its representation, and combine the representations by linear aggregation. This modelling approach is simple in form yet delivers unexpectedly excellent performance: it matches the prevailing explicit route under most conditions and exceeds it when a mixture carries more components than the training set covered. Moreover, an encoder produced this way has a clear advantage over per-component descriptors when it is transferred to a similar task: it greatly reduces the data requirements.
papers.title: Interaction without an interaction module

papers.abstract: Two competing reduction pathways can deliver a single stereochemical outcome. This computational study reveals that within an achiral TFA model, the reduction of 2-alkenylquinolines can begin through nearly isoenergetic 1,4-hydride transfer to either the quinoline ring or the alkenyl side chain. The resulting sequences are proposed to converge on a common prochiral iminium intermediate. Furthermore, analysis of the final chiral phosphoric acid-controlled 1,2-hydride transfer predicts the preferential formation of the experimentally observed major enantiomer.
papers.title: Computational Analysis of Competing Reduction Pathways in the Asymmetric Transfer Hydrogenation of 2-Alkenylquinolines

papers.abstract: Fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) maps local physicochemical properties with a confocal laser-scanning microscope. Soft materials are promising targets for FLIM because they demand multi-scale microanalysis; of particular interest are the interfacial properties of complex fluids. However, within each pixel, interfacial and non-interfacial FLIM signals are mixed, which complicates the physical interpretation of FLIM results at interfaces. Here, we propose a systematic FLIM approach: acquire three-dimensional FLIM data at near-diffraction-limited resolution, identify the mixing mechanism by phasor analysis, and perform pixel-level mono- or bi-exponential fitting according to that mechanism. As a proof of concept, we apply this approach to the complex interfaces of grease, in which tens-of-nanometer-scale thickener fibers form a three-dimensional network in the base oil. We prepare a grease labeled with a molecular-rotor dye whose fluorescence lifetime is coupled to the oil viscosity. Three-dimensional FLIM reveals that the lifetime significantly increases at the fiber–oil interfaces. Phasor analysis shows that this lifetime heterogeneity originates from a binary mixture of free-oil and fiber-bound states. Pixel-level bi-exponential fitting then separates the FLIM images into two state maps. In the fiber-bound state, the intramolecular rotation of the dye is arrested, indicating that the oil is solid-like rather than viscous at the interfaces. Beyond the ~180 nm resolution of our images, the lifetime-domain separation resolves the coexistence of the two states within a single diffraction-limited voxel. Finally, we generalize our approach so that FLIM can be broadly applied to map interfacial properties in soft complex materials.
papers.title: Three-dimensional fluorescence lifetime imaging of a molecular rotor at complex interfaces of grease

papers.abstract: Thin polymer films exhibit thickness-dependent viscoelastic behavior attributed to enhanced segmental mobility near free surfaces, a phenomenon recently linked to surface-induced constraint release (SICR) in entangled polymer melts. While self-consistent theoretical treatments of this mechanism exist, computationally lightweight phenomenological models that isolate the role of specific structural assumptions remain comparatively underexplored. This work showcases a developed closed-form, depth-resolved generalized Maxwell model in which local relaxation times are derived from a depth-dependent entanglement molecular weight profile, motivated by reptation scaling (tau~Z^3.4) and literature-reported surface entanglement enhancement ratios. With this framework, we directly compare two assumptions for combining depth-dependent relaxation behavior into an effective film modulus: a depth-independent linear superposition, and an entanglement-coupled, double-reptation-inspired mixing rule. Holding the underlying relaxation-time profile identical between both models, we find that the choice of coupling mechanism alters the predicted storage modulus by up to ~40%, with the divergence peaking at an intermediate film thickness rather than increasing monotonically as films thin. This work shows that the peak location is associated with, though not fully predicted by, the frequency-dependent heterogeneity of local relaxation times across the film. These results indicate that depth-coupling assumptions in phenomenological thin-film rheology models are not a minor implementation detail, but materially and non-trivially shape predicted thickness-dependent behavior, with implications for how such models should be constructed and interpreted going forward.
papers.title: Surface-Induced Constraint Release in Confined Polymer Films: A Computational Phenomenological Study

papers.abstract: Pore confinement in zirconium-based metal–organic frameworks (Zr-MOFs) is often described using the cage–window ratio (Γ CW ), the largest cavity diameter divided by the pore-limiting diameter (D f ), yet whether this composite coordinate carries information beyond Df alone remains unclear. We modeled CO 2 uptake, heat of adsorption (HoA), and CO 2 /N 2 selectivity for 239 Zr-containing MOFs at two pressures relevant to vacuum-swing adsorption using structure-grouped machine learning with SHAP interpretation, reaching test R 2 values of 0.77–0.88. Although Γ CW correlated positively with all three targets, controlling for D f weakened these associations and reversed their sign, while the reciprocal analysis left the D f associations largely unchanged and a difference-based formulation produced no significant association. D f played different roles across the three targets, indicating that the apparent confinement effect mainly reflects the limiting aperture rather than relative cage–window architecture.
papers.title: Interpretable Machine Learning Disentangles Pore Confinement Across Multiple Zr-MOF CO2 Capture Targets

papers.abstract: Reliable assessment of buried solid–solid interfaces is essential for understanding and improving electrochemical devices including solid-state batteries. Electrical measurements such as electrochemical impedance spectroscopy provide an attractive (operando) diagnostic but probe interfacial contact only indirectly through its influence on charge transport. Consequently, the extent to which interfacial morphology can be inferred from the electrical response remains unclear. Here, we use 3D electric network simulations to study how interfacial morphology governs the impedance detectability of non-ideal contacts at constriction-dominated interfaces. The resulting general principles are discussed using metal dissolution at interfaces with fast charge-transfer kinetics as a representative case. We show that no universal detection threshold exists. Instead, detectability depends on the remaining contact area, the lateral distribution of contact and non-contact regions, and the sample thickness. In limiting cases with small, finely distributed pores, contact losses exceeding 90% may remain largely undetectable, whereas localized contact loss produces pronounced impedance features at substantially higher remaining contact areas. These findings reveal a morphology-induced diagnostic blind spot in impedance-based interface analysis and demonstrate that the absence of a measurable interface signal does not necessarily imply intimate or stable interfacial contact. This diagnostic blind spot therefore challenges the reliability of conclusions and material parameters derived from electrical measurements without independent knowledge of the underlying interface morphology.
papers.title: Limitations of Impedance Spectroscopy in Detecting Interfacial Contact Quality – Insights from Metal Anode Dissolution in Solid-State Batteries

papers.abstract: Steroid hormones are central to the development, metabolism, homeostasis and reproduction of animals and have been the subject of many evolutionary, ecotoxicological and human health studies. Coarse-grain molecular dynamics (CG MD) simulations are a powerful tool to study the structural and dynamic behavior of steroid hormones and their interactions. Here, we expand the capabilities of the widely used Martini 3 CG framework by parameterizing and validating a set of 20 steroid hormone models — including both endogenous and synthetic molecules — to enable their study across diverse targets, systems, and fields of interest. Hormone parameterization followed Martini 3 guidelines, while leveraging the similarities with the parent cholesterol molecule, for which a Martini 3 model is available. Notably, we were able to base our parameterization on the hundreds of experimental structures in the protein data bank that contain steroid hormones, instead of relying on atomistic simulations as is typical with Martini. The parameterized models match to within 5% target molecular volumes, and recover the overall hydrophobicity trend of the hormones, although higher hydrophobicities tended to be overestimated. In free simulations of protein-hormone systems the experimentally known binding poses could be recovered for 89% of the cases, indicating a successful parameterization also from a functional standpoint. Since several Martini 3 protein models were tested, we also incidentally show that the flexibility of the OLIVES and GōMartini models makes them best suited for this type of protein–ligand recognition. Finally, models were validated in interaction with membranes by comparison to reference atomistic data. We expect that the availability of our fully validated Martini 3 CG steroid hormone models will contribute to new studies, collaborations, and applications across different scientific fields.
papers.title: Martini 3 Coarse-Grained Models for Steroid Hormones

papers.abstract: Nucleic acids are central to many biomolecular processes central to cellular life, yet characterising their molecular motions and fluctuations with atomic resolution remains challenging. We introduce high-resolution relaxometry, combined with high-field nuclear spin relaxation, as a powerful tool to probe motions in nucleic acids. After recording an extensive spin-relaxation dataset from 2 to 23 T, we propose a framework, within the model-free approach, that allowed us to identify motions occurring both on the picosecond and low nanosecond time scales. By integrating these results with molecular dynamics simulations and ensembles, obtained from residual dipolar coupling (RDC) measurements, we propose a time-resolved model that includes fast helical motions and slower pervasive sugar puckering motions. The approach outlined in this study also provides a framework for interrogating molecular dynamics in nucleic acids with spin relaxation experiments and benchmarking molecular dynamics simulations that aim to characterise dynamic processes.
papers.title: High-resolution relaxometry suggests the presence of pervasive nano-second sugar motions in a DNA duplex.
Sulfotransferase Catalyzed Resolution and Nucleophilic Substitution of Alcohols to Access N-H-Heterocycles

papers.abstract: Coupling block copolymer self-assembly with ultrafast Joule heating enables second-scale crystallization of ordered mesoporous oxides while preserving long-range mesoscopic order. Using this strategy, we synthesize long-range ordered mesoporous magnesium-aluminum oxide frameworks at low magnesium contents exhibiting defect spinel-related nanocrystalline structures. Ex situ isothermal holds at 1000 to 1155 °C reveal rapid crystallite enlargement followed by a plateau in apparent crystallite size. In pure γ-alumina, this early saturation, together with retention of the ordered mesostructure, is consistent with geometrically constrained crystallite growth. Magnesium incorporation enables further crystallite enlargement before saturation, yielding larger defect-spinel-related domains while retaining long-range mesoscopic order. We further demonstrate the incorporation of in situ crystallized platinum nanoparticles within the ordered magnesium-aluminum oxide framework and their activity for methylcyclohexane dehydrogenation at 350 °C. These results demonstrate that ultrafast Joule heating can access distinct crystallization trajectories in compositionally modified mesoporous oxides that are precluded by mesostructural collapse during conventional furnace heating.
papers.title: Joule Heating Induced Structural Evolution of Ordered Mesoporous Mg-Al Spinel-Related Oxides

papers.abstract: High-throughput experimentation (HTE) supplies enough reaction data to train machine-learning models, yet yield-prediction models are typically reported on a single dataset, and both their cross-dataset stability and their attainable ceiling are rarely examined. Using a single pipeline without per-dataset tuning, this work compares five model architectures under three categorical encodings on thirteen HTE datasets drawn from five public source collections, and estimates a noise ceiling for every dataset that repeats a condition. Accuracy is governed by the encoding rather than by the algorithm: switching a multilayer perceptron from integer to one-hot encoding raises its mean held-out R2 by 0.168. Across datasets, the spread in validation-selected held-out R2 tracks the noise ceiling, with a mean capture ratio of 86.35%.
