Attribution rankings show some regularity: the reactant slots rank at the top, followed by temperature and the additive, while the equivalence and metal slots carry the smallest mean shares. The limits are equally clear: substrate-disjoint and ordered cross-validation both give negative R2, and no cross-dataset transfer succeeds, so the framework supports interpolation only. On the only dataset with enough distinct reactant pairs, predicting unseen combinations of known reactants reaches R2 = 0.58, whereas predicting unseen reactants with molecular fingerprints reaches 0.41. Ranking by predicted yield outperforms expected improvement, whose uncertainty signal neither ranks the error nor is calibrated.
papers.title: Yield Prediction and Condition Recommendation on High-Throughput Experimentation Datasets: Encoding Effects and Noise Ceilings

papers.abstract: Selecting effective solvents and antisolvents requires navigating vast chemical, composition, and temperature spaces where exhaustive experimentation is prohibitively costly and low average regression errors do not guarantee that the best candidates appear within a short experimental screen. We introduce SolviScope, a graph neural network framework for solubility prediction and solvent ranking in pure and binary solvent systems. SolviScope-Pure combines a two-dimensional gated graph encoder with intermolecular cross-attention, avoiding three-dimensional conformer generation. SolviScope-Binary integrates hierarchical message passing with Kamlet–Taft and Hansen descriptors and temperature–composition conditioning. Both models use explicit ranking objectives. SolviScope-Pure achieves a molar logS root-mean-square error of 0.77 on a 7,264-measurement structural hold-out set, lower errors than FastSolv on two overlap-filtered external benchmarks, and better solvent-ranking correlations for 8 of 10 industrially relevant solutes. Across two industrial mixture benchmarks comprising 13 solutes, SolviScope-Binary achieves per-solute Spearman’s ρ of 0.51–0.91 and recovers the experimentally most and least soluble systems within its top-five and bottom-five predictions for every solute. Retrospective studies of two unseen APIs further demonstrate solvent/antisolvent prioritization and correct composition ordering in solvent–water mixtures. Cooling-crystallization assessments reveal that successful isothermal ranking does not establish reliable cooling-drop ranking or quantitative working-capacity prediction. These results support SolviScope as a tool for prioritizing experimental solvent screens, with prospective validation needed to establish broader applicability and experimental savings.
papers.title: SolviScope: An Interaction-Aware Graph Neural Network for Solvent Ranking of Small Organic Molecules in Pure and Multicomponent Solvent Systems

papers.abstract: Covalent labeling mass spectrometry (CL-MS) reports the solvent exposure of individual residues, but how much structural information an experiment returns depends on which labeling reagent is used. Currently, there are no tools available to guide the reagent choice. Here, we present PROBE-Select (PRotein-Oriented Best-reagent Evaluator for Selective labeling), a computational workflow that selects labeling reagents for a given protein sequence and is available as a web application on the Rosetta Online Server that Includes Everyone (ROSIE). Starting from a sequence, the workflow generates a ColabFold ensemble of candidate structures under diversity-promoting settings, removes models dominated by nonregular secondary structure, clusters the remaining models, and selects three representative conformations. The workflow then retains as reporters all residues whose predicted solvent exposure differs between at least two of the three representatives by more than a threshold T. Reporters are mapped to compatible labeling reagents, and each reagent is scored by the number of reporters it can label for each conformation pair. On a benchmark of 11 proteins with experimentally characterized alternative conformations, the workflow identified 182 reporter residues at T = 5. The number of reporters increased with the structural separation between representatives, and the number of reporters available to each reagent differed between proteins and between pairs of representatives. Diethylpyrocarbonate was the top-ranked residue-selective reagent in 8 of the 10 benchmark proteins that had reporters. PROBE-Select returns the reagent ranking, the residue-level exposure data behind it, and the three representative structures. PROBE-Select is freely available for academic and non-profit use, and can be accessed with a GitHub account via this link ( r2.graylab.jhu.edu/apps/submit/probe-select ).
papers.title: PROBE-Select: A Web Server for Selecting Optimal Protein-Specific Labeling Reagents to Maximize Structural Information Obtained from Covalent Labeling Mass Spectrometry

papers.abstract: Herein we report the total-defluorination of 1,1,1,2-tetrafluoroethane (HFC-134a) and pentafluoroethane (HFC-125) using a KOtBu-DMSO mixture to generate KF. The lab production rate and space time yield of KF generated in flow reaches 3.76 gh-1 and 7978 gh-1L-1 from HFC-134a, and 0.57 gh-1 and 57 gh-L-1 from HFC-125. A detailed study of the mechanism of defluorination was conducted through sampling of intermediates via flow aliquots, and analysis by multinuclear NMR spectroscopy.
papers.title: Mechanistic Analysis and Optimisation of the Defluorination of Hydrofluorocarbon Refrigerants

papers.abstract: Herein, we report the synthesis of a new hypervalent iodine reagent, ((((( tert butyldimethylsilyl)oxy)methyl)sulfonyl)(diazo)methyl)(phenyl)- λ 3-iodaneyl trifluoromethanesulfonate (HIR 3 ), from the Diversity-Oriented Clicking (DOC) hub tert -butyl(((diazomethyl)sulfonyl)methoxy)dimethylsilane ( t Bu-DMSM), thereby reversing the native reactivity of its diazo carbon. Reaction of 3 with nucleophilic silyl enol ethers affords β-diazosulfones in good to excellent yields. Subsequent rhodium-catalysed intramolecular 1,3-C–H insertion provides novel cyclopropanes bearing a masked sulfonyl fluoride group in good to excellent yields and diastereoselectivities. Unmasking of this group enables the late-stage formation of cyclopropyl sulfonyl fluorides, either from the isolated cyclopropanes or through a one-pot, two-step sequence from the βdiazosulfones. We further demonstrate that the major cyclopropane diastereomer undergoes base-mediated epimerisation to afford an otherwise inaccessible diastereomer, which participates in sulfur(VI) fluoride exchange (SuFEx) reactions to furnish the corresponding sulfonates. Finally, trapping of the intermediate sulfinate with benzyl bromide electrophiles, rather than conversion into the sulfonyl fluoride, provides access to structurally diverse sulfones.
papers.title: Umpolung of a Diazo Sulfonyl Fluoride Surrogate Expands Diversity-Oriented Clicking to Cyclopropanes

papers.abstract: Interactive study guides, with practice problems that change every time, help on request and small simulations, are valuable and slow to build; few instructors have time to make one for every unit. I describe a workflow that lets one instructor, a chemist with no programming background, build such guides with a generative AI coding assistant in about ten minutes each, plus about half an hour of polishing, and deliver them through GitHub Pages to Canvas or D2L Brightspace. Twenty pages for General Chemistry I, a course for non-science majors, biochemistry and Organic Chemistry I illustrate it; seventeen were built with this workflow over about a month. Each guide is a single web page that runs in any current browser, needs no account and sends nothing to a server. The guides share a design: a roadmap of the topic, sections in teaching order, problems whose numbers change each time, feedback on wrong answers, and small virtual instruments such as a titration, a calorimeter and a thin-layer plate; nine offer three levels of help. The biochemistry and organic guides take their values from named textbooks, and a check of every page, which ran about 1.6 million generated problems and recomputed each answer independently, found no wrong answer key but did find faults that reading had missed: named mistakes accepted as correct, correct answers rejected, an answer given away, and physically impossible setups; all were fixed and the check run again. No learning outcomes are claimed; evaluation is future work.
papers.title: Built in Minutes, Checked by Script: Instructor-Made Interactive Chemistry Study Guides with Generative AI

papers.abstract: The use of phytocannabinoid compounds has exploded since the opening up of medicinal and recreational cannabis markets as well as the legalization of industrial hemp. Chemical derivatives of the naturally occurring phytocannabinoids have been explored as novel therapeutics to treat numerous diseases and medical conditions. Here, we describe a new chemically modified phytocannabinoid derivative, namely hexahydrocannabinolic acid (HHCA), produced from plant-derived tetrahydrocannabinolic acid (THCA). Catalytic hydrogenation of THCA affords HHCA as a diastereomeric mixture at the 9-position on the ring that was separated chromatographically into the isolated 9R and 9S isomers. We assessed their cytotoxic activity on Jurkat T cells and, while a mixture of both isomers of HHCA were found to be more active than THCA, the isolated 9S HHCA isomer was significantly more active than the 9R HHCA isomer. This finding offers not only new molecules to assess for drug discovery, but possibly new mechanisms of action for chemically modified phytocannabinoids.
papers.title: Chiral Separation of Hexahydrocannabinolic Acid (HHCA) Isomers Have Differential Activity Against Jurkat T Cells

papers.abstract: Silver thiolate coordination polymers (CPs) exhibit diverse structures and physical properties, although thermal behavior of silver thiophenolate CPs has rarely been investigated. In this study, we investigated the effects of ligands containing rigid aromatic rings and flexible alkoxy chains on the thermal phase transitions of silver thiophenolate CPs. A series of para -alkoxy-substituted silver thiophenolate CPs (AgSAr-OCX, where X denotes the number of carbon atoms in the alkoxy chain) were prepared through ligand exchange reactions. Structural characterization revealed that all AgSAr-OCX derivatives formed layered crystal structures and that the conformational order of alkyl chains increased with increasing chain length. DSC analysis showed that the number and temperatures of the thermal transitions strongly depended on alkyl chain length, with longer-chain derivatives exhibiting multiple thermal events. Variable-temperature powder X-ray diffraction measurements revealed two successive lamellar-to-lamellar transitions followed by transformation into a hexagonal columnar phase for the longer-chain derivatives. Variable-temperature FT-IR measurements further indicated conformational disordering of the alkyl chains during the reversible low-temperature transition. These multiple phase transitions may arise from the combination of rigid aromatic rings that stabilize the layered structures and flexible alkoxy chains that provide thermal responsiveness through conformational changes.
papers.title: Multiple Phase Transition Behavior of Silver Thiophenolates with Rigid Aromatic Rings and Flexible Alkoxy Chains

papers.abstract: Lead-free halide double perovskites are grabbing attention as these compounds are environmentally friendly, stable and prominent for their high-performances in photovoltaics. Here we report a comprehensive first-principles study of the double perovskite Cs2LiFeBr6 using density functional theory with an on-site Hubbard correction. Cs2LiFeBr6 is geometrically relaxed and crystallizes in the cubic elpasolite structure (Fm-3m, No. 225). Thermodynamic stability is confirmed formation energy calculations. The dynamic stability is calculated by phonon calculation. The elastic constants indicate ductile mechanical behavior. The band gap is 0.444 eV; inclusion of the Hubbard correction yields a fully spin-polarized semiconducting ground state with an indirect band gap of 0.927 eV. Carrier effective masses are asymmetric. The static dielectric constant is 5.06, and the absorption coefficient exceeds 104 cm−1 from 1.17 eV, indicating Cs2LiFeBr6 is effective in visible-range solar energy harvesting. Although the band gap is indirect, the lowest direct allowed transition lies only 0.029 eV above it, so the spectroscopic limited maximum efficiency reaches 24.9% for a 1 µm film and maximum of 26.18% for a 5 µm film. This study unveils the structural stability, mechanical properties, chemical stability, and potential of solar cell applications of the structure.
papers.title: Novel Lead-free double perovskite Cs2LiFeBr6 as photovoltaics: a DFT study of structural, mechanical, spin-resolved electronic and optical properties

papers.abstract: Accurate spatial quantitation of endogenous biomolecules is paramount to rationalize disease progression in tissues and translate findings into clinical use. In this contribution, we present a streamlined and quality-controlled spatial quantitation pipeline for accurate quantitative mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) of lipids. By creating miniaturized mimetic tissue models (MTM) spiked with stable isotope labelled standards (SILS) matching the tissue used for MSI, calibration and MSI experiments are performed from the same sample slide minimizing measurement variabilities. By determining the absolute SILS concentrations and lipid annotations via LC-MS/MS in the same MTMs as used for MSI, measurements are intrinsically quality controlled and quantitation results via MSI can be reported in units of µglipid/mgprotein commonly employed in lipidomics. We present an in-depth comparison of spatial quantitation via MSI and bulk LC-MS/MS for the same samples, i.e. mouse heart tissue, yielding good overall agreement between both quantification modalities for 95 endogenous lipids. Furthermore, we demonstrate the capability to capture heterogenous lipid expressions during disease progression quantitatively by charting lipidomic changes upon myocardial infarction-induced tissue remodeling. Our workflow reports absolute spatial quantitation results for 10 lipid classes and identifies 19 regulated lipids that are in line with known cellular remodeling events in fibrotic heart tissue.
papers.title: Mimetic tissue models for accurate lipid quantitation in fibrotic mouse heart by MALDI-MSI

papers.abstract: AqSol-Blend investigates molecular representation changes within a reproducible CPU-trained ensemble for aqueous solubility prediction. The study combines controlled development comparisons, an overlap-screened external evaluation and fresh-environment training reproduction. The method integrates LightGBM, Mordredbased CatBoost and robust-scaled support-vector regression with fixed weights of 0.675, 0.225 and 0.100. On the Therapeutics Data Commons AqSolDB benchmark, the ensemble achieves a mean absolute error of 0.736 ± 0.014 across five runs. Substituting Mordred descriptors for the CatBoost branch’s 2,937 fingerprint and RDKit features reduces development MAE by 0.0078 and improves nine of ten splits. In contrast, seed averaging, alternative CatBoost losses and reduced LightGBM capacity do not improve the development baseline. On an overlap-screened external cohort of 360 compounds from BigSolDB, the frozen five-run average obtains MAE 1.008, compared with 1.017 for its predecessor and 1.065 for a fixed random-forest baseline. The external improvement over the predecessor remains uncertain. Development reused validation partitions and included four sequential benchmark test evaluations; external results are interpreted separately because measurement conditions and concentration conventions differ.
papers.title: AqSol-Blend: A CPU-Trained Descriptor Ensemble for Aqueous Solubility Prediction

papers.abstract: Generative models now predict a reaction’s transition state (TS) in milliseconds, but they cannot say when a guess is wrong. On the RDB7 benchmark, 17.7% of the TS guesses from GoFlow, a flow-matching TS generator, have a stereocentre the wrong way round, and 85% of those still count as accurate by the usual distance-based score. 90% of these errors are whole mirror images, which have the same energy and vibrational frequencies as the correct TS, so they also pass a frequency check. We present TS Second Opinion, a model-agnostic layer that runs after generation. Chemists state checks in plain English; a large language model (Claude) writes each check as Python, and a gate keeps it only if it accepts at least 99% of 9,540 reference DFT transition states, never crashes, and still catches mirrored or distorted ones. The accepted checks then test every guess, repair whole mirror images by reflection, and assign each reaction a verdict (trust, check with DFT, or re-generate); conformal selection turns the ranking into a set of trusted reactions with a stated average error rate. On 1,194 held-out RDB7 reactions with eight GoFlow models, two LLM-written stereo checks catch 93% of wrong-handed guesses at 0.2% false alarms, wrong-handed final answers fall from 17.7% to 2.3%, and 80% of reactions can be trusted at a 5% average geometry-error rate. New ωB97X/def2-SVP transition-state optimisations on 16 reactions support both the symmetry argument and the verdicts: an unrepaired mirror image converges to a first-order saddle point 0.0006 kcal/mol from the repaired one, all six trusted guesses reach the reference TS, and none of the six re-generate guesses do, although five of them still pass a DFT frequency check. The results are mostly retrospective, on one dataset and one model family; code, data and a browser app are openly available.
papers.title: TS Second Opinion: catching, repairing and triaging mirror-image errors in machine-learned transition states

papers.abstract: The isothermal section of the ternary Gd–Os–Ge diagram at 800 °C was investigated with samples synthesized and characterized using scanning electron microscopy and X-ray diffraction. The collected data were used to construct a ternary phase diagram, providing insight into the phase formation trends and potential regions of phase stability. Four novel ternary compounds in this system, namely, Gd 2 OsGe 2 (Sc 2 CoSi 2 -type), GdOs 1- x Ge 2 (CeNiSi 2 -type), Gd 2 Os 3 Ge 5 (U 2 Co 3 Si 5 -type) and Gd 3.4 Os 4 Ge 12.6 (Yb 3 Rh 4 Sn 13 -type) were reported, showing a lack of Os-rich phases. The physical properties study of the Gd 3.4 Os 4 Ge 12.6 include magnetic and transport properties. The site-disordered Gd 3.4 Os 4 Ge 12.6 (Yb 3 Rh 4 Sn 13 -type) exhibits possible antiferromagnetic correlations and an unusual increasing electrical conductivity trend isuggesting possible semimetallic properties with a zT value of 0.05, one of the highest figures of merit found among ordered Yb 3 Rh 4 Sn 13 -type compounds. The cage-like structure of skutterudite-related Yb 3 Rh 4 Sn 13 -type compounds provides a promising investigation for its thermoelectric properties, as it has large internal disorder from atomic mixing, site splitting, and a cage of neighboring atoms to scatter heat-carrying acoustic phonons, both favorable for low thermal conductivity. The intermetallic phases of this exploration were investigated with density functional theory for their respective electronic structures featuring strong Os–Ge bonding, resulting in different Os-centered polyhedra throughout the Ge-rich phase phases.
papers.title: Systematic Exploration of the Gd–Os–Ge Ternary System with Magnetic and Transport Property Studies of Highly-Disordered Quasiskutterudite Gd3.4Os4Ge12.6

papers.abstract: Heterocyclic scaffolds are central structural elements in medicinal chemistry because incorporationofnitrogen,oxygen orsulfurintoaringcan altermolecularshape, electronicdistribution,ionisation,hydrogen-bondingcapacity,lipophilicityand metabolicbehaviour.Thesefeaturesallowmedicinalchemiststotunetarget recognitionanddrug-likepropertieswhileretainingacompactandsynthetically modifiable framework. Nitrogen-containing heterocycles are particularly prominent in approvedsmall-moleculemedicines;aninfluentialanalysisofUSFDA-approved pharmaceuticalsreportedthat59% ofuniquesmall-moleculedrugsinitsdataset contained at least one nitrogen heterocycle [1]. A later analysis of 321 unique smallmolecule drugs approved during 2013–2023 reported that 82% contained at least one nitrogen heterocycle[12].These valuesarisefrom differentapprovalperiodsand datasetsandshouldnotbeinterpretedasauniversalordirectlycomparable prevalenceestimate.Thepresentnarrativereviewdiscussesthecontributionof heterocyclic scaffolds to modern drug design, with emphasis on scaffold selection, structure–activityrelationships(SAR),representativetherapeuticapplications, physicochemicaloptimisationandcomputationalapproaches.Five-andsixmemberedmonocyclicrings,fusedsystemsandsaturatedheterocyclesare considered,includingimidazole,triazole,pyridine,pyrimidine,indole,quinoline, piperidineandmorpholinemotifs.Selectedmarketeddrugsillustratehow heterocycles can act as recognition elements, tune basicity and solubility, or serve as bioisostericreplacements.Thereview alsoexaminestheintegrationofmolecular docking,ligand-basedmodelling,virtualscreeningandmachine-learningmethods intoheterocycle-focuseddiscovery.Importantly,aheterocyclicringdoesnot independentlyguaranteepotency,selectivityorfavourablepharmacokinetics;its value depends on substitution pattern, three-dimensional context, target biology and whole-moleculeproperties.Currentchallengesincludepromiscuousbinding, metabolic liabilities, solubility limitations, synthetic accessibility, selectivity and overreliance on computational scores. A rational workflow combining medicinal-chemistry design,experimentaltestinganditerativeoptimisationisthereforeessentialfor translating heterocyclic hits into safe and effective drug candidates.
papers.title: ROLE OF HETEROCYCLIC SCAFFOLDS IN MODERN DRUG DESIGN: STRUCTURE–ACTIVITY RELATIONSHIPS, THERAPEUTIC APPLICATIONS AND EMERGING COMPUTATIONAL APPROACHES

papers.abstract: High-throughput chemistry enables parallel exploration of multiple reactions. But it often involves manual operations and the handling of data inputs and outputs across synthesis and analytical instruments that use different software and file formats. Automating high-throughput synthesis and purity analysis requires seamless information transfer throughout the process. Existing digital chemistry tools offer powerful capabilities for experiment design, automation, data management, and analysis; however, laboratories commonly rely on a combination of these tools rather than a single integrated platform. To streamline data transfer between the instruments used for synthesis (Tecan Liquid Handler), workup (Opentrons Liquid Handler), and purity analysis (Waters ACQUITY HPLC and QDa MS) at the Acceleration Consortium’s Medicinal Chemistry Self Driving Lab, we developed a workspace, XinPilot. XinPilot addresses this project-level interoperability problem through a chemist-designed Windows desktop workspace that brings together chemical stock information, synthesis records, reaction schemes, expected products, and analytical evidence within a portable project. Working alongside existing instrument-control systems, XinPilot generates worklists for the Tecan Fluent and Opentrons Flex and OT2 liquid handlers, records manual reagent additions, and imports transfer records from other liquid-handling workflows in Excel, CSV, and JSON-compatible formats. These results can be combined into a unified reaction map when they use the same plate format. Chemical IDs and reaction-to-analysis well mappings preserve the relationships among reaction compositions, expected products, and analytical samples. Integrated PyParse-based analysis allows chemists to inspect UV chromatograms, mass spectra, and integrated peaks. Chemists can also reassign product peaks for individual experiments while retaining the automated assignments for other experiments, without requiring coding knowledge. Experimental records, original imported files, and supported analytical inspection data can be retained in portable .xinpilot.zip projects for subsequent review, handover, and synthesis planning. An experimentally executed Suzuki–Miyaura campaign combining Tecan dispensing, manual additions, Opentrons aqueous workup and LC-MS review is presented as a tutorial-style demonstration of the workflow. Additional experimental examples independently performed by other chemists are provided in the Supporting Information. A separate demonstration uses published experimental data from 192 Chemspeed reactions. These data were converted into XinPilot-compatible transfer records and imported into two projects. Reaction structures were also generated using XinPilot's Cheminformatics tools, and both projects were exported as portable .xinpilot.zip files. Overall, XinPilot provides an integrated open‑source workspace for generating worklists for parallel synthesis and workup using Tecan and Opentron liquid handlers, facilitating the purity analysis and maintaining traceable links between experimental conditions, reaction products, and analytical results.
papers.title: XinPilot: a chemist-designed open‑source desktop workspace for traceable high-throughput synthesis and purity analysis

papers.abstract: For a molecule with several titratable sites, a measured pKa reports a change in the number of bound protons, but not the population of each tautomer. The biological chromophore biliverdin (BV) is a longstanding example: the protonation of its four pyrrole nitrogens controls its photoactivity, yet the reported pKa values vary by about two units, and ring C is typically assumed deprotonated in neutral BV without a site-resolving measurement. BV is also flexible, so its protonation microstates and its conformers form coupled ensembles: the shape of the molecule changes how tightly it binds the proton. Here, we compute the macroscopic pKa of BV in explicit water and the populations of its four neutral tautomers, from the site-resolved pKa of the four rings. Enhanced quantum-mechanical simulations follow a proton into bulk water, and the free energies of proton transfer between rings and of ring rotation connect all protonation states in one thermodynamically consistent network. In the locked-helix conformation that dominates in water, BV has a macroscopic pKa of 4.0, and its four nitrogens are almost equally basic (site pKa values of 4.5 for rings B and C and 4.9 for rings A and D). No single tautomer dominates: the tautomers deprotonated at rings B and C each make up 36% of neutral BV, and those deprotonated at rings A and D 14% each. Opening the helix at ring D, as in bacteriophytochromes, raises the macroscopic pKa to 6.4 and shifts the neutral form almost entirely to the ring B (71%) and ring C (27%) tautomers. The conformation of BV thus controls its proton binding more than the choice of ring.
papers.title: Enhanced Quantum Simulations Reveal Conformation-Controlled, Site-Resolved Proton Binding in Biliverdin

papers.abstract: As Copper (Cu) interconnect dimensions continue to shrink, conventional tantalum/tantalum nitride (Ta/TaN) liner/barrier layers occupy an increasing fraction of the available interconnect volume and introduce additional electrical resistance because of their relatively high resistivity. Therefore, a key challenge is to develop ultrathin liner/barrier materials that can maintain low resistivity while providing effective Cu diffusion-barrier performance. In this work, we demonstrate MoC x as a liner-free barrier material using plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD). For this PEALD-grown film, cycloheptatriene molybdenum tricarbonyl, (η 6 -C 7 H 8 )Mo(CO) 3 , was first introduced as a precursor to synthesize ultrathin molybdenum carbide (MoC x ) films. The effects of plasma reactants, plasma power, deposition temperature, film thickness, and substrate types were systematically evaluated to clarify how PEALD process conditions and substrate chemistry influence the electrical performance of ultrathin MoC x films. We observed nucleation differences during the growth based on the substrate; MoC x films deposited on Al 2 O 3 consistently exhibited lower resistivity than those grown on SiO 2 . Using the optimized deposition process, amorphous MoC x films thinner than 5 nm showed resistivities as low as ~230 μΩ·cm without any post-deposition annealing. For reference, current Ta/TaN liner/barrier layers typically exceed 500 μΩ·cm resistivity in the sub-5 nm thickness regime. Sub-5 nm MoC x film also showed good Cu adhesion and effective Cu diffusion-barrier behavior after thermal annealing of up to 500 °C. These results demonstrate the potential of ultrathin amorphous MoC x as a low-resistivity liner-free barrier material for advanced Cu interconnects.
papers.title: Plasma-Enhanced Atomic Layer Deposition and Substrate Engineering of Low-Resistivity Ultrathin MoCx Films for Advanced Interconnect Applications

papers.abstract: Air pollution adversely impacts health globally, disproportionately affecting urban populations. Regulatory monitoring is often too spatially coarse to capture true intra-urban variability, needed to prioritize and guide localized interventions and policies. High-density lower-cost sensor (LCS) networks, mobile monitoring, satellite-derived products, and advanced interpolation techniques are emerging to support higher spatial resolution characterization. However, results from related studies are varied, disconnected across different fields, and as yet with no defined standards or guidance. This review examines the literature from 2005-2025 to systematically compare data collection and modeling pipelines for accuracy and application to the intra-urban challenge. 166 studies from regional to neighborhood scale were analyzed quantitatively on monitoring network characteristics (geographic location, spatial density, target pollutants, study duration) and interpolation modeling approaches (algorithms, predictive covariates, performance metrics). Studies from Europe, Asia, and North America dominated the literature, with particulate matter being the most studied pollutant. While 95% of studies had measurement density below 20,000 km2/device (metro scale), none had sufficient resolution for capturing intra-urban heterogeneity. Modeling approaches shifted over time from primarily geostatistical methods toward increasingly sophisticated machine learning and deep learning techniques incorporating diverse covariates, including meteorology, land use, traffic patterns, and satellite data products. More than measurement density or model complexity, strategic use of both static and dynamic covariates in data driven models was most consistently associated with performance improvement for interpolation of both PM2.5 and NOx. However, major gaps remain including (1) imbalance in data availability geographically, temporally, and across pollutant species, leading to major challenges in assessing and achieving transferability of models globally, (2) limited data availability at appropriate intra-urban scale for most metro areas, (3) lack of evaluation and reporting standards necessary to truly compare performance of different data-model pipelines, and (4) general lack of generating or reporting uncertainty quantification on model outputs, critically needed for interpretability and sensitivity analyses. These gaps point to an urgent need for not only interdisciplinary collaboration and innovation but also discipline-wide guidance that will enable objective assessment of model performance and state-of-the-art, including shared benchmark datasets, standardized evaluation metrics, mandatory unit reporting, and guidelines for complete model specifications.
papers.title: Air pollution sensing to urban air quality insight: review of spatially interpolated data products from sensor networks

papers.abstract: Water extracts chlorogenic acids, which contribute to the sourness and bitterness of coffee, together with caffeine. We examined whether a less polar solvent changes that balance. Coarse-ground coffee was brewed for 20 minutes at 75 degrees Celsius in deionized water or 95 percent denatured ethanol and the extracts followed by UV-Vis and infrared spectroscopy; spent grounds from earlier brews were examined by electron and optical microscopy. The caffeine-region band near 275 nm grew about three times faster in water, while the chlorogenic acid region near 320 nm was suppressed proportionally more in ethanol, raising the ratio of the two bands from about 1.2 to 1.5 to 1.7 within a large reading uncertainty, and only the ethanol extracts showed a scattering baseline. Infrared spectra of the undiluted extracts were dominated by the solvents, identified isopropanol as the ethanol’s denaturant and showed no coffee band above the detection limit, and ethanol-brewed grounds more often showed exposed cell walls. These pilot data point to slower, partially selective extraction in ethanol, a direction relevant to lower-acid coffee concentrates, although acidity and caffeine were not measured directly. We also report the measurement problems the data revealed.
papers.title: Brewing Coffee in Ethanol Instead of Water: A Multi-Technique Pilot Study

papers.abstract: Complete-basis-set (CBS) extrapolation is widely used to estimate electronic energies beyond finite-basis calculations. However, students may encounter it primarily as a formula or automated correction, which obscures how a CBS value is constructed from a sequence of finite-basis energies. We describe a scaffolded Excel activity that makes this process visible by linking energy tables, component extrapolations, and convergence plots. Students first examine Hartree-Fock and correlation-energy convergence in the hydrogen chloride heteronuclear diatomic molecule, compare CBS estimates obtained from alternative extrapolation choices, and then apply the same workflow to the hydrogen fluoride molecule HF. The activity culminates in the calculation and justification of CBS-derived atomization energies and comparison to experiment. This activity is implemented in an upper-division computational chemistry course, and was evaluated through a pre-activity quiz and rubric-based analysis of completed student work. In general, students executed the component extrapolations successfully, yet evaluating sensitivity and justifying a final reported value proved more challenging. The activity offers a transparent and adaptable approach for teaching students to evaluate, rather than merely obtain, computational chemistry results.
papers.title: Making Complete-Basis-Set Extrapolation Visible: A Spreadsheet-Based Activity for Upper-Division Computational Chemistry

papers.abstract: Soft nanoscale confinement fundamentally alters the thermodynamic and kinetic landscape of chemical reactions, yet a predictive understanding of how nanoreactor geometry dictates reactivity remains elusive. In this work, we demonstrate that the dimensionality of soft confinement governs the onset of nanomaterial formation. By systematically tuning the water-to-surfactant molar ratio () in self-assembled lecithin reverse micelles, we decoupled the geometry of the host template from its chemical composition. We utilized the in situ nucleation of gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) as an active optical and structural probe across isotropic, anisotropic, and bulk-like spatial domains. Correlating UV-Vis spectroscopy with small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) analyses, we reveal that confinement dimensionality acts as an ON/OFF switch for the reduction of gold ions. Under extreme isotropic confinement (), where the interfacial water network is severely restricted, AuNP formation is suppressed for at least 30 days. Conversely, a hydration-induced structural transition toward anisotropic, wormlike domains () coincides with the onset of AuNP nucleation and yields the highest reaction extent. Finally, further expansion into bulk-like regimes () dilutes the gold precursor within the aqueous domains, attenuating the reaction yield. We rationalize these trends within a phenomenological framework based on classical nucleation theory, highlighting confinement dimensionality as a design parameter for soft nanoreactors and tailored plasmonic nanomaterials.
papers.title: Probing the dimensionality of confinement in soft nanoreactors through plasmonic nanoparticles nucleation

papers.abstract: Laboratory mixtures of known composition serve as ground truth for explainable AI (XAI) in vibrational spectroscopy, on the assumption that the class difference is the spectrum of the added molecule. We tested this assumption on a public Raman dataset (785 nm) of 16 dried droplets in a 2 × 2 design: a phosphatidylcholine–phenylalanine–lactate base with or without collagen–mucin and with or without DNA. Besides the 16,107 spectra, we used three records stored with the data but not analysed before: white-light images, LiveTrack focus heights and acquisition timestamps. All inference was at the droplet level. DNA raised the base bands more than any DNA band, and the two added components were not additive (p = 0.032). DNA doubled the Raman yield of the deposit (×1.97, p = 2 × 10-4). Deposit optical density in the white-light images predicted yield across droplets (r = 0.93) and within most droplets, and with optical density in the model the DNA effect fell to ×1.05 (95% CI 0.77–1.44). Focus heights agreed with a thicker film: yield rose with local height in DNA-free deposits but much less with DNA (p = 3 × 10-4). Band ratios to phenylalanine still changed with DNA after adjustment for optical density. Five maps had been acquired 8–15 days after the rest; they showed a 3.2-fold higher background, and acquisition date was predictable from held-out droplets. The DNA class therefore combines deposit optics, a modest compositional change and a date-dependent background. Attributions should be judged against this decomposed effect rather than against reference bands of DNA.
papers.title: Deposit optics, film thickness and acquisition date confound Raman spectra of dried droplets

papers.abstract: Designing crystalline materials with ultralow thermal conductivity remains an important challenge for optimizing thermoelectric energy conversion and thermal barrier coatings. Crystalline solids exhibiting glass-like thermal transport are of special interest because they approach the minimum thermal conductivity achievable in an ordered structure. Here, we investigate the ultralow thermal conductivity of crystalline AgGaGeS8-8xSe8x and Ag2-xGa2-xGe2+xS8-8xSe8x (x = 0.00, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00). In these systems, selenium incorporation strongly suppresses crystalline thermal transport, leading to glass-like properties while preserving structural crystallinity. Across all compositions, the ultralow thermal conductivity is associated with a disordered silver substructure characterized by weak Ag–Ch interactions and pronounced anharmonicity, where selenium substitution promotes softening of the silver dynamics. Heat-capacity measurements reveal boson peaks in the endmember compounds, which for AgGaGe3Se8 is significantly more intense and shifted to lower temperature. Together, these results suggest that selenium promotes low-frequency silver vibrations that drive the emergence of glass-like thermal transport. Furthermore, selenium exhibits a pronounced preference for the chalcogen site most strongly interacting with silver, demonstrating that local anion chemistry, rather than average composition, governs the thermal transport response. This selective occupancy provides a structural basis for the emergence of glass-like thermal conductivity at remarkably low selenium contents.
papers.title: Emergence of Glass-like Thermal Transport through Anion-Engineering in Complex Silver Gallium Germanium Chalcogenides

papers.abstract: Ethylene carbonate (EC)-free electrolytes are promising for high-voltage lithium-ion batteries. However, their benefits have been demonstrated primarily for layered oxide cathodes, while their effects on olivine phosphates remain unclear. Here, we show that EC removal accelerates the degradation of LiMn 0.6 Fe 0.4 PO 4 (LMFP64), in contrast to LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811). Experiments and first-principles calculations suggest that these opposite responses reflect distinct degradation pathways associated with transition-metal–oxygen (TM–O) covalency. On NCM811, strongly hybridized O 2 p states near the Fermi level favor EC dehydrogenation, initiating degradation; EC removal eliminates this pathway. In contrast, olivine models exhibit weaker TM 3d–O 2 p hybridization, more ionic TM–O bonding, and stronger PF 6 − adsorption at TM sites. Without EC, experiments on LMFP64 reveal salt decomposition before cycling and accelerated degradation; EC otherwise limits anion access to TM sites. These findings show that the effect of EC removal is cathode-dependent and can be rationalized by TM–O covalency.
papers.title: Opposite Effects of Removing Ethylene Carbonate from the Electrolyte on Ni-Rich Layered Oxide and Mn-Rich Olivine Phosphate Cathodes

papers.abstract: Gemini (dimeric) surfactants, molecules bearing two hydrophobic tails and two head groups joined by a spacer, have been developed across cationic, anionic, nonionic, zwitterionic, sugar-based, and amino acid-based chemistries over several decades. To the author's knowledge, this review is the first to combine a systematic patent landscape analysis spanning all major charge classes with a survey of current academic research trends to ask a direct question: Does patent activity track academic attention in this field? Drawing on 41 patent families listed in this review (Supporting Information S1) and over 20 peer-reviewed sources, the answer is no. Cationic quaternary ammonium gemini surfactants, driven mainly by enhanced oil recovery, corrosion inhibition, antimicrobial, and personal care applications, account for 25 of the 41 patent families identified here. In contrast, recent academic reviews describe amino acid- and sugar-based gemini surfactants, rather than cationic quaternary ammonium chemistry, as the field's emerging green surfactant direction; searches specifically for arginine- or lysine-specific gemini surfactant patents returned no on-point results. This review further documents a recurring definitional ambiguity between "two hydrophobic tails" and "two charge centres" in patent claim language, a near absence of true single-molecule zwitterionic gemini surfactants, and no agricultural or pesticide adjuvant application identified for any gemini surfactant charge type in either the patent or the academic searches. These findings identify several concrete, evidence-based directions for future synthetic, formulation, and intellectual property work.
papers.title: Patent Landscape of Gemini (Dimeric) Surfactants: Cationic Dominance in Intellectual Property versus the Emerging Green Surfactant Narrative

papers.abstract: Although alkenyl radicals are conceptually desirable for anti‑Markovnikov hydroalkenylation, their direct addition to unactivated alkenes is kinetically inaccessible owing to their intrinsically low electrophilicity and competing strong hydrogen atom abstraction reactivity. Herein, we establish a novel strategy to realize the first radical‑mediated formal anti‑Markovnikov hydroalkenylation of unactivated alkenes. This approach utilizes the combination of highly electrophilic triphenylphosphonium methyl (TPPM) radicals with weak H atom abstraction reactivity and carbonyl compounds as practical alkenyl‑radical surrogates. The transformation begins with the photocatalytic reduction of bromomethyl triphenylphosphonium bromide to generate TPPM radicals, which add to unactivated alkenes to form carbon-centered radicals that abstract a hydrogen atom from thiophenol. The resulting phosphonium salts subsequently undergo an in‑situ Wittig reaction with carbonyl compounds to furnish the devised hydroalkenylation products. This protocol exhibits good functional group tolerance, broad substrate scope covering both activated and unactivated olefins, and allows late‑stage functionalization of natural product derivatives.
papers.title: Radical‑Mediated Formal Anti‑Markovnikov Hydroalkenylation of Unactivated Alkenes Enabled by a Functional Alkenyl‑Radical Surrogate Strategy

papers.abstract: Rare sugars, monosaccharides that occur only rarely in nature, exhibit physicochemical and biological properties distinct from those of naturally abundant sugars such as D-glucose. Their widespread utilization has been hindered by limitations in existing production methods, which rely primarily on equilibrium-constrained biocatalytic cascades or on synthetic approaches requiring multiple steps or organic reagents. Here we show the one-pot heterogeneous catalytic epimerization of methyl glucosides into rare sugar derivatives over supported Ru catalysts under hydrogen atmosphere in water. Among the supported metals examined, Ru uniquely promotes regioselective stereoinversion of 1- O -methyl β-D-glucopyranoside at the C3 position to produce 1- O -methyl β-D-allopyranoside without requiring additional reagents or multistep reactions. Isotopelabeling experiments reveal that dehydrogenation and hydrogenation proceed substantially faster than net epimerization, identifying surface-confined molecular rotation of a keto intermediate as the rate-determining step. Computer simulations further show that the experimentally observed regioselectivity originates from the low rotational free energy barriers and relatively high stability of the keto intermediate on the Ru surface. These findings identify molecular rotational dynamics on catalyst surfaces as a governing principle for stereochemical inversion reactions.
papers.title: Regioselective sugar epimerization to rare sugar on ruthenium surface

papers.abstract: The rational design of catalysts capable of efficiently utilizing CO2 is critical for sustainable chemical processes. The Super-dry reforming of methane (Super-DRM), which couples dry reforming of methane (DRM) with the reverse water gas shift (RWGS) reactions, offers a promising route to maximize CO2 conversion. Modulating the crystal phase of nanocatalysts offers a powerful strategy to enhance catalytic performance, yet the relationship between bulk phase and catalytic behavior remains poorly understood. A significant obstacle in resolving this issue is obtaining atomic-level insights on the surface structure of phase-controlled catalyst under reaction conditions. In this study, we employ in-situ gas cell transmission electron microscopy to investigate the surface structure of faceted PtNi nanoparticles during Super-DRM at moderate temperatures (550 ℃). Atomic-resolution in-situ observations reveal that the reaction environment induces a pronounced nickel segregation and subsequent coke formation on the surface of disordered A1-PtNi nanoparticles. In contrast, the ordered L10 phase exhibits remarkable resistance to such segregation on its {111} facets. This structural rigidity effectively suppresses coke formation and lowers the kinetic barrier for CH4 activation by 27 kJ/mol compared to the disordered phase. Complemented by in-situ spectroscopy and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, our findings demonstrate that the bulk crystal ordering acts as an anchor for surface structures, governing the catalytic behaviors. This study unveils a direct atomic-level link between crystal ordering, surface reconstruction, and catalytic performance, offering valuable design principles for robust intermetallic catalysts in CO2 utilization.
papers.title: Revealing Phase-Controlled Surface Structure in PtNi Nanocatalysts via In-situ Gas Cell Transmission Electron Microscopy
Electrochemically driven thermomechanical energy harvesting

papers.abstract: Single-crystal filters that pass thermal neutrons and remove epithermal and fast neutrons and γ rays have been chosen from a handful of materials. For 18 449 inorganic crystals of the Materials Project, the thickness L₀.₈ at which a large single crystal oriented away from Bragg reflections transmits 80% of a 300 K Maxwellian beam over 0.5–3 Å was computed, together with its rejection −ln T of a 1/E neutron spectrum (1 eV–100 keV), of a fission spectrum and of 1 and 6 MeV photons at that thickness; 3 437 crystals have density-functional and 1 279 machine-learned phonons. A composition-only proxy reproduces the bulk order of L₀.₈ (Spearman ρ = 0.83 at 293 K, 0.95 at 77 K) but not the top of the ranking, which a single elastic Debye temperature largely recovers. Against measured total cross-sections the acceptance criterion fixed in advance was not met (6 of 13 crystals fail); restricted to single-crystal data, 4 of 11 fail, or 6 of 11 without an allowance for the spread between datasets; and the model lies above all four sapphire datasets. With a model uncertainty of 0.138 in ln L₀.₈ propagated by 20 000 Monte Carlo draws, the Pareto front of commercially grown crystals (epithermal against 1 MeV photon rejection) consists of known filters alone with probability 0.10 at 293 K and 0.04 at 77 K, and cooling reorders it. No grown crystal that is not a known filter beats sapphire with probability above 0.90, the level fixed for a statement. 6H-SiC and chrysoberyl are candidates on the epithermal axis: the probability that 6H-SiC rejects the 1/E spectrum better than sapphire is 0.85 at 293 K and 0.88 at 77 K (chrysoberyl: 0.66 and 0.85); with an error component shared by all compounds it rises to 0.93 and 0.95, and with sapphire corrected by its measured residual it falls to 0.69 and 0.73. On the fission spectrum neither candidate is distinguishable from sapphire. Counting every transmitted particle instead of the uncollided ones changes the epithermal rejection by −0.23 to −6.28 and reorders the front, so uncollided figures of merit rank filters optimistically for uncollimated beams. The pipeline that produces the atlas is openly available; the atlas and its uncertainties will be archived openly on acceptance.
papers.title: A database-wide atlas of single-crystal filters for thermal neutron beams

papers.abstract: Conformationally rigid heterobicyclic motifs with well-defined exit vectors have emerged as valuable isosteric replacements for pyridine. While these rigid 3D structures successfully mimic 3,5-disubstituted pyridine derivatives, no isosteric analogues of 2,3-disubstituted pyridines have been reported, despite their widespread occurrence in bioactive compounds. Herein, we report the first diastereoselective synthesis of hetero-[2]-ladderanes, representing a new class of potential 2,3-disubstituted pyridine isosteres, via carbonyl photoexcitation. This protocol is amenable to a variety of 2-azetines and isatins, with remarkable functional-group tolerance, enabling rapid construction of complex spiro-oxa-aza-[2]-ladderanes as single diastereomers. Notably, benzaldehyde derivatives could also participate, affording oxa-aza-[2]-ladderanes with high stereoselectivity. Exit-vector analysis of an oxa-aza-[2]ladderane and a 2,3-disubstituted pyridine-based drug demonstrated the potential of this scaffold as a possible isosteric mimic of 2,3-disubstituted pyridine. Experimental-based mechanistic studies combined with density functional theory have rationalized the observed reactivity and selectivity. Finally, we explored an unprecedented strainenabled, aromaticity-driven Grob-type fragmentation of a hetero-[2]-ladderane, yielding synthetically valuable αhydroxy-β-amino ketone and aminotriol derivatives.
papers.title: Diastereoselective Synthesis of Hetero-[2]-Ladderanes

papers.abstract: Selective synthesis of α-aryl-β-amino aldehydes remains less developed despite considerable progress in Mannich reactions, aza-Michael additions and asymmetric hydroformylation. Here we report a phenyliodine(III) bis(trifluoroacetate) (PIFA)-mediated oxidative rearrangement of cinnamyl amines through formal 1,2-aryl migration. The reaction proceeds at 0 °C under ambient air and accommodates diverse nitrogen substituents, migrating aryl groups and pharmaceutical-derived substrates. A 6-gram preparation and subsequent transformations to β-amino acids, 1,3-amino alcohols, 1,3-diamines and azetidines, together with the synthesis of a valifenalate isomer, demonstrate the synthetic utility of the aldehyde products. Mechanistic experiments suggest a pathway involving a bis(trifluoroacetate) intermediate. An initial asymmetric variant using chiral iodine(III) reagents furnished a celecoxib-derived chiral aldehyde, with up to 77% ee measured for its reduced chiral alcohol derivative.
papers.title: Direct Access to α-Aryl-β-Amino Aldehydes via Hypervalent Iodine-Mediated Oxidative Rearrangement of Cinnamyl Amines

papers.abstract: Wireframe DNA nanostructures are built from edges of prescribed length meeting at vertices of prescribed valency, which makes their design space a geometric one: which equal-edge frameworks can be built at all, given a maximum vertex degree, a minimum edge angle and a steric clearance. We apply a constrained growth construction—each new vertex placed by trilateration at a fixed strut length from at least three placed vertices, accepted only if the resulting framework still satisfies the design constraints—and report three results. First, under a degree cap of six the construction is extremely selective: of all periodic face-choice patterns tested, only the Boerdijk–Coxeter tetrahelix grows without stalling, and it does so because its interior vertices have degree exactly six, saturating the budget. Second, raising the cap to seven unlocks a one-parameter family of kinked variants indexed by the defect spacing k, whose radius is programmable from 0.52 to 1.13 strut lengths and whose handedness alternates with k, while straightness stays above 0.99. Values k ∈ {3, 5, 8} stall for an identifiable reason—the capped vertex lands at unit distance from a fourth earlier vertex—and run freely at a cap of eight. Both caps are within demonstrated multi-arm junction capability. Third, two members of the family, the pure tetrahelix and a k = 6 variant, were routed into DNA, energy-minimised and run for 5×105 oxDNA steps at 30◦C: both are stable, with second-half mean energies −1.4919±0.0017 and −1.5004 ± 0.0019 per nucleotide and shape changes under 4%. The kinked variant routes into 8 strand cycles against the tetrahelix’s 22. We also report what did not survive checking: a twist–stretch coupling that vanished under length convergence, and a circular-dichroism sign rule that its own descriptor failed to predict.
papers.title: Constraint-guided equal-strut growth generates a tunable family of DNA-realizable wireframe filaments
Polarization Is Required to Model Electrostatic Preorganization: The Case of Chorismate Mutase

papers.abstract: Dinitrosyl iron complexes (DNICs) are widespread biological nitric oxide (NO) storage and delivery motifs, yet their highly delocalized electronic structure generally resists NO-centered reductive chemistry. Here, we establish ligandcentered reduction as a strategy for unlocking nitroxyl (HNO)-generating DNIC reactivity. A redox-active formazanate ligand (L) stabilizes a super-reduced formal {LFe(NO) 2 } 11 state beyond the conventional {Fe(NO) 2 } 9/10 redox pair. EPR and Mössbauer spectroscopy, together with density functional theory calculations, identify predominantly ligand-centered reduction, yielding an {Fe(NO) 2 } 10 unit coupled to a formazanate radical dianion, L 2−• . Electronic communication between the reduced ligand and the [Fe(NO) 2 ] unit enhances Fe-to-NO π backbonding, consistent with experimental ν(NO) redshifts. Importantly, protonation triggers HNO release, representing an unprecedented example of HNO generation from the super reduced DNIC scaffold. Isotopically distinct H 14 NO/H 15 NO is trapped with PPh 3 , along with the 14/15 N 2 O characterization. Calculations support direct nitrosyl protonation to form an Fe-bound HNO intermediate, followed by solvent-assisted HNO release and subsequent N 2 O formation. These findings establish that ligand-centered electron accommodation coupled to nitrosyl protonation enables HNO generation from a formally super-reduced DNIC, extending DNIC reactivity beyond conventional NO donation.
papers.title: Redox-active ligand facilitates HNO generation in a super-reduced dinitrosyl iron complex

papers.abstract: The hydricity of M–H intermediates is a key descriptor and optimization target for the rational design of molecular hydrogen evolution electrocatalysts. Adsorption to an electrode surface is known to augment catalytic rate, but it remains unclear how adsorption affects M-H hydricity. Herein, we quantitatively compare the catalytic activity and mechanism of the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) from cobalt tetrasulfophthalocyanine (CoTSPc) in a dissolved aqueous form (CoTSPc (aq) ) and when adsorbed to the surface of a carbon electrode (CoTSPc/C). At the same electrode potential, CoTSPc/C catalyzes HER at a rate that is over five orders of magnitude faster than CoTSPc (aq) . Mechanistic studies indicate that both CoTSPc/C and CoTSPc (aq) catalyze HER via a rate-limiting hydride transfer to a proton donor in solution to form H 2 . Hydride transfer from Co-H in CoTSPc (aq) is a purely chemical step defined by a constant hydricity of 22.4 kcal mol −1 that is independent of applied potential. In contrast, hydride transfer from Co-H in CoTSPc/C is strongly polarization dependent, decreasing hydricity by ~23 kcal mol −1 V −1 to values as low as 1.2 kcal mol −1 at −1.1 V vs SHE, leading to the observed rate promotion. We attribute this mechanistic change to the positioning of the CoTSPc-H intermediate within the electrochemical double layer, such that the hydride traverses the interfacial electrostatic potential difference during the RLS. These results demonstrate the power of surface adsorption to generate highly reactive molecular hydrides and fundamentally reshape the free energy landscape of electrocatalysis.
papers.title: Polarization-Driven Hydride Transfer Promotes Cobalt Tetrasulfophthalocyanine-Catalyzed Hydrogen Evolution by Five Orders of Magnitude

papers.abstract: Molecular qubits, owing to their designability and tunability, have emerged as fundamental units for quantum technologies. Among them, molecular qubit frameworks (MQFs) offer unique advantages in long-range ordered lattices and microporosity that provide well-defined phonon environments and guest-tunable spin dynamics. These features greatly enhance qubit performance and enable room temperature quantum operations, holding promise for quantum sensing applications. Herein, we compare the qubit performance of 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexahydroxytriphenylene (HHTP) and tetrathiafulvalene tetrabenzoic acid (H4TTFTB), which form stable radicals upon spontaneous oxidation in the air. We found that optical phonons dominate spin relaxation in HHTP, whereas H4TTFTB exhibits stronger spin-orbit coupling and higher acoustic phonon population that account for its shorter spin relaxation time. Meanwhile, H4TTFTB features a nuclear-spin-free core and in turn a prolonged phase memory time, making it a favorable qubit candidate. Furthermore, we synthesized three MQFs using H4TTFTB as the ligand, which not only retain the superior room-temperature qubit performance but also possess porous channels, establishing a viable platform for future quantum information applications.
papers.title: Tetrathiafulvalene-Based Molecular Qubit Frameworks with Room-Temperature Quantum Coherence

papers.abstract: An experimental kinetic study of the decarboxylation of pentafluorobenzoic acid is reported. This work demonstrates a thermal decarboxylation pathway that is operative under conditions commonly employed for catalytic decarboxylative coupling reactions. This work also reveals a dramatic rate enhancement for the benzoate salt relative to the neutral acid and the importance of basic additives in accelerating the decarboxylation of the pentafluorobenzoic acid. Additionally, decarboxylation of the acid displays a strong solvent dependence with the polar aprotic solvent DMA leading to more rapid thermal decarboxylation as well as an increased influence of Ni additives.
papers.title: The Importance of Base and Solvent in the Ni-Mediated Decarboxylation of Pentafluorobenzoic Acid

papers.abstract: Ferulic acid (FA) is a phenolic antioxidant whose potential applications are limited by poor aqueous solubility and bioavailability. Novel ferulate salts of ethyl, propyl, and isopropyl esters of L-tyrosine and L-phenylalanine were synthesized and characterized in terms of their physicochemical properties, antioxidant activity, and acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibition. All synthesized ferulates exhibited improved aqueous solubility compared with FA, with tyrosine ethyl ester ferulate, [TyrOEt][FA], showing the highest solubility. The salts retained or enhanced antioxidant activity, with tyrosine-derived compounds exhibiting nearly twofold higher activity than FA in the ORAC assay. The ferulate salts also demonstrated stronger AChE inhibition than FA, with phenylalanine isopropyl ester ferulate, [PheOiPr][FA], showing the greatest inhibitory potency among the ferulates. Comparison with the corresponding chloride salts indicated that the amino acid ester cations were primarily responsible for AChE inhibition. Kinetic analysis revealed a mixed inhibition mechanism with a predominant competitive component for the most active compounds. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations identified interactions with key aromatic residues within the AChE binding gorge, while MM/GBSA calculations supported favorable binding of the amino acid esters. The synthesized compounds generally had limited effects on L929 fibroblast viability, although tyrosine propyl ester salts showed greater cytotoxicity. These findings demonstrate that salt formation with amino acid esters improves the physicochemical properties of FA while preserving its antioxidant potential, whereas AChE inhibitory activity is primarily determined by the structure of the amino acid ester moiety and its interactions with key residues within the enzyme's active-site gorge.
papers.title: Acetylcholinesterase Activity Modulation by Proteinogenic Amino Acid Ester Ferulates salts with Enhanced Solubility and Antioxidant Properties

papers.abstract: Synthesizing ultrasmall thermoresponsive nanoparticles within poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPA) hydrogels without the use of strong ligands remains challenging, as intrinsically weak interfacial interactions and structural heterogeneity in conventional networks often lead to poor size control and aggregation. Here, we report a programmable PNIPA-based hydrogel constructed from star-shaped polymers via living radical polymerization, in which a homogeneous network containing locally reinforced crosslinking domains enables ligand-free in situ formation of ultrasmall metal nanoparticles. The uniform network provides a spatially consistent reaction environment, allowing synchronized and controllable particle growth across length scales. Nanoparticle size is governed by network architecture rather than by synthetic conditions, and the resulting hydrogel composites exhibit exceptional stability under thermal cycling and harsh chemical environments, despite relying solely on amide functionalities. Stabilization does not arise from rigid immobilization or strong ligand coordination along the polymer chains; instead, it emerges from the collective engagement of multiple spatially distributed, amide-enriched crosslinking domains. These reinforced domains generate a cooperative multiple-anchoring effect, creating a soft yet adaptive chelation-like confinement. This work establishes a versatile platform for strong-ligand-free yet robust and controllable nanoparticle synthesis, extendable to colloidal dispersions, diverse polymer matrices, and various metal nanoparticles.
papers.title: Uniform Gel Networks with Amide-Rich Crosslinking Domains Amplify Weak Interactions for Growth of Ultrasmall Nanoparticles without Added Strong Ligand
